techniques.why: additive harmonic stack -- the general-purpose way to build any harmonic instrument colour: a seven-harmonic gbuzz stack doubled by a twin three cents above, so the pair beats slowly; the colour is gbuzz's own two numbers, how many partials (7) and how fast they fall away (0.68, 0.64)
techniques.code:
kad0    poscil 0.0004, 0.053         ; slow drift, upper stack
aa10    gbuzz 0.52, (kfreq * koct1), 7, 1, 0.68, giCos          ; harmonic stack
aa20    gbuzz 0.34, (kfreq * koct1) * (1.0018 + kad0), 7, 1, 0.64, giCos ; twin, +3 cents
asig    = (aa10 + aa20) * kvol1

techniques.why: A two-operator FM bell: a glassy, inharmonic strike whose colour rings down while the note holds. Method: J. Chowning, 'The Synthesis of Complex Audio Spectra by Means of Frequency Modulation', JAES 21(7), 1973 -- a 1:1.41 carrier:modulator ratio puts the sidebands off the harmonic grid, and a large index falling over the note makes the strike dense and the ring simple. Chowning's amplitude envelope is left out: the mean level STANDS and only the COLOUR rings down, to a held floor; a doublet beats the level at a fixed rate in Hz. A new strike restarts carriers and colour: a hit into a sounding note cuts it. The partial at 0.41 f, an octave and a third below the key, is as strong as the key, so the bell sits partly under the note. NOT a cast church bell (no hum/tierce partials: cast_bell), NOT a tubular bell or chime (tube modes: tubular_bell), NOT six-operator DX FM -- that is fm3.

index.note: Peak FM index at the strike, 1 at 0 to 16 at 1. At 220 Hz the strike centroid runs 214 -> 903 -> 2882 Hz (0 / .27 / 1). Sideband room caps it high up: above .89 at 880 Hz, above .35 at 1760 Hz it does nothing.

mellow.gloss: soft strike (centroid 2.4 f) settling near the key's own sine: a round bell

warm.gloss: strike centroid 4.1 f settling to 1.3 f: the plain FM bell, clang then hum

bright.gloss: strike centroid 8.3 f, settled 2.1 f: a glassy clang that stays bright

harsh.gloss: strike centroid 11 f, settled 2.9 f: a hard metallic clang, dense to the top

ring.note: Seconds the index falls in a straight line to its floor, 0.5 at 0 to 5 at 1. Only the colour rings down, the level stays. Colour 90 % settled at 0.5 / 2.0 / 4.15 s for 0 / .44 / 1.

quick.gloss: colour 90 % down by 1.0 s: a short clang, then the settled tone

medium.gloss: colour 90 % down by 2.0 s: the clang fades over a couple of seconds

long.gloss: colour 90 % down by 3.9 s: the strike's brightness lingers deep into the note

detune.note: Doublet spacing d = 0..2 Hz, fixed in Hz: the bell sits on the key, its partner d Hz above. Partial k beats at |1 + k*1.41|*d Hz. 0 stands still. A tuner reads the key; the pair's weighted mean is 0.22*d Hz sharp.

pure.gloss: no doublet: one still tone, the level stands once the colour has settled

gentle.gloss: 0.8 Hz spacing: key beats 0.8 Hz, the 0.41 f partial 0.33 Hz -- a slow sway

wide.gloss: 1.7 Hz spacing: key 1.7 Hz, 2.41 f 4.1 Hz -- a quick, plainly audible warble

techniques.code:
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes
; Chowning FM bell (JAES 1973): c:m 1:1.41 puts the sidebands off the harmonic grid
kindex  = 0.3333 ; index [0.0..1.0]: the FM index at the strike, 1 at 0 to 16 at 1 -- how many sidebands the bell starts with
kring   = 0.4444 ; ring [0.0..1.0]: seconds the index takes to fall to its floor, 0.5 at 0 to 5 at 1 -- the colour rings down, the level stays
kdetune = 0.55   ; detune [0.0..1.0]: the doublet's spacing, 0 to 2 Hz -- the bell on the key, its partner that far above
kf0     = kfreq * koct1
kd0     = 2 * kdetune                  ; Hz, not cents: a fixed beat rate
kroom0  limit (min(sr * 0.45, 20000) / kf0 - 1) / 1.41 - 1, 0, 40  ; index cap: top sideband in band
kpk0    min 1 + 15 * kindex, kroom0
kix0    = kpk0 * (0.2417 + 0.7583 * (1 - min(knote / (0.5 + 4.5 * kring), 1)))
        if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
          reinit FMBELLON
        endif
FMBELLON:
abl0    foscili 0.4, kf0, 1, 1.41, kix0, giSine
abt0    foscili 0.26, kf0 + kd0, 1, 1.41, kix0 * 0.94, giSine
; reference: a sine from phase 0, not a constant, so the fresh follower starts right
aref0   poscil 0.46, kf0, giSine
; keep: at detune 0 the carriers add in phase; 0.1 Hz holds the mean, passes the beat
abal0   balance abl0 + abt0, aref0, 0.1
        rireturn
asig    = abal0 * kvol1

techniques.why: A struck cast church bell by modal synthesis: 29 two-pole resonators (`zdf_2pole`) at the measured partials of a modern English bell (Perrin, Charnley & DePont, JSV 90(1) 1983, Table 2), decays from Fletcher & Rossing Table 21.4 as constant Q: at 220 Hz the prime rings 43 s, the hum 138 s, until the voice releases. kfreq is the strike note (prime); the hum sounds an octave below it, the nominal an octave above. Every partial but the 18-meridian one is a split pair that beats, the low three as wide as the old Warner bell's (1855). third retunes only tierce and (4,1#) to the major-third bell (Schoofs et al. 1987). Strike amplitudes are this entry's own reading of Oancea et al. 2011. A re-strike restarts the bank, it never builds up; a bend or legato key change retunes the ring. NOT the two-operator FM bell (fm_bell), NOT a handbell, tubular bell or chime.
techniques.code:
; DECAY: SELF
; LOUDNESS: clapper
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes
; Church bell by modal synthesis: Perrin, Charnley & DePont 1983; decays Fletcher & Rossing.
kc      = kfreq * koct1
kthd    = 0.0    ; third[0.0..1.0]: minor-third bell to major-third bell
kclp    = 4.0    ; clapper[1.0..16.0]: contact corner as a multiple of the strike note, heavy to light
kwrb    = 0.5    ; warble[0.0..1.0]: how far the two halves of each partial stand apart
kup     timeinsts
; The strike restarts the idle clock: the engine primes a new orchestra with the gate shut.
kidl    init 1
khit    changed2 ktrig
kidl    = (kgateraw > 0 ? 0 : (khit == 1 ? 0 : kidl) + ksmps / sr)
        if khit == 1 then
          reinit BELLHIT
        endif
asig    = 0
        if kidl > 0.3 kgoto BELLIDLE
BELLHIT:
icl     limit i(kclp), 1, 16
ith     limit i(kthd), 0, 1
iwb     limit i(kwrb), 0, 1
ikc     = i(kc)
ikc     = (ikc < 20 ? 220 : ikc)
ifc     limit ikc * icl, 20, 8000
iamp    = (i(kup) > 0 ? 1 : 0)
acon    mpulse iamp, 0
aex     tone acon, ifc
kth     limit kthd, 0, 1
kwb     limit kwrb, 0, 1
isum    = 0
idir    = 0
; CBELL(n'f'Q'amp'split): a resonator at f*(1+warble*split), f = kc*ratio (km2, km5: moved by
; `third`), i$F at the strike. CBELL2(n'n+1'f'Q'amp'split): the two halves, +split and -split.
; zdf_2pole, not mode: a retuned mode grows without bound. 0.25/sin, 1/cos, sin(x)/x and adir
; follow from its recurrence. Live weight <= strike weight: a partial out at the strike stays
; out. The 16 kHz fade acts in norm, output and adir. The sum stays out of the macro: faster.
#define CBELL(N'F'Q'A'S) #
iz      = i$F * (1 + iwb * $S)
iy      = 3.14159265 * (iz < 20 ? 20 : (iz > 16000 ? 16000 : iz)) / sr
ig$N    = $A * (iz >= 20 ? 1 : 0) * limit((16000 - iz) / 500, 0, 1)
isum    = isum + ig$N / sqrt(1 + (iz / ifc)^2)
idir    = idir + ig$N * 0.25 * tan(iy)
is$N    = 0.25 / sin(iy)
kv      = $F * (1 + kwb * $S)
kp      limit kv, 20, 16000
kx      = 3.14159265 * kp / sr
kw$N    = is$N * min($A * limit((16000 - kv) / 500, 0, 1), ig$N) / cos(kx)
a$N     zdf_2pole aex, kp, $Q * sin(2 * kx) / (2 * kx)
#
#define CBELL2(I'J'G'R'B'T) #
$CBELL($I'$G'$R'$B'$T)
$CBELL($J'$G'$R'$B'-$T)
#
$CBELL2(0'1'kc*.4996'6923'.0101'.001175)
$CBELL2(2'3'kc'4264'.2715'.00264)
ikm2    = ikc * (1.1827 * (1.25 / 1.1827) ^ ith)
km2     = kc * (1.1827 * (1.25 / 1.1827) ^ kth)
$CBELL2(4'5'km2'5042'.084'.000995)
$CBELL2(6'7'kc*1.5062'2408'.102'.0001815)
$CBELL2(8'9'kc*2'1599'.5'.000256)
ikm5    = ikc * (2.5137 * (2.575 / 2.5137) ^ ith)
km5     = kc * (2.5137 * (2.575 / 2.5137) ^ kth)
$CBELL2(10'11'km5'938'.342'.000102)
$CBELL2(12'13'kc*2.662'2554'.342'.0001925)
$CBELL2(14'15'kc*3.0112'4012'.1815'.000905)
$CBELL2(16'17'kc*4.1664'4663'.342'.00088)
$CBELL2(18'19'kc*5.4327'4343'.342'.001115)
$CBELL2(20'21'kc*6.7961'3622'.342'.000452)
$CBELL(22'kc*8.2153'3622'.684'0)
$CBELL2(23'24'kc*9.687'3622'.342'.000176)
$CBELL2(25'26'kc*11.19'3622'.342'.000305)
$CBELL2(27'28'kc*12.71'3622'.342'.00047)
inrm    = 4.45 / (isum > 0 ? isum : 1)
adir    = aex * idir
        rireturn
asig    = (a0 * kw0 + a1 * kw1 + a2 * kw2 + a3 * kw3 + a4 * kw4 + a5 * kw5 + a6 * kw6 + a7 * kw7 + a8 * kw8 + a9 * kw9 + a10 * kw10 + a11 * kw11 + a12 * kw12 + a13 * kw13 + a14 * kw14 + a15 * kw15 + a16 * kw16 + a17 * kw17 + a18 * kw18 + a19 * kw19 + a20 * kw20 + a21 * kw21 + a22 * kw22 + a23 * kw23 + a24 * kw24 + a25 * kw25 + a26 * kw26 + a27 * kw27 + a28 * kw28 - adir) * inrm * kvol1
BELLIDLE:

third.note: Tierce 1.1827 f (290 c, the minor-third bell) to 1.25 f (386 c, major), the (4,1#) 2.5137 -> 2.575 f with it; hum, prime, quint and nominal stay. Live: turning it while the bell rings slides the tierce.

minor.gloss: tierce a flat minor third above the strike note: the church-bell sound

neutral.gloss: tierce 338 c, between minor and major: an unsettled bell

major.gloss: tierce a pure major third (1.25 f): the brighter, major-third bell

clapper.note: One-pole contact corner = clapper x strike note, max 8 kHz; read at the strike. At 220 Hz the strike's centroid (first 50 ms) is 513 / 737 / 1091 Hz at 1 / 4 / 16, peaks 1.3 dB apart. Above a 500 Hz key, 16 is capped.

heavy.gloss: corner at the note: strike centroid 2.3 f at 220 Hz, the darkest strike

medium.gloss: corner at 4x the note: strike centroid 3.4 f, falling to 1.4 f by 2 s

light.gloss: corner at 16x: strike centroid 5 f at 220 Hz, the hardest, brightest strike

warble.note: Each split partial is two equal halves, warble x its measured split apart: beat = warble x split x f, nulls full. At 220 Hz, warble .5: prime 0.58 Hz, tierce 0.26, hum 0.13. Live; 1 is the source bells' own splits.

still.gloss: no splits: every partial one steady tone, the bell only decays

gentle.gloss: half the source splits: at 220 Hz the prime swells every 1.7 s

wide.gloss: the source bells' splits: at 220 Hz the prime beats 1.2 Hz

heard.hinweis: Körper am 2026-11-21 neu gebaut (Modalsynthese nach der Partialtabelle von Perrin, Charnley & DePont; Knöpfe third/clapper/warble), bisher nur gemessen, nicht gehört. „church bell“ und „carillon“ benennen ein reales Instrument und sind gegen eine Aufnahme zu beurteilen.

techniques.why: A struck orchestral chime (tubular bell), left to ring. Modal synthesis: eight `zdf_2pole` resonators at the modes of a plugged chime (Fletcher & Rossing, Table 19.3), weighted by free-free shapes at the strike point, struck through a one-pole hammer. kfreq is the STRIKE TONE, heard an octave under the fourth mode: no partial sits on it, two modes sound below it. Damping borrowed from mallet_bar's aluminium: at 220 Hz 42 s low, 14 s high, until the envelope closes. A re-strike restarts the ring; a bend retunes it. NOT a marimba or glockenspiel bar (mallet_bar), NOT a church bell (cast_bell), NOT the FM bell (fm_bell).
techniques.code:
; DECAY: SELF
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes -- the key is the STRIKE TONE, a virtual pitch an octave under mode 4;
; no partial sits on the key: a pitch probe looking for one there fails by design
; modal synthesis, struck chime: Fletcher & Rossing 1998, Table 19.3 (193 g plug)
; damping: mallet_bar's aluminium law, BORROWED
; Level: G = 3.57 in inrm is a level choice, not part of the model.
kc      = kfreq * koct1
khm     = 4.0    ; hammer[1.0..16.0]: how hard the hammer is, soft felt to hard plastic, as the contact corner over the strike tone
kspt    = 0.0    ; spot[0.0..0.22]: where the tube is struck, from its capped top down to the node of its lowest mode
kup     timeinsts
; idle skip: the strike restarts the idle clock, the engine primes with the gate shut
kidl    init 1
khit    changed2 ktrig
kidl    = (kgateraw > 0 ? 0 : (khit == 1 ? 0 : kidl) + ksmps / sr)
        if khit == 1 then
          reinit TBELLHIT
        endif
asig    = 0
        if kidl > 0.3 kgoto TBELLIDLE
TBELLHIT:
im      limit i(khm), 1, 16
ix      limit i(kspt), 0, 0.22
ikc     = i(kc)
ikc     = (ikc < 20 ? 220 : ikc)
ifc     limit ikc * im, 20, 8000
iamp    = (i(kup) > 0 ? 1 : 0)
acon    mpulse iamp, 0
aex     tone acon, ifc
igb     = 0.33
ive     = 8.03e-9
isum    = 0
asum    = 0
; TBELLMODE(n'ratio'beta'sigma): one mode; beta, sigma = its uniform-bar free-free shape
; zdf_2pole, not mode: a retuned mode grows without bound
; 0.5/sin(2 pi f/sr): every mode starts at 1/2, at either rate
#define TBELLMODE(N'R'B'S) #
ib      = $B * ix
iw$N    = abs(cosh(ib) + cos(ib) - $S * (sinh(ib) + sin(ib))) / 2
if$N    = ikc * $R
iQ$N    = sr * sin(6.28318531 * limit(if$N, 20, 16000) / sr) / (igb + 39.4784176 * ive * if$N * if$N)
ie$N    = (if$N >= 20 ? 1 : 0) * limit((16000 - if$N) / 500, 0, 1)
ig$N    = ie$N / sqrt(1 + (if$N / ifc)^2)
isum    = isum + iw$N * ig$N
kq$N    = kc * $R
kp$N    limit kq$N, 20, 16000
a$N     zdf_2pole aex * (ie$N > 0 ? 1 : 0) * (0.5 / sin(6.28318531 * kp$N / sr)), kp$N, iQ$N, 2
asum    = asum + a$N * iw$N * min(limit((16000 - kq$N) / 500, 0, 1), ie$N)
#
$TBELLMODE(1'0.24'4.73004'0.98250)
$TBELLMODE(2'0.63'7.85320'1.00078)
$TBELLMODE(3'1.22'10.99561'0.99997)
$TBELLMODE(4'2.00'14.13717'1)
$TBELLMODE(5'2.93'17.27876'1)
$TBELLMODE(6'4.01'20.42035'1)
$TBELLMODE(7'5.21'23.56194'1)
$TBELLMODE(8'6.50'26.70354'1)
; inrm inside the section: after rireturn an i-term folds once, at build
inrm    = 3.57 / (isum > 0 ? isum : 1)
        rireturn
asig    = asum * inrm * kvol1
TBELLIDLE:

hammer.note: Contact corner = hammer x strike tone, max 8 kHz: low leaves the lower modes, high strikes every mode. Read at the strike.

soft.gloss: the low modes lead: dark, muffled

medium.gloss: strike-tone modes clear, top modes rounded

hard.gloss: every mode struck: the brightest strike

spot.note: Strike point from the capped top, in tube lengths (uniform-bar shapes); not monotonic, each mode has its own nodes. Read at the strike.

rim.gloss: where players strike: every mode full

muted.gloss: modes 4-6 near their nodes: the strike tone fades

no deep hum.gloss: the lowest mode on its node

heard.hinweis: Neuer Körper, nur gemessen, nicht gehört. 'Röhrenglocke' benennt ein reales Instrument und ist gegen eine Aufnahme zu beurteilen. Die Taste ist der Schlagton, eine virtuelle Tonhöhe eine Oktave unter der vierten Mode: kein Teilton liegt auf ihr, zwei Moden klingen darunter; ein Tonhöhenmesser, der dort einen Teilton sucht, meldet Fehler. Die Dämpfung ist von mallet_bars Aluminium geborgt, für Messing nicht gemessen. Ein Neuanschlag startet den Ausklang neu.

techniques.why: three-operator phase modulation: TWO modulators driving one carrier's phase in linear combination, so the spectrum carries two sideband families and the drive travels back and forth BETWEEN them. That travel is what two operators cannot do -- with one modulator a control can only make its single family stronger or weaker, never trade it for a different one. Method: Chowning, JAES 21(7), 1973; the topology and the word-to-parameter directions from Hayes & Saitis 2020, thirty sound designers on exactly this layout. Csound 6.18 has no generic N-operator opcode, so the two modulators are summed into a `phasor` and read through `tablei`. BJ's reading of the setting this was found at, 2026-07-30: bassoon-like, with a kind of pulse-width modulation -- the `fm` entry beside it reads tine-piano-like. It is NOT a bassoon and does not claim to be one; that reading is what two families trading sounds like at ratio 1.0. DECLARED, and the first thing to know before routing it as a melodic voice: the body transposes exactly with `kfreq`, but WHICH OCTAVE it sounds in is set by `ratio 3`. With `ratio 2` at 1.0 a half-integer `ratio 3` puts the whole spectrum on a grid of `kfreq`/2, so the note sounds an OCTAVE BELOW the key -- measured f0 exactly `kfreq`/2 at 1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5, 5.5 and 6.5, and exactly `kfreq` at 2, 3, 4, 6, 7 and 8, at every register from 55 to 1760 Hz. That subharmonic grid is a setting the axis offers, not the one it ships on: the default is 6.0 and plays the key (+0 ct measured). DECLARED: it STANDS -- the host owns the note-off, so unlike `fm`/`fm_bell`/`metallic_fm` there is no index decay ringing it down (sustain 0.996 to 0.999 across six registers). The spectrum is HARMONIC at every setting: 1.3 to 2.1 % of the energy off the series, measured against the grid the body actually has. An earlier reading of this entry reported 59 to 64 % "off-series" and called the axis an alternation between harmonic and inharmonic -- that was the partials counted against the KEY on a body sounding an octave below it, i.e. the signature of the subharmonic above and not of inharmonicity. What alternates along `ratio 3` is the sounding octave, not the harmonicity. Hayes & Saitis report that on this topology `bright` and `rough` load on the same parameter moves, so a setting cannot be made brighter without also being heard as rougher; that is their finding on their data. Nothing in this repository measures either word, so it is not restated here as a measurement -- reach for this entry for brightness and for two-family movement, and treat roughness as untested. THE MOVEMENT IS IN THE SUSTAIN, and that has to be said because the platform's own movement meter reads the whole note and a spectral attack alone can satisfy it: with the trade frozen this body reads 105 cents over the note and 0 through the sustain, so its onset alone would clear the 60-cent threshold. Running, it reads 748 cents through the sustain at the default (307 to 1405 across the axes). The band is bounded by Carson's rule SUMMED over both operators -- carrier + (I+1)*fm each, both spending the same room -- and the whole drive is scaled by one factor when it does not fit, so the balance between the families and the FRACTION that travels survive the bound. Bounding each operator as if it were alone let the travelling drive arrive on top of an already-full index: at ratio 8/8, both indices 0.6 and `trade` 0.75 on a 440 Hz note at sr 44100 that put a sideband at 49 kHz and 42.7 % of the energy off the grid, against 1.4 % now. The cost of the bound is at the top of the keyboard: above about 880 Hz the drive is scaled down and the body thins toward a sine (centroid 6050 Hz at 880, 5489 at 1760). Two operators on exactly the SAME ratio are one oscillator with a constant total drive and have nothing to trade: unguarded, the diagonal moves 0 to 9 cents through the sustain. A separation of 0.01 already moves 1130, so the guard fires only within 0.02 and pushes toward the middle of the range, which reaches 0.7 % of the ratio plane and cannot leave the declared range. The trade oscillator is FREE-RUNNING and the note-on does not reset it, which is the platform's own rule for a loop -- so two notes played minutes apart start at different points in the breath, and the first window's colour differs by up to 375 Hz depending on how long the plugin has been open. Loudness inside a note: 0.01 to 0.19 dB at 220 Hz across all six axes, 0.03 to 0.20 dB at 55 Hz. GATED 2026-07-30 (`tools/lco_axis_probe.py --gate`, 729 corners x 6 registers, at the gate's sr 44100): every corner renders, moves and holds one loudness -- loudness spread 0.03 dB across the corners, 0.0 dB across the registers, 0.03 dB crossed, worst peak 0.66 against the host's 2.52. It reports 339 of 3645 corner-renders away from 220 Hz that do not move, 338 of them at 1760 Hz: at sr 44100 the band ends eleven harmonics above an 1760 Hz note, and two sideband families at high ratios do not fit in it at all, so the band bound scales the drive to nothing. That is the gate's rate, not the instrument's -- re-rendered at the plugin's default 176400 the same corners move 1066 to 1151 cents. Nearest existing entry, and what it was heard against: `fm`.
techniques.code:
kc      = kfreq * koct1
kr2     = 1.00   ; ratio 2[1.0..8.0]: operator 2's tuning ratio -- a whole number is harmonic, between them not
kr3     = 6.00   ; ratio 3[1.0..8.0]: operator 3's ratio, the second family
ki2     = 0.26   ; index 2[0.0..0.6]: how deep operator 2 drives, in CYCLES of carrier phase
ki3     = 0.20   ; index 3[0.0..0.6]: how deep operator 3 drives
ktrd    = 0.21   ; trade[0.20..0.75]: what FRACTION of the drive travels between the two operators.
                 ;   A fraction and not an amount, so it means the same at any depth: a fixed amount
                 ;   is swamped once both indices are deep. The floor is not zero -- a body always
                 ;   trades a little. The floor is set by the THINNEST body, not by this default:

                 ;   is swamped once both indices are deep. The floor is not zero -- a body always
                 ;   trades a little. The floor is set by the THINNEST body, not by this default:
                 ;   with both indices at zero, 0.10 leaves two ratio settings static and 0.20 does not
kons    = 0.6    ; onset[0.002..0.6]: seconds the sidebands need to arrive -- a SPECTRAL attack
kr3g    = (abs(kr3 - kr2) < 0.02 ? (kr2 > 4.5 ? kr2 - 1.75 : kr2 + 1.75) : kr3)  ; two operators
                                            ;   on exactly the SAME ratio are ONE oscillator with a
                                            ;   constant total drive, so there is nothing to trade:
                                            ;   measured, the diagonal moves 0 to 9 cents through the
                                            ;   sustain. A separation of 0.01 already moves 1130, so
                                            ;   only true coincidence is escaped -- and TOWARDS the
                                            ;   middle, so the push cannot leave the declared range
kdrv    = ki2 + ki3 + 0.20                  ; the drive there is to share, plus a floor so a body
                                            ;   with both indices at zero still has something to trade
ktr     = ktrd * kdrv                       ; the amount that travels, before the band is consulted
kpk2    = max(ki2 + ktr, 0.001)             ; what an operator PEAKS at is its own index PLUS all of
kpk3    = max(ki3 + ktr, 0.001)             ;   the travelling drive -- both arrive on one operator
kroom   limit min(sr * 0.45, 20000) / kc - 1 - kr2 - kr3g, 0, 4000  ; the room the BAND leaves above the two
                                            ;   modulators' first pair. Carson's rule per operator,
                                            ;   summed: (I+1)*fm each, and they spend the SAME room.
                                            ;   Bounding each operator as if it were alone is what put
                                            ;   a 49 kHz sideband on a 440 Hz note at sr 44100
kneed   = 6.2832 * (kpk2 * kr2 + kpk3 * kr3g)   ; radians, so cycles * 2pi
kscl    = min(1, kroom / kneed)              ; one factor for all three, so the balance between the
                                            ;   families and the FRACTION that travels survive it
ki2c    = ki2 * kscl
ki3c    = ki3 * kscl
ktrc    = ktr * kscl
ksw     oscili 0.5, 0.45, giSine            ; free-running, 2.2 s -- more than one cycle in a 3 s note
kt2     = ktrc * (0.5 + ksw)                ; the SAME drive, moving from operator 2 ...
kt3     = ktrc * (0.5 - ksw)                ;   ... to operator 3 and back. Not a level wobble:
karr    = min(knote / kons, 1)              ;   what changes is WHICH family carries the spectrum
am2     poscil (ki2c + kt2) * karr, kc * kr2, giSine
am3     poscil (ki3c + kt3) * karr, kc * kr3g, giSine
aph     phasor kc
apm     = aph + am2 + am3
acar    tablei apm, giSine, 1, 0, 1
aref    poscil 0.45, kc                     ; steady level reference
asig    balance acar, aref, 10              ; loudness held, colour free. 10 Hz not 1: at a long onset
                                            ;   on a 55 Hz note a 1 Hz follower cannot keep up
asig    = asig * kvol1

heard.hinweis: 2026-07-30: trägt zusätzlich die Oberflächenformen des gestrichenen Eintrags `fm` (fm, frequency modulation, phase modulation, operator …), weil das Verfahren hier weiterlebt und das Wort sonst ins Leere liefe. NICHT übernommen: „2 op fm“ / „2 operator fm“ — das benennt eine Konstruktion, die dieser Eintrag nicht ist. 2026-07-31: dazu die Oberflächenformen des ebenfalls gestrichenen `fm_ep` (electric piano, rhodes, wurlitzer, tine, reed piano, dx piano …), auf BJs Wort „fm_ep ist primitiv und auf der Abschussliste“ (2026-07-30) und „ep_fm3“ (2026-07-31). NICHT übernommen: das nackte „piano“ — das benennt ein akustisches Klavier, und in der Bibliothek gibt es keines; das Wort läuft jetzt ins Leere, statt auf eine Frequenzmodulation zu zeigen, die es nicht einlöst. ERKLÄRTE LÜCKE: `fm_ep` hatte `ring` und `strike`, dieser Eintrag hat weder eine Abklingzeit noch einen Anschlag — er STEHT (Sustain 0,996 bis 0,999). Ein E-Piano klingt ab. Der Eintrag mit Abklingzeit und Feedback ist `fm_stack`. 2026-07-31, BJs erster Höreindruck auf der 4x-Seite: der Eintrag ist „sehr mächtig“, und EINE Kombination hat er benannt — `ratio 3` = under zusammen mit `onset` = slow geht „sehr klar richtung trombone“. Das ist die erste Wort-Kombination-Zuordnung, die dieser Eintrag von einem Ohr hat, und sie kommt nicht aus einer Messung: `under` legt das Spektrum eine Oktave unter die Taste, `slow` lässt die Seitenbänder langsam ankommen — zusammen ein tiefer Körper, dessen Helligkeit erst aufgeht. Nicht verallgemeinern und nicht umdeuten; es gilt für diese zwei Anker. 2026-07-31, zweiter Teil desselben Tages: die E-Piano-Oberflächenformen sind wieder hier weg und stehen jetzt auf `ep_fm3`, dem geschlagenen Gegenstück, das an diesem Tag auf BJs Anweisung gebaut wurde („nimm die neuen erkenntnisse und baue also ein ep_fm3 oder epiano als parameter im fm3"). Damit ist die oben ERKLÄRTE LÜCKE geschlossen: die Wörter zeigen nicht mehr auf einen stehenden Körper, sondern auf einen, der abklingt. Die beiden Einträge benennen einander wie `plucked_wire` und `string`: dieser hier ist die GEHALTENE FM-Lesart, `ep_fm3` die geschlagene.

techniques.why: electric piano -- tine, reed and the FM piano: a struck tine over a body that holds, and a note that falls away while the key is down. The STRUCK reading of frequency modulation -- `fm3` is the held one, and the two name each other the way `plucked_wire` and `string` do. Method: Chowning 1973's percussive construction, the modulation index carrying its own decaying envelope. The tine's ratio, its range and the fact that the far family dies while the near one stands are measured, not recalled: 1386 named electric pianos in the DX7 corpus, docs/LCO_TIMBRE_SEMANTICS.md §7. Pre-build record: docs/plans/PLAN_lco_ep_fm3.md. It replaces the struck `fm_ep`, which had every axis this one has except the two that were missing -- the tine's ratio was hardcoded at 14.2 with no knob on it, and the body did not decay at all. NAMED VOICINGS, on BJ's instruction of 2026-07-31 ("biete die klangcharacterista von rhodes I, II, V und wurlitzer etc. an") and corrected the same day on his second one: "ja, korrekt, ABER Du baust ein FM epiano, kein physisches." So the rows are NOT derived from what a real Rhodes pickup does. They are MEASURED from what FM programmers actually did when they wrote these names on a patch -- the DX7 corpus, grouped by the name on the voice (docs/LCO_TIMBRE_SEMANTICS.md §7, tools/dx7_corpus.py --profile). What the corpus separates, and by how much: | name | Stimmen | far ratio | far drive | ratio-2 share | carrier fall | | rhodes/roads | 971 | 14 in 521, then 12, 22, 10 | 71 | 3 % | 99->75 | | suitcase | 24 | 11, 13.5, 13, 12 | 75 | 0 % | 99->75 | | stage | 3 | 14 | 64 | 0 % | 99->75 | | mark 1 / mk 2 / mark iii | 21 | 1 and 14 | 65 | 0 % | 99->93 | | dyno | 157 | 14 in 32 AND 26 in 30 | 80 | 17 % | 99->75 | | wurlitzer | 334 | 14, then 11, 7 | 58 | 41 % | 99->85 | | tine | 99 | 12 in 32, then 14 | 58, and it STAYS (99->85) | 9 % | 99->90 | THREE THINGS THAT MEASUREMENT SAYS AND THE INSTRUMENT WORLD DOES NOT. First, the Mark numbers are not an FM distinction: 21 voices carry one across 119,296, there is no Mark V in the corpus at all, and what the few Mark patches DO share is that they barely decay (carrier 99->93 against everything else's 99->75). What FM programmers separated instead is `dyno` (157) and `suitcase` (24). Second, `dyno` is bimodal on the tine ratio -- 14 in 32 voices and 26 in 30 -- and it is the hottest drive of any group; that second mode is what the name means here. Third, and OPPOSITE to the acoustic instruments: an FM Wurlitzer patch decays LESS than an FM Rhodes patch (99->85 against 99->75), and its separation on this entry is not `tine` at all -- both sit at 14 -- but `hollow`, because 41 % of its modulators sit in the 2-8 band with 198 voices at exactly 2.0, against 3 % for the Rhodes. A modulator at twice the carrier is what cancels the even partials, which is this entry's `hollow` axis by construction. | voicing | tine | ting | ring | hollow | strike | decay | | rhodes | 14 | 0.55 | 0.30 | 0.10 | 0.62 | 0.45 | the corpus's centre of gravity | | rhodes suitcase | 12 | 0.62 | 0.30 | 0.05 | 0.62 | 0.45 | a lower tine and a hotter one | | rhodes stage | 14 | 0.42 | 0.30 | 0.05 | 0.55 | 0.45 | the softest drive of any group | | rhodes mark | 14 | 0.45 | 0.30 | 0.05 | 0.50 | 0.22 | rings on; the one thing the Mark patches share | | dyno | 26 | 0.75 | 0.30 | 0.35 | 0.72 | 0.45 | the second mode and the hottest drive | | wurlitzer | 14 | 0.38 | 0.30 | 0.80 | 0.60 | 0.33 | the even partials cancelled, weakest drive, and it rings LONGER than the Rhodes | | tine | 12 | 0.38 | 0.65 | 0.20 | 0.58 | 0.28 | the far family stays instead of dying | The far-ratio column transfers as a value, since both instruments count it in multiples of the note. The drive and envelope columns are DIRECTIONS only -- the DX7's output level rises with modulation index but does not count cycles, and its EG rate runs the opposite way to `onset`. So the ratios are measured and the other five columns are this entry's reading of a measured direction; BJ's ear decides them. WHAT THE PHYSICAL INSTRUMENTS DO, kept because it explains WHY the FM patches look like this and NOT as the source of any row above: Pfeifle & Muenster, "Tone Production of the Wurlitzer and Rhodes E-Pianos", DAGA 2017 Kiel, 556-559, measured a Rhodes Mark I/II and a Wurlitzer EP200 and found both timbres come from the PICKUP, not the vibrator -- tine and reed both move almost sinusoidally. A Rhodes tine centred on the wedge magnet outputs at TWICE the fundamental, and off centre, or under a larger deflection, the flux change turns asymmetric and the harmonics arrive; the inharmonic part is the brass tonebar and is strongest in the upper register. The Wurlitzer's reed has negligible higher modes, so its harmonics come from the reed's non-symmetric design changing the capacitance differently on each excursion -- the bark. That is why an FM Wurlitzer is built from a low-order modulator and an FM Rhodes from a high one. WHAT THESE ROWS DO NOT CARRY: the amplifier and the effects. The cased instrument is a tremolo, the stage instrument through a phase-shifter pedal is a phaser, and the bark is an overdrive -- none of that is in this body. THE EFFECTS ARE KNOBS ON THE SYNTH, NOT LINES IN THIS BODY. Wired 2026-07-31 on BJ's instruction ("Was fehlt sind Effekte ... verzerrung, tremolo, chorus, phaser"), they sit in the amplifier behind the voices, which is what these instruments' effects ARE: the cased instrument has ONE tremolo for the whole instrument, not one per key. Reach them with SET lines and never with Csound -- `fx_trem_rate` / `fx_trem_depth` / `fx_trem_stereo`, `fx_chorus_rate` / `fx_chorus_depth` / `fx_chorus_mix`, `fx_phaser_rate` / `fx_phaser_depth` / `fx_phaser_feedback` / `fx_phaser_mix`, `fx_dist_drive` / `fx_dist_mix`. All four are OFF at their defaults, so a prompt that does not ask for one gets none. TWO WORDS THAT WOULD OTHERWISE LAND IN THE WRONG PLACE: `tremolo` is also a movement in this library and `distorted` also a sound word, and both of those write into the BODY. Alongside this entry they belong on the knobs above -- a per-voice tremolo beats against itself the moment two keys are held, and this body's own drive is already its `strike` axis. WHERE THE NAMED VOICINGS PUT THEM: the cased voicing = a stereo PAN, because that instrument's vibrato pans between its two amplifier pairs, so `fx_trem_stereo` near 1 with a rate around 5 Hz; the reed voicing = an AMPLITUDE tremolo from its one amplifier, `fx_trem_stereo` 0; the stage voicing through a phase-shifter pedal = `fx_phaser_*` slow, rate under 0.5; the bright-chorused voicing = chorus. THE BARK IS NOT ON THIS LIST and must not be routed here -- BJ heard two attempts on 2026-07-31 and ruled it out: "es klingt nicht ab. das ist ein 4-sekunden-bark. ein bark bei einem epiano klingt aber nach hoechstens 1 sek ab ... das bark-Sample hat keine Transiente, die wird verschluckt." Measured, the amplifier cut the attack contrast from the dry body's +6.8 dB to +5.3 and its excess over that body GREW across the note (+3.9 to +5.0 dB) rather than dying. The corpus says why, over 842 named e-pianos: the far modulator -- the bright, barking part -- falls at envelope rate 50 where the carrier falls at 25, so the bark carries its OWN envelope at about twice the speed of the note. A stage behind the voices has no envelope; it follows the level, and the level falls more slowly than the modulation. So the bark is `strike` on THIS entry, in the body, and never `fx_dist_*`. Those five are starting points for the ear and NOT measurements -- the corpus above measures the patch, and a pedal in front of an amplifier leaves no trace in a DX7 voice.
techniques.code:
; DECAY: SELF
; LOUDNESS: decay
; Struck once and then falling away while the key is held, the way an electric piano
; does -- the player's envelope cannot hold it up. The STANDING reading of this body is
; `fm3`: a prompt that wants a held two-modulator FM tone belongs there, not here.
kc      = kfreq * koct1
ktine   = 14.0   ; tine[6.0..28.0]: where the metal of the strike stands, as a multiple of
                 ;   the note. Measured over 1386 named electric pianos in the DX7 corpus:
                 ;   14 is the mode (595 voices) and 10, 12, 18, 22, 26, 28 all occur
kting   = 0.55   ; ting[0.0..1.0]: how much of the strike is that metal
kring   = 0.30   ; ring[0.0..1.0]: how long the metal takes to die back into the body
khol    = 0.55   ; hollow[0.0..1.0]: the body's harmonics, full series to odd only
kstr    = 0.64   ; strike[0.0..1.0]: how bright the body starts before it softens
kdec    = 0.45   ; decay[0.0..1.0]: how fast the whole note falls away
; --- Chowning 1973 (JAES 21(7), 526-534) builds a struck tone by giving the modulation
;     INDEX its own decaying envelope, so the spectrum darkens as the note falls instead
;     of being filtered down. Both envelopes below are that, and the corpus says how the
;     two differ: a DX7 electric piano's FAR modulator dies back (envelope level 99 -> 75)
;     while its NEAR one stands (99 -> 93). So the body softens and then holds; the metal
;     goes away entirely.
ktau    = 0.08 + 1.40 * kring * kring                ; the tine's time constant, seconds
ktfd    = exp(-knote / ktau)                         ; and the one shape it decays on
kbdx    = (1.302 + 2.898 * kstr) * (0.60 + 0.40 * exp(-knote / 1.10))
; --- 0.60 and not 0.29 is the corpus's own number and it is load-bearing twice over. A
;     `foscili` at a carrier:modulator ratio of 1:1 or 1:2 has sidebands that fold through
;     DC and interfere with the upper ones, so its LEVEL is a function of its index -- at
;     amp 0.30 and 220 Hz, 1:1 measures +0.24, -0.43, -2.88, -1.49, +0.01 dB against a
;     sine at index 0.5, 0.9, 1.5, 3.2, 4.2. An index envelope on such a pair is therefore
;     also an amplitude envelope, and with the old 3.4x swing the whole body SWELLED
;     4.55 dB over the first 1.3 s at `decay` 0 / `hollow` 0.25 / `ting` 0, which
;     `; DECAY: SELF` does not cover and `--gate` does not catch (its swell candidate is a
;     linear fit from t = 1 s and reads the later decay as a fall). The corpus fixes the
;     depth without a fitted number: its NEAR modulators fall only from envelope level 99
;     to 93 over the note while the far ones fall to 75, which is where the settle belongs.
; --- 1.302..4.200 is `fm_ep`'s own index range, kept rather than re-chosen. Lowering
;     the floor to 0.8 left the body at index 0.23 once it had settled -- near enough
;     to a bare sine that `lco_axis_probe --gate` failed 27 corners for not moving,
;     all of them at `strike` 0 with `ting` 0. The old entry's floor is the capability
;     this one has to preserve, not a number to improve on.
ktng    = 3.0 * kting * ktfd
; --- the tine's LEVEL falls on that same shape and not only its index, because an index
;     falling to zero does not remove an operator pair -- it turns the pair into a bare
;     sine ON the note, which then adds in phase with the body. Measured before this line
;     existed: the whole body SWELLED 1.5 dB over the first half second and only fell
;     after, which `; DECAY: SELF` does not cover (`declares_decay` passes a fall and
;     fails a swell). The corpus has it right: its algorithm 5 gives every carrier its own
;     envelope, so the modulator's level cuts the index and the carrier's cuts the pair.
; --- Nyquist, Carson's rule PER PAIR. These are three separate carriers with one
;     modulator each, so each pair's deviation is its own -- unlike `fm3` and
;     `metallic_fm`, where two modulators arrive on ONE carrier phase and the room has to
;     be shared. What is reserved is what an operator can EVER ask for, never what it is
;     asking for now: a guard that divides by the live index divides the envelope and the
;     axis straight back out, and `metallic_fm` records three `ring` settings rendering
;     BIT-IDENTICAL from exactly that mistake.
kband   limit (min(sr * 0.45, 20000) / kc) - 1, 2, 4000  ; room above the carrier, in notes
ktr     limit ktine, 1, max(kband, 1)                ; the tine cannot stand above the band
; --- capped at the band and not at half of it. Half reserved room for the tine to keep an
;     index of 1, which `ksct` below already handles on its own -- and the cost was the
;     axis: measured, `tine` 14, 22 and 28 rendered IDENTICALLY from 880 Hz and the whole
;     declared range collapsed to one sound from 1530 Hz. That is the exact fault this
;     body's own guard comment cites against `metallic_fm`, left in the entry's headline
;     axis. At the band the collapse starts at about 2860 Hz instead, which is where the
;     physics really puts it: a 28th partial of 2860 Hz is 80 kHz and no reserve invents it.
kscb    = min(1, max(kband / 2 - 1, 0) / 4.2)        ; 4.200 = kbdx at the strike, `strike` 1
ksct    = min(1, max(kband / ktr - 1, 0) / 3.0)      ; 3.0 = ktng at the strike, `ting` 1
; --- three carriers on the note, which is the shape the corpus's own algorithm 5 has in
;     854 of those 1386 voices. `hollow` is a LEVEL crossfade and never a ratio sweep: a
;     modulator ratio swept from 1 to 2 passes through 1.5, and `fm3`'s `ratio 3` measures
;     what that does -- the note drops an octave. Equal power on both crossfades, so they
;     move colour and not level.
aevn    foscili 0.30, kc, 1, 1, kbdx * kscb, giSine    ; body, the full series
aodd    foscili 0.30, kc, 1, 2, kbdx * kscb, giSine, 0.25   ; body, even partials cancelled
; --- the quarter cycle on `aodd` is not a tuned number, it is QUADRATURE. Both body pairs
;     run on the same carrier, the same table and, without it, the same start phase, so
;     their fundamentals add IN PHASE and the sum is louder in the middle of `hollow` than
;     at either end -- and because a `foscili` at these ratios has a level that follows its
;     index (see above), that coherent sum is also a level that MOVES as `kbdx` decays.
;     Measured with both at phase 0: the body swelled 2.87 dB at `hollow` 0.25 while
;     `hollow` 0 and 1, each a single carrier, swelled 0.00. A quarter cycle puts the two
;     in quadrature at the note, where the sum is the power sum whatever the index does.
atin    foscili 0.30, kc, 1, ktr, ktng * ksct, giSine  ; the tine
abod    = aevn * sqrt(1 - khol) + aodd * sqrt(khol)
; --- body and tine are ONE equal-power crossfade whose position is the strike itself:
;     `ting` says how far it travels, `ktfd` brings it home. The hammer's energy goes into
;     the metal at the strike and comes back to the body as the metal dies, so the tine
;     LEAVES rather than thinning into a sine on the note -- and because the two sides are
;     complementary the sum's power is flat, which leaves `exp(-knote / ktaud)` as the only
;     amplitude shape in the body and therefore the only thing `; DECAY: SELF` has to
;     cover. Both other constructions were rendered and rejected on measurement, not
;     taste: with the tine merely losing its index the whole body SWELLED 1.5 dB before it
;     fell (a bare sine on the note, adding in phase with the body), and with the body
;     ducked for the whole note instead of for the strike `ting` cost 5.2 dB across its
;     own range -- a colour control behaving as a volume control, which
;     docs/LCO_CONCEPT.md §4 requires to stay catchable.
kmix    = kting * ktfd
asum    = abod * sqrt(1 - kmix) + atin * sqrt(kmix)
; --- NO level follower anywhere in this body, on purpose. `fm_ep` held its loudness with
;     `balance ..., 10`, and a 10 Hz corner tracks and FLATTENS everything slower than
;     itself -- a tine decaying with a 0.21 s constant is 4.8 Hz, so the strike was being
;     levelled out by the body's own loudness guard. That is what BJ heard as "eintoenig
;     und schlicht" (2026-07-31). Moving the corner does not repair it: at `ring` = 1 the
;     tine's constant is 1.5 s, which is under 1 Hz as well. It is not needed either --
;     frequency modulation redistributes power rather than adding it, and both crossfades
;     above are equal-power, so the level holds across every axis without a follower.
ktaud   = 0.30 + 11.0 * (1 - kdec) * (1 - kdec)       ; seconds
asig    = asum * exp(-knote / ktaud) * kvol1

tine.note: where the metal of the strike stands, as a multiple of the note. THIS IS THE AXIS `fm_ep` DID NOT HAVE: it hardcoded 14.2 and put no control on it, which is the defect docs/LCO_TIMBRE_SEMANTICS.md §4.8 records for the old `fm` -- "what the designers reached for hardest has no knob here". Hayes & Saitis 2020 measured the modulator tuning ratio as the single largest correlate of `bright` (0.56/0.54, p<.001) over thirty sound designers on this topology, so raising this is their measured direction for that word. The RANGE is the corpus's own: over 1386 named electric pianos 14 is the mode with 595 voices, and 10, 12, 18, 22, 26 and 28 all occur -- the tine is a range and not a number. DECLARED, and measured rather than softened: this axis DIES at the top of the keyboard, because a 28th partial of 2860 Hz is 80 kHz and no reserve invents it. Five values of this axis rendered at one pitch come back as 5 different sounds at 220 Hz, 4 at 880, 3 at 1530, 2 at 2000 and ONE from about 2860 Hz up -- above that the entry has five axes, not six.

close metal.gloss: the metal sits near the body, more thud than ting

tine.gloss: the corpus's own most common tine, 595 of 1386 voices

high tine.gloss: thin and glassy, well clear of the body

needle.gloss: the top of the corpus's range; only low notes carry it

ting.note: how much of the strike is metal. This is the single feature that separates an electric piano from a plain FM tone; at 0 the instrument is only its body. The metal fades back out of the tone as the note is held -- it loses its brightness, and it trades against the body rather than being added on top, so this moves colour and not level. Hayes & Saitis measured the modulator GAIN rising for both `bright` (0.41/0.52) and `rough` (0.63/0.51).

none.gloss: the body alone, no metal in the strike

classic.gloss: the default: a struck electric piano

clangy.gloss: the metal is most of the attack

ring.note: how long the metal takes to die back into the body -- the tine's time constant, 0.08 s at the bottom and 1.48 s at the top. Short is a quick struck-tine click, long is a metallic buzz that stays through most of the note. Both ends are the corpus's: its far modulators fall from envelope level 99 to 75 at rate 50, which is quick, but the rate varies across the 1386 voices. This is the tine's OWN decay and not the note's -- that is `decay`.

click.gloss: the metal is gone in a third of a second

medium.gloss: the metal carries into the note

long.gloss: a wurlitzer-like reed that buzzes on

hollow.note: the body's harmonics, from the full series to odd only. Low keeps every harmonic and sounds broad and piano-like; high cancels the even ones, which is what makes a reed sound hollow and nasal. It is a LEVEL crossfade between two bodies and never a ratio sweep: a modulator ratio swept from 1 to 2 passes through 1.5, and `fm3`'s `ratio 3` measures what that does -- the note drops an octave. Equal power, so it moves colour and not level.

strike.note: how bright the body starts before it softens. This shapes the tone and not the volume -- a hard strike is brighter, not louder, because frequency modulation redistributes power rather than adding it. The body settles to 29 % of its opening index over about a second and then HOLDS there, which is the corpus's near modulator: envelope level 99 falling only to 93 while the far one falls to 75.

soft.gloss: barely struck, almost a sine body

hard.gloss: the body opens bright and closes down over a second

decay.note: how fast the whole note falls away while the key is held: a time constant of 11.3 s at the bottom and 0.30 s at the top. This is the axis `fm_ep` did not have at all -- docs/LCO_CONCEPT.md §4 records that `fm_ep` emitted no amplitude envelope and was the STANDING reading of an instrument whose whole character is that it falls away, and that "the convention's other half -- the real instrument, with its own decay -- does not exist at all". The body declares `; DECAY: SELF` and the player's envelope cannot hold the note up. A prompt that wants a held FM tone belongs in `fm3`. The corpus's carriers decay too, from envelope level 99 to 75.

clipped.gloss: a third of a second; struck and gone

heard.hinweis: Gebaut als eigener Eintrag und nicht als Parameter in `fm3`, aus drei Gründen, die in docs/plans/PLAN_lco_ep_fm3.md stehen: ein `epiano`-Regler müsste Tine-Verhältnis, Tine-Abklingen und Notenabklingen zugleich treiben, was Authoring-Regel 2 verbietet; `fm3` ist als STEHEND deklariert und BJ hat es so gehört; und die E-Piano-Wörter standen bereits auf `fm3` mit einer dort ERKLÄRTEN Lücke, die ein Eintrag schließt und ein Regler nicht. CLAUDE.md Authoring-Regel 6 untersagt einen Build für ein FM-E-Piano ausdrücklich (BJ, 2026-07-26); die Anweisung vom 2026-07-31 ist die spätere und wurde als solche behandelt, nicht stillschweigend umgangen. VERGLEICH, gerendert VOR der ersten Orchesterzeile (Regel 4): tools/lco_listening/ep_fm3_ab/ mit `metallic_fm` als nächstem Bibliothekseintrag und drei SA3-Referenzen auf „solo electric piano", weil dieser Eintrag den Namen eines echten Instruments führt. Versuchsbudget: drei. OFFENER DEFEKT, gemessen und nicht behoben: bei langen `decay`-Werten SCHWILLT dieser Körper um bis zu 1,99 dB, bevor er fällt (16 von 270 abgesuchten Ecken über 1 dB, am schlimmsten bei `decay` 0 / `hollow` 1,0 / `ting` 0,5) — dort ist die eigene `; DECAY: SELF`-Deklaration also unwahr. Ursache strukturell: ein `foscili` bei Träger:Modulator 1:1 oder 1:2 hat Seitenbänder, die durch DC falten, sein Pegel hängt damit vom Index ab, und eine Indexhüllkurve auf so einem Paar ist zugleich eine Amplitudenhüllkurve; bei `decay` 0 fällt die deklarierte Kurve nur 0,77 dB/s und wird davon überholt. Drei Korrekturen sind gelaufen und stehen mit ihren Messwerten in den Kommentaren des Körpers (4,55 → 2,87 → 1,99 dB); eine vierte würde die schlimmste Ecke wieder nur verschieben. `lco_axis_probe --gate` sieht das NICHT — sein Schwell-Kandidat ist eine Gerade ab t = 1 s und liest den Anstieg als Fall. techniques.why: drum head / membrane / skin: the STANDING skin -- a membrane kept sounding by a continuous rub (hand, friction, wind), not struck; nothing decays, the note's envelope is the host's. Method: modal synthesis of the circular membrane, ten `mvmfilter` resonators (Mathews & Smith 2003) at the Bessel-zero ratios j_mn/j_11 (Morse & Ingard; Fletcher & Rossing) driven by one noise weighted |J_m(j_mn r)| at the rub point, with the kettledrum ratios and relative Q measured by Christian, Davis, Tubis, Anderson, Mills & Rossing (JASA 1984). pitched = ideal membrane to measured kettledrum, strikepos = rubbed at the centre to near the rim, damping = open ringing to a muffled skin. Declared: at pitched 1 the upper modes stand on 2:3:4:5:6 over half the key, so the ear can hear the octave below the played note, as on timpani. A struck drum is struck_drum; conga, bongo, djembe, tabla stay here.

pitched.note: Moves every mode as itself from the ideal membrane's Bessel ratios (0) to the measured kettledrum's (1); the key stays the (1,1) mode. Toward 1 the upper modes line up as 2:3:4:5:6 over half the key.

tom.gloss: Bessel ratios: loudest near 1, 1.35, 1.83, 2.2-2.3 x key, (0,1) at 0.63, no series

mixed.gloss: halfway between the two sets: peaks 11 dB over the noise, centroid 2.4-2.5 f

timpani.gloss: 1, 1.48, 1.97, 2.87 x key: a series on half the key; peaks 11-12 dB over the noise

strikepos.note: Where the skin is rubbed: the centre (0) to r = 0.85 of the radius (1), never on the rim. Each mode enters by its shape there, |J_m(j_mn r)|; the point drifts by up to 0.1 around the knob, slowly.

centre.gloss: round modes only: key band -21 dB; the broad (0,1) below the key holds -6 dB of all

halfway.gloss: key band -8..-9 dB of the total, below-key -10; peaks 14 dB over the noise

rim.gloss: r = 0.85: the rippling (m,1) modes, below-key band -17 dB; peaks 18 dB over the noise

damping.note: One factor on every mode's Q, the (1,1) from 40 open to 4 muffled. The level holds, so a lower Q hands more of it to the hiss between the modes: muffled is brighter, not darker.

open.gloss: (1,1) Q 40: resonances 14-15 dB over the noise; centroid 1.9-2.0 f

damped.gloss: (1,1) Q 12.6: peaks 8-10 dB over the noise; centroid 2.6-2.8 f

muffled.gloss: (1,1) Q 4: peaks 5-6 dB over the hiss between them; centroid 3.4-3.6 f

techniques.code:
; DRUM HEAD: a membrane kept sounding by a continuous rub, not struck; nothing decays.
; Modal synthesis of the circular membrane: Bessel ratios j_mn/j_11 at pitched 0, the kettledrum measured by Christian, Davis, Tubis et al. (JASA 1984) at 1; one noise enters each mode by its shape |J_m(j_mn r)| at the rub point r.
; mvmfilter, not mode: mode rescales its state when the key changes and every lower note bursts.
; kP is the exact noise power of the ten recursions, from mvmfilter's own impulse response (pairwise cross-power G_ij): one rms at every key, setting and rate.
; The rub point drifts slowly around the knob, keyed to the note: that drift is the movement.
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes

kpitch  = 0.25   ; pitched [0..1]: ideal membrane at 0, measured kettledrum at 1, every mode moving as itself
kspot   = 0.35   ; strikepos [0..1]: where the skin is rubbed, from its centre out to near the rim
kdamp   = 0.35   ; damping [0..1]: one factor on the Q of every mode, from open ringing to a felt-muffled skin

kkey    = kfreq * koct1
ktop    = 15000
kpt     = kspot + 0.060 * sin(6.283185307 * 0.17 * knote) + 0.040 * sin(6.283185307 * 0.07 * knote)
kpt     = (kpt > 1 ? 2 - kpt : abs(kpt))
krr     = 0.85 * kpt
krr2    = krr * krr
kq      = 40 * (0.1 ^ kdamp)
kkp     init -1
kpp     init -1
kdp     init -1
kchg    = (kkey != kkp || kpitch != kpp || kdamp != kdp ? 1 : 0)
kkp     = kkey
kpp     = kpitch
kdp     = kdamp
; DHEADM(mode'ratio at pitched 0'its step to pitched 1'Q factor'r^m'7 coefficients of |J_m| in r^2)
#define DHEADM(N'R'D'QX'M'C0'C1'C2'C3'C4'C5'C6) #
kn$N    = $R + kpitch * $D
kf$N    limit kkey * kn$N, 20, ktop
kq$N    = kq * $QX
kt$N    = kq$N / (3.14159265 * kf$N)
kw$N    = (kkey * kn$N < ktop ? abs($M * ($C0 + krr2 * ($C1 + krr2 * ($C2 + krr2 * ($C3 + krr2 * ($C4 + krr2 * ($C5 + krr2 * ($C6)))))))) : 0)
#
$DHEADM(01'0.6276'0.1863'0.305'1'1'-1.4458'0.522582'-0.0839495'0.00758534'-0.000437551'1.63945e-05)
$DHEADM(11'1'0'1'krr'1.91585'-3.51606'2.15094'-0.657889'0.120636'-0.0145654'0.00108665)
$DHEADM(21'1.3403'0.1597'3.188'krr2'3.29683'-7.24603'5.97209'-2.62436'0.718382'-0.13081'0.0139285)
$DHEADM(02'1.4406'0.2105'0.826'1'1'-7.61776'14.5065'-12.2681'5.79739'-1.67392'0.257008)
$DHEADM(31'1.6651'0.3116'6.672'krr2 * krr'5.4107'-13.7655'14.0067'-7.90919'2.84651'-0.679037'0.0899344)
$DHEADM(12'1.8309'0.1691'1.25'krr'3.50776'-21.5793'44.23'-45.1858'27.2085'-10.0421'1.86931)
$DHEADM(41'1.9804'0.4615'5.189'krr2 * krr2'8.63481'-24.8594'29.8081'-20.3648'8.97672'-2.59148'0.396899)
$DHEADM(22'2.1967'0.6695'1.791'krr2'8.85566'-52.2669'115.493'-135.024'95.3807'-40.8862'8.48571)
$DHEADM(03'2.2585'0.4567'1.018'1'0.999872'-18.7028'87.1689'-178.137'195.214'-118.077'31.8534)

; kP = sum_i w_i (w_i G_ii + sum_j>i w_j 2G_ij), row by row in this order
; DHEADR(i) closes the previous row into kP and opens row i; DHEADX(i'j) adds the pair (i,j)
#define DHEADP(N) #
  krad$N = exp(-3.14159265 * kf$N / (kq$N * sr))
  kcos$N = cos(6.28318531 * kf$N / sr)
  ksin$N = sin(6.28318531 * kf$N / sr)
  kRprod      = krad$N * krad$N
  kc2     = 2 * kcos$N * kcos$N - 1
  kd$N   = 0.5 / (1 - kRprod) + 0.5 * (1 - kRprod * kc2) / (1 - 2 * kRprod * kc2 + kRprod * kRprod)
#
#define DHEADR(I) #
kP      = kP + kwr * kS
kwr     = kw$I
kS      = kwr * kd$I
#
#define DHEADX(I'J) #

  kcd     = kcos$I * kcos$J + ksin$I * ksin$J
  kcs     = kcos$I * kcos$J - ksin$I * ksin$J

#
#define DHEADT(I'J) #
kS      = kS + kw$J * kx$I$J
#

kS      = 0
kwr     = 0
