techniques.why: tuned metal bar as a STANDING tone: ideal free-free bar partials (h 2.76/5.4/8.93/13.34), brighter and thinner than a big bell, rung by a continuous noise exciter through a bank of high-Q resonators, so it holds for as long as the key is held. A bar that is struck once and rings down (glockenspiel, celesta, marimba, xylophone) is mallet_bar; a plucked metal tongue (kalimba, mbira, music box) is plucked_tine.
techniques.code:
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes
; A metal bar as a STANDING tone: five free-free beam modes (Euler-Bernoulli ratios) rung by continuous noise while the key is held; Q and weights this entry's own.
; mvmfilter (Mathews & Smith, SMAC 2003), not mode: a retuned mode bursts and grows without bound under a trill.
; Frequency and decay stay k-rate: at a-rate frequency mvmfilter does not ring.
; INPUT / sqrt(ke), ke = E the exact noise gain (kr2 = r^2, kc2 = cos 2theta): one level at every key and both rates.
; kw fades a mode out over 14-15 kHz on its OUTPUT weight: a hard gate clicks under a bend.
; SBARM(ratio'Q'weight): mode at kf1 * ratio, 1/e decay time Q / (pi * f), output weight.
#define SBARM(R'Q'W) #
kf      limit kf1 * $R, 20, 15000
kw      limit (15000 - kf1 * $R) / 1000, 0, 1
kr2     = exp(-6.283185307 * kf / ($Q * sr))
kc2     = cos(12.566370614 * kf / sr)
ke      = 0.5 / (1 - kr2) + 0.5 * (1 - kr2 * kc2) / (1 - 2 * kr2 * kc2 + kr2 * kr2)
am      mvmfilter aex / sqrt(ke), kf, $Q / (3.14159265 * kf)
asum    += am * $W * kw
#
kf1     = kfreq * koct1
; IDLE: 50 ms after the gate falls (the host mutes the voice) the bank is skipped, its ring frozen, once kdef shows mode 1 charged within 2 %: a short first note would freeze a half-built ring.
kidle   init 1
kdef    init 1
kidle   = (kgateraw > 0 ? 0 : kidle + ksmps / sr)
asig    = 0
        if kidle > 0.05 && kdef < 0.02 kgoto SBARIDLE
; Seeded per voice: one constant seed made all voices sum coherently.
aex     rand 0.06, frac(abs(sin(ivoice * 12.9898)) * 43758.5453), 1
asum    = 0
$SBARM(1'900'0.8500)
kdef    = kdef * kr2 ^ ksmps
$SBARM(2.76'1025'0.4497)
$SBARM(5.40'1150'0.2432)
$SBARM(8.93'1275'0.1275)
$SBARM(13.34'1400'0.0615)
; 6.3726 is a level choice.
asig    = asum * 6.3726
SBARIDLE:
asig    = asig * kvol1

heard.hinweis: Neu aufgebaut 2026-11-21: mvmfilter statt mode, Pegelgesetz je Mode exakt. Der Pegel steht über die Tastatur gleich (innerhalb 0,1 dB bis 2,3 kHz, −0,36 dB von 3 bis 4,2 kHz, beide Raten), aber er wandert: fünf rauschgetriebene Moden von nur f/Q Breite (Grundmode 0,06 Hz bei 55 Hz, 2 Hz bei 1760 Hz) geben über 20 s gehaltenen Ton eine 50-ms-Hüllkurve mit 12–17 dB Spanne (Standardabweichung 2,2–3,1 dB, 5–95 % 7–11 dB); das Q ist nicht gesenkt. Über dem obersten Teilton liegt mehr Rauschen als vorher (mvmfilter fällt nur mit 6 dB/Okt: ab dem 1,5-fachen der obersten Mode 14–17 dB mehr; 16–20 kHz bei Taste 110 Hz −50,6 statt −77,6 dB re Gesamtpegel). Eine frische Stimme baut den Ton über tau = Q/(πf) auf (Grundmode 5,2 s bei 55 Hz, 0,65 s bei 440 Hz), eine Stimme, die schon geklungen hat, setzt nach einer Pause auf ihrem stehenden Pegel wieder ein. Ob das Wandern als lebendiges Metall oder als Pumpen wirkt und ob das Rauschen stört, ist am Instrument zu prüfen.

techniques.why: A struck free-free bar, wood or metal, one strike per note left to ring: a marimba, xylophone or glockenspiel bar, no resonator tube, no motor. Modal synthesis: five two-pole resonators (`zdf_2pole`) at measured tuned-bar ratios (Gough, Springer Handbook of Acoustics ch. 15), weighted by the free-free mode shapes at the strike point, damped by Chaigne & Doutaut's law, struck through a one-pole mallet. tuning = how deeply the bar is undercut, material = how long it rings, mallet = hardness, spot = where it is hit. NOT a vibraphone; a plucked metal tongue is plucked_tine, a standing noise-rung bar is struck_bar. Limits: the ring ends when the synth's envelope closes (hold the key or lengthen the release); a re-strike restarts the ring, a bend or legato retunes it; aluminium rings up to 41 s; strikes come out up to 3 dB quieter at the attack (lowest keys, soft mallet, glockenspiel tuning).
techniques.code:
; DECAY: SELF
; LOUDNESS: tuning
; LOUDNESS: material
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes
; mallet bar: modal synthesis of a free-free bar, struck once per note.
; Ratios from measured tuned bars (Gough, Springer Handbook of Acoustics ch. 15, Figs.
; 15.120/15.121 after Fletcher & Rossing): glockenspiel 1:2.71:5.15:8.43:12.21, xylophone
; 1:3:6, marimba 1:3.9:9.23. The log interpolation between them is this entry's own; modes
; 4 and 5 keep the glockenspiel ratios and fade out by tuning .5 (no source gives them for
; an undercut bar).
; Strike weights: Euler-Bernoulli free-free shapes |phi_n(x)|/|phi_n(0)|, the uniform
; bar's at every tuning (own). Damping law alpha = gB/2 + 2 pi^2 (eta/E) f^2 (Chaigne &
; Doutaut, as given by McAdams, Chaigne & Roussarie, JASA 115(3), 2004): rosewood eta/E
; 235 ns (Doutaut & Chaigne 1994, Table I), gB 8/s (McAdams' synthesis setting);
; aluminium gB .33/s, eta/E 8.03 ns, INFERRED from F&R's vibraphone bar without resonator
; (A3 40 s, A5 24 s). Q is fixed at the strike. No resonator, no motor.
; Mallet: a one-pole stand-in for the Hertz contact, its corner a multiple of the key,
; capped at 8 kHz. Observed as the bar's VELOCITY: every mode starts at its crest.
; THE RESONATOR is `zdf_2pole` in bandpass (Csound Opcodes/wpfilters.c, g = tan(pi f/sr)),
; not `mode`: a ringing `mode` that is retuned without a strike (bend, legato, bind)
; bursts, and under a fast pitch modulation grows without bound; this filter keeps its
; state in signal scale. Two terms follow from its recurrence; neither is fitted. Its
; impulse answer is a cosine of amplitude 2g/(1+g^2) = sin(2 pi f/sr), so the input
; factor 0.5/sin(2 pi f/sr) starts every mode at amplitude 1/2 at either rate. Its decay
; rate is (sr/(2Q)) sin(2 pi f/sr), so Q = sr sin(2 pi f/sr) / (gB + 4 pi^2 (eta/E) f^2)
; realises the damping law at either rate.
; The contact delays mode n by atan(f_n/fc) and its own transient keeps the sum under the
; L1 bound inrm normalises to; by how much depends on where the weight sits (up to 3 dB
; under the default strike: lowest keys, soft mallet, glockenspiel tuning). That spread
; of the strike peak is the model's and is not corrected.
; Every knob is read at the strike. A re-strike restarts the ring; a bend or a legato
; key change retunes it.
; Level: G = 3.30 in inrm is a level choice, not part of the model.
kc      = kfreq * koct1
ktun    = 0.5    ; tuning[0.0..1.0]: how deeply the bar is undercut, glockenspiel to xylophone to marimba
kmat    = 0.0    ; material[0.0..1.0]: rosewood to aluminium, how long the bar rings
kmal    = 4.0    ; mallet[1.0..16.0]: mallet hardness, yarn to hard plastic, as the contact corner over the played pitch
kspt    = 0.333  ; spot[0.30..0.50]: where the bar is struck, from near the end towards the middle
kup     timeinsts
        if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
          reinit HIT
        endif
HIT:
itn     limit i(ktun), 0, 1
imt     limit i(kmat), 0, 1
im      limit i(kmal), 1, 16
ix      limit i(kspt), 0.30, 0.50
ikc     = i(kc)
ikc     = (ikc < 20 ? 220 : ikc)
ifc     limit ikc * im, 20, 8000
iamp    = (i(kup) > 0 ? 1 : 0)
acon    mpulse iamp, 0
aex     tone acon, ifc
; damping law, log between rosewood (0) and aluminium (1)
igb     = 8 * (0.33 / 8) ^ imt
ive     = 235e-9 * (8.03e-9 / 235e-9) ^ imt
; tuning: glockenspiel (0) -> xylophone (.5) -> marimba (1), log per mode
ilo     = (itn < 0.5 ? 2 * itn : 1)
ihi     = (itn > 0.5 ? 2 * itn - 1 : 0)
ifd     = (itn < 0.5 ? 1 - 2 * itn : 0)
ir1     = 1
ir2     = 2.71 * (3.00 / 2.71) ^ ilo * (3.90 / 3.00) ^ ihi
ir3     = 5.15 * (6.00 / 5.15) ^ ilo * (9.23 / 6.00) ^ ihi
ir4     = 8.43
ir5     = 12.21
; strike weights, free-free shapes (beta L, sigma) at the spot
ib      = 4.73004 * ix
iw1     = abs(cosh(ib) + cos(ib) - 0.98250 * (sinh(ib) + sin(ib))) / 2
ib      = 7.85320 * ix
iw2     = abs(cosh(ib) + cos(ib) - 1.00078 * (sinh(ib) + sin(ib))) / 2
ib      = 10.99561 * ix
iw3     = abs(cosh(ib) + cos(ib) - 0.99997 * (sinh(ib) + sin(ib))) / 2
ib      = 14.13717 * ix
iw4     = ifd * abs(cosh(ib) + cos(ib) - (sinh(ib) + sin(ib))) / 2
ib      = 17.27876 * ix
iw5     = ifd * abs(cosh(ib) + cos(ib) - (sinh(ib) + sin(ib))) / 2
; per mode: frequency at the strike, Q from the damping law, gate, contact loss
if1     = ikc * ir1
iQ1     = sr * sin(6.28318531 * limit(if1, 20, 16000) / sr) / (igb + 39.4784176 * ive * if1 * if1)
ig1     = (if1 >= 20 && if1 < 16000 ? 1 : 0) / sqrt(1 + (if1 / ifc)^2)
if2     = ikc * ir2
iQ2     = sr * sin(6.28318531 * limit(if2, 20, 16000) / sr) / (igb + 39.4784176 * ive * if2 * if2)
ig2     = (if2 >= 20 && if2 < 16000 ? 1 : 0) / sqrt(1 + (if2 / ifc)^2)
if3     = ikc * ir3
iQ3     = sr * sin(6.28318531 * limit(if3, 20, 16000) / sr) / (igb + 39.4784176 * ive * if3 * if3)
ig3     = (if3 >= 20 && if3 < 16000 ? 1 : 0) / sqrt(1 + (if3 / ifc)^2)
if4     = ikc * ir4
iQ4     = sr * sin(6.28318531 * limit(if4, 20, 16000) / sr) / (igb + 39.4784176 * ive * if4 * if4)
ig4     = (if4 >= 20 && if4 < 16000 ? 1 : 0) / sqrt(1 + (if4 / ifc)^2)
if5     = ikc * ir5
iQ5     = sr * sin(6.28318531 * limit(if5, 20, 16000) / sr) / (igb + 39.4784176 * ive * if5 * if5)
ig5     = (if5 >= 20 && if5 < 16000 ? 1 : 0) / sqrt(1 + (if5 / ifc)^2)
isum    = iw1 * ig1 + iw2 * ig2 + iw3 * ig3 + iw4 * ig4 + iw5 * ig5
; the bank: input factor 0.5/sin(2 pi f/sr), see above; a mode outside 20 Hz..16 kHz
; at the strike is not excited, and one that leaves that band while ringing is muted
kq1     = kc * ir1
kp1     limit kq1, 20, 16000
a1      zdf_2pole aex * (if1 >= 20 && if1 < 16000 ? 1 : 0) * (0.5 / sin(6.28318531 * kp1 / sr)), kp1, iQ1, 2
kq2     = kc * ir2
kp2     limit kq2, 20, 16000
a2      zdf_2pole aex * (if2 >= 20 && if2 < 16000 ? 1 : 0) * (0.5 / sin(6.28318531 * kp2 / sr)), kp2, iQ2, 2
kq3     = kc * ir3
kp3     limit kq3, 20, 16000
a3      zdf_2pole aex * (if3 >= 20 && if3 < 16000 ? 1 : 0) * (0.5 / sin(6.28318531 * kp3 / sr)), kp3, iQ3, 2
kq4     = kc * ir4
kp4     limit kq4, 20, 16000
a4      zdf_2pole aex * (if4 >= 20 && if4 < 16000 ? 1 : 0) * (0.5 / sin(6.28318531 * kp4 / sr)), kp4, iQ4, 2
kq5     = kc * ir5
kp5     limit kq5, 20, 16000
a5      zdf_2pole aex * (if5 >= 20 && if5 < 16000 ? 1 : 0) * (0.5 / sin(6.28318531 * kp5 / sr)), kp5, iQ5, 2
inrm    = 3.30 / (isum > 0 ? isum : 1)
        rireturn
asig    = (a1 * iw1 * (kq1 >= 20 && kq1 < 16000 ? 1 : 0) + a2 * iw2 * (kq2 >= 20 && kq2 < 16000 ? 1 : 0) + a3 * iw3 * (kq3 >= 20 && kq3 < 16000 ? 1 : 0) + a4 * iw4 * (kq4 >= 20 && kq4 < 16000 ? 1 : 0) + a5 * iw5 * (kq5 >= 20 && kq5 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)) * inrm * kvol1

tuning.note: How deeply the bar is undercut: mode ratios 1:2.71:5.15:8.43:12.21 (glockenspiel), 1:3:6 (xylophone), 1:3.9:9.23 (marimba). Read at the strike.

glockenspiel.gloss: plain uniform bar: five inharmonic partials, clangy

xylophone.gloss: second partial a twelfth up: hollow, dry knock

marimba.gloss: second partial near two octaves up: round, mellow

material.note: Damping law from rosewood (0: fundamental T60 1.7 s at 110 Hz, 0.4 s at 1760 Hz) to aluminium (1: 41 s and 10.5 s). High modes always die first. Read at the strike.

rosewood.gloss: dry wooden knock, upper partials gone at once

aluminium.gloss: long metallic ring, partials hang on for seconds

mallet.note: Mallet hardness: the contact's corner as a multiple of the played pitch, capped at 8 kHz. Low strikes only the fundamental, high strikes every mode. Read at the strike.

soft.gloss: yarn mallet: dark thump, mostly the fundamental

medium.gloss: rubber mallet: upper partials present but rounded

hard.gloss: hard plastic or brass: bright click, every partial

spot.note: Strike point as a fraction of the bar's length, from near the end (0.30) to the centre (0.50), where the second and fourth modes have a node and drop out. Read at the strike.

end.gloss: near the end: weak fundamental, second partial leads

centre.gloss: centre: strongest fundamental, second partial gone

heard.hinweis: Neuer Körper, nur gemessen, nicht gehört. Marimba, Xylophon und Glockenspiel benennen reale Instrumente und sind gegen eine Aufnahme zu beurteilen.

techniques.why: A metal tongue clamped at one end, plucked once and left to ring: the tine of a kalimba, mbira or music-box comb. Modal synthesis of a clamped-free bar: two `mvmfilter` modes at the Euler-Bernoulli ratio 1 : 6.27, the overtone weighted by the force it puts into the bridge (derived from the mode shapes). bridge pulls the overtone down to the 5.3x Chapman (2006) measured on a kalimba key with overhang; pluck = thumb to nail; ring = how long it holds. Limits: the bar's 17.5x and 34.4x modes are left out, so no high clang; past the first ping the note is a plain decaying sine (the overtone dies about 6x sooner than the fundamental); a new pluck cuts the ring with a click as loud as the ring; the ring ends when the synth's envelope closes (hold the key or lengthen the release); knobs act at the next pluck. No box, no buzzers, no mbira 14x mode, no lead-weighted music-box teeth.
techniques.code:
; DECAY: SELF
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes
; modal clamped-free bar (Euler-Bernoulli, Rayleigh 1896), modes 1 : 6.2669; mode 2 weighted
; by root shear force, derived (1.3874 = sigma2/sigma1); bridge toward Chapman's 5.30x (2006)
; modes 3, 4 left out: with them the strike peak wandered across the knobs
; mvmfilter, not mode, k-rate args; inside the reinit: each pluck from rest. kup 0 mutes the
; build-time pulse
kc      = kfreq * koct1
kbrg    = 0.5    ; bridge[0.0..1.0]: free cantilever to a tine with an overhang behind the bridge
kplk    = 6.0    ; pluck[1.0..16.0]: release corner as a multiple of the played pitch, thumb to nail
krng    = 0.5    ; ring[0.0..1.0]: how long the tine holds
kup     timeinsts
        if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
          reinit HIT
        endif
HIT:
ib      limit i(kbrg), 0.0, 1.0
ip      limit i(kplk), 1.0, 16.0
irn     limit i(krng), 0.0, 1.0
iqf     = 100 * 8 ^ irn
ikc     = i(kc)
ikc     = (ikc < 20 ? 220 : ikc)
ifc     limit ikc * ip, 20, 8000
iamp    = (i(kup) > 0 ? 1 : 0)
acon    mpulse iamp, 0
aex     tone acon, ifc
ir2     = 6.2669 * (5.30 / 6.2669) ^ ib
iw2     = 1.3874 / sqrt(ir2)
io1     = (ikc < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
io2     = (ikc * ir2 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
isum    = io1 / sqrt(1 + (ikc / ifc) ^ 2) + iw2 * io2 / sqrt(1 + (ikc * ir2 / ifc) ^ 2)
isum    = (isum > 0 ? isum : 1)
; level choice: isum evens the pluck over knobs and keys; 1.67 is its loudness
inrm    = 1.67 / isum
kp1     limit kc, 20, 16000
kp2     limit kc * ir2, 20, 16000
a1      mvmfilter aex, kp1, iqf / (3.14159265 * kp1)
a2      mvmfilter aex, kp2, iqf / (3.14159265 * kp2)
amix    = (a1 * io1 + a2 * iw2 * io2) * inrm
        rireturn
asig    = amix * kvol1

bridge.note: How the tine is held: 0 a free cantilever (overtone at 6.27x), 1 an overhang behind the bridge (overtone at 5.30x, Chapman 2006). Between: interpolated. Above 2.5-3 kHz played the overtone is dropped. Read at the pluck.

cantilever.gloss: music-box tooth: a free tongue, overtone at 6.27x

long key.gloss: overtone at 5.86x, as on Chapman's lowest kalimba key

overhang.gloss: short kalimba key: the overtone pulled down to 5.30x

pluck.note: How sharply the tine is let go: a release corner as a multiple of the played pitch, capped at 8 kHz. Low is the soft flesh of a thumb, high a fingernail snapping off. Read at the pluck.

thumb.gloss: soft release: nearly a pure tone, overtone 17 dB down

fingertip.gloss: the sproing: overtone 7.5 dB under the fundamental

nail.gloss: snapped off a nail: the overtone at its brightest, 5 dB under

ring.note: How long the tine holds: one Q for both modes, 100 to 800, so the fundamental's T60 is 1 to 8 s at 220 Hz and halves each octave up; the overtone dies about 6x sooner. Read at the pluck.

plink.gloss: short: gone in about 1 s at 220 Hz, the overtone a blip

long.gloss: music-box ring: about 8 s at 220 Hz, 2 s at 880 Hz

heard.hinweis: Neuer Körper, nur gemessen, nicht gehört. Kalimba, Mbira und Spieluhr benennen reale Instrumente und sind gegen eine Aufnahme eines solchen zu beurteilen; Kasten, Schnarrer, die hohen Balkenmoden (17,5x, 34,4x) und bleibeschwerte Spieluhrzungen fehlen.

techniques.why: A struck handpan note left to ring: the round steel tone of a hang or pantam, octave and twelfth tuned into the note, a neighbouring octave that swells back and beats after the strike, and the low air resonance of the shell. Modal synthesis on mvmfilter: modes 1:2:3 plus the shell pair 7.50/8.16 (Rossing et al., ISMA 2007), the 85 Hz Helmholtz cavity (Wessel, Morrison & Rossing 2008), decay by register after Alon (2015), struck by a raised-cosine contact pulse. upper = hang or steelpan third mode, hand = palm to fingertip, neighbour = how strongly the octave beats in, cavity = the air hum. Limits: a new strike cuts the ring, a step as large as the ring was; the ring ends when the synth's envelope closes; every knob acts at the next strike; the neighbour is linear and one way, not steelpan coupling; the cavity stays at 85 Hz at every key.
techniques.code:
; DECAY: SELF
; LOUDNESS: hand
; LOUDNESS: cavity
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes
; handpan: modal synthesis of one struck handpan note field.
; Modes 1 : 2 : 3, the third crossfading equal-power to 4 by `upper` (hang to steelpan
; tuning), and the shell pair 7.50 / 8.16 (Rossing et al., ISMA 2007). Cavity: the shell's
; Helmholtz resonance at 85 Hz (Wessel, Morrison & Rossing, POMA 2008), Q 20 this entry's own.
; Neighbour: a second octave mode 4.5 Hz above, driven one way by mode 2, so it rings up after
; the strike (hang note coupling: Rossing et al. 2007 Figs. 9-10; the delayed octave measured
; by Hawley & Morrison, JASA 2021, is a STEELPAN finding). 4.5 Hz sits in the 3.1-8.6 Hz beat
; range Alon (MSc York 2015) measured. Linear and one way: not the steelpan's coupling.
; T60 3.2 s to 220 Hz, 3.0 s at 330-440, 2.5 s from 660, log f between (Alon 2015, per NOTE);
; read here per MODE at its own frequency, INFERRED, so the upper modes fade first.
; Contact: a raised-cosine force pulse (Bilbao, Numerical Sound Synthesis, 2009) of length
; 0.7203 / (hand x key, capped 8 kHz), rounded to whole samples so its area is exactly one.
; Its spectrum sinc(x)/(1-x^2), x = f T, is -3 dB at hand x key; each mode is struck with
; that spectrum at its own frequency, T the rounded length.
; mvmfilter (Mathews & Smith, SMAC 2003): impulse response r^n cos(n th), exact pitch at any
; rate, and its level holds while the key glides. A mode outside 20 Hz..16 kHz at the strike
; is not struck. A new strike CUTS the ring (a one-sample step as large as the ring was at
; that moment) and restarts it; every knob acts at the next strike.
kc      = kfreq * koct1
kupr    = 0.0    ; upper[0.0..1.0]: third mode a twelfth above (hang) to two octaves above (steelpan tuning)
khnd    = 2.0    ; hand[1.0..8.0]: contact corner as a multiple of the played pitch, palm to fingertip
knbr    = 0.4    ; neighbour[0.2..0.6]: how strongly the octave neighbour rings up after the strike
kcav    = 0.5    ; cavity[0.0..1.0]: level of the shell's air resonance, fixed at 85 Hz
kup     timeinsts
        if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
          reinit HIT
        endif
HIT:
iu      limit i(kupr), 0.0, 1.0
ih      limit i(khnd), 1.0, 8.0
inb     limit i(knbr), 0.2, 0.6
icv     limit i(kcav), 0.0, 1.0
ikc     = i(kc)
ikc     = (ikc < 20 ? 220 : ikc)                      ; kfreq is 0 on a never-played voice
ifc     limit ikc * ih, 20, 8000
iNs     = round(0.7203 * sr / ifc)                    ; pulse length in samples: -3 dB at ifc
iNs     = (iNs < 2 ? 2 : iNs)
iT      = iNs / sr
iamp    = (i(kup) > 0 ? 1 : 0)                        ; the build pass is silent
aph     linseg 0, iT, 1
aex     = (1 - cos(2 * $M_PI * aph)) * iamp / iNs     ; unit area, ends at exactly 0
iw3     = cos($M_PI / 2 * iu)
iw4     = sin($M_PI / 2 * iu)
ir[]    fillarray 1, 2, 3, 4, 7.50, 8.16
iw[]    fillarray 1, 1, iw3, iw4, 1, 1
iv[]    init 6
itau[]  init 6
isum    = 0
ii      = 0
while ii < 6 do
  ifq    = ikc * ir[ii]
  iv[ii] = iw[ii] * (ifq >= 20 && ifq < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
  ix     = ifq * iT
  idn    = 1 - ix * ix
  idn    = (abs(idn) < 1e-6 ? 1 : idn)
  ip     = (abs(1 - ix * ix) < 1e-6 ? 0.5 : sin($M_PI * ix) / ($M_PI * ix) / idn)
  isum   += iv[ii] * ip
  il     = log(ifq)
  it60   = (ifq <= 220 ? 3.2 : (ifq < 330 ? 3.2 - 0.2 * (il - log(220)) / log(1.5) : (ifq <= 440 ? 3.0 : (ifq < 660 ? 3.0 - 0.5 * (il - log(440)) / log(1.5) : 2.5))))
  itau[ii] = it60 / log(1000)
  ii     += 1
od
ix      = 85 * iT
idn     = 1 - ix * ix
idn     = (abs(idn) < 1e-6 ? 1 : idn)
igc     = (abs(1 - ix * ix) < 1e-6 ? 0.5 : sin($M_PI * ix) / ($M_PI * ix) / idn)
isum    += icv * igc
; Level: the signed pulse gains sum to isum at the pulse centre; G = 1.690 is a LEVEL choice
; (a default strike at 220 Hz peaks near asig 1.6). The cavity takes its share of that sum,
; so more cavity is less note: declared LOUDNESS. Not a correction of the model.
inrm    = 1.690 / (isum > 0 ? isum : 1)
; Neighbour feed for mvmfilter, derived: B (detuned D = 4.5 Hz, same tau as mode 2) driven by
; mode 2 crests at t* = atan(pi D tau)/(pi D); the feed puts that crest at `neighbour` times
; mode 2's initial amplitude, at every key and both rates.
itb     = itau[1]
idl     = 2 * $M_PI * 4.5 / sr
itp     = taninv($M_PI * 4.5 * itb) / ($M_PI * 4.5)
ifb     = inb * idl / (sin($M_PI * 4.5 * itp) * exp(-itp / itb))
ifb     = ifb * (ikc * 2 + 4.5 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
ktau1   = itau[0]
kl1     limit kc, 20, 0.45 * sr
a1      mvmfilter aex * iv[0], kl1, ktau1
ktau2   = itau[1]
kl2     limit kc * 2, 20, 0.45 * sr
a2      mvmfilter aex * iv[1], kl2, ktau2
ktau3   = itau[2]
kl3     limit kc * 3, 20, 0.45 * sr
a3      mvmfilter aex * iv[2], kl3, ktau3
ktau4   = itau[3]
kl4     limit kc * 4, 20, 0.45 * sr
a4      mvmfilter aex * iv[3], kl4, ktau4
ktau5   = itau[4]
kl5     limit kc * 7.50, 20, 0.45 * sr
a5      mvmfilter aex * iv[4], kl5, ktau5
ktau6   = itau[5]
kl6     limit kc * 8.16, 20, 0.45 * sr
a6      mvmfilter aex * iv[5], kl6, ktau6
klb     limit kc * 2 + 4.5, 20, 0.45 * sr + 4.5       ; keeps its 4.5 Hz when mode 2 sits at its cap
ab      mvmfilter a2 * ifb, klb, ktau2
ktc     = 20 / ($M_PI * 85)                           ; body resonance, FIXED in Hz
acv     mvmfilter aex * icv, 85, ktc                  ; body resonance, FIXED in Hz
amix    = (a1 + a2 + a3 + a4 + a5 + a6 + ab + acv) * inrm
        rireturn
asig    = amix * kvol1

upper.note: Third mode of the note: 0 a twelfth above the fundamental (1:2:3, hang tuning), 1 two octaves above (1:2:4, steelpan tuning), equal-power between. Read at the strike.

hang.gloss: 1:2:3, octave and twelfth: the open, sweet hang note

steelpan.gloss: 1:2:4, octave and double octave: the steelpan's colour

hand.note: Contact: a raised-cosine pulse, -3 dB at this multiple of the played pitch, capped at 8 kHz. 1 strikes fundamental and octave, 8 reaches the shell modes. The strike level moves about 1 dB over it. Read at the strike.

palm.gloss: soft palm or thumb: dark, fundamental and a faint octave

finger.gloss: fingertip tap: fundamental, octave and twelfth

flick.gloss: hard nail flick: the high shell modes ring as well

neighbour.note: A second octave mode 4.5 Hz above, driven by the note's octave: it rings up to this fraction of the octave's strike level at about 0.1 s and beats against it at 4.5 Hz. Linear and one way. Read at the strike.

faint.gloss: a slight shimmer on the octave

beating.gloss: the octave swells back after the strike and beats clearly

cavity.note: The shell's Helmholtz resonance, 85 Hz at every key, T60 0.5 s. It takes its share of the strike: at 1 the steel note's attack is about 3 dB down (more at the top keys), the whole strike about 1 dB. Read at the strike.

none.gloss: no air resonance: the steel note alone

full.gloss: a short low air hum under every strike

heard.hinweis: Neuer Körper, nur gemessen, nicht gehört. Der Name beansprucht ein reales Instrument: gegen eine Aufnahme eines echten Handpans (Hang, Pantam) zu beurteilen. Grenzen: ein neuer Anschlag schneidet den Nachklang ab (ein Sprung so groß wie der Klang in dem Moment); jeder Regler wirkt erst beim nächsten Anschlag; der Nachbar ist linear und einseitig, keine Steelpan-Kopplung; die Luftresonanz bleibt bei jeder Taste auf 85 Hz.

techniques.why: cymbal / crash / ride / splash (a hi-hat or an 808 cymbal is metal_squares): a metal plate held as a STANDING wash -- a dense bank of high-Q resonators, all off the harmonic grid, rung by a continuous noise exciter, so it sounds for as long as the key is held and does not ring down like a struck cymbal; weak fundamental, energy piled into the upper modes (strongest at 6-8x the key).
techniques.code:
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes
; A metal plate as a STANDING wash: nine inharmonic modes rung by continuous noise while the key is held; ratios, Q and weights this entry's own, not a measured cymbal.
; mvmfilter (Mathews & Smith, SMAC 2003), not mode: a retuned mode bursts and grows without bound under a trill.
; Frequency and decay stay k-rate: at a-rate frequency mvmfilter does not ring.
; INPUT / sqrt(ke), ke = E the exact noise gain (kr2 = r^2, kc2 = cos 2theta): one level at every key and both rates.
; kw fades a mode out over 14-15 kHz on its OUTPUT weight: a hard gate clicks under a bend.
; CYMM(ratio'Q'weight): mode at kf1 * ratio, 1/e decay time Q / (pi * f), output weight.
#define CYMM(R'Q'W) #
kf      limit kf1 * $R, 20, 15000
kw      limit (15000 - kf1 * $R) / 1000, 0, 1
kr2     = exp(-6.283185307 * kf / ($Q * sr))
kc2     = cos(12.566370614 * kf / sr)
ke      = 0.5 / (1 - kr2) + 0.5 * (1 - kr2 * kc2) / (1 - 2 * kr2 * kc2 + kr2 * kr2)
am      mvmfilter aex / sqrt(ke), kf, $Q / (3.14159265 * kf)
asum    += am * $W * kw
#
kf1     = kfreq * koct1
; IDLE: 50 ms after the gate falls (the host mutes the voice) the bank is skipped and its ring freezes until the next note.
kidle   init 1
kidle   = (kgateraw > 0 ? 0 : kidle + ksmps / sr)
asig    = 0
        if kidle > 0.05 kgoto CYMIDLE
; Seeded per voice: one constant seed made all voices sum coherently.
aex     rand 0.09, frac(abs(sin(ivoice * 12.9898)) * 43758.5453), 1
asum    = 0
$CYMM(1'260'0.2200)
$CYMM(2.19'285'0.2688)
$CYMM(3.41'310'0.3252)
$CYMM(4.83'335'0.3719)
$CYMM(6.37'360'0.4103)
$CYMM(8.09'385'0.4278)
$CYMM(10.24'410'0.3375)
$CYMM(12.71'435'0.2322)
$CYMM(15.83'460'0.1404)
; 3.5030 is a level choice.
asig    = asum * 3.5030
CYMIDLE:
asig    = asig * kvol1

heard.hinweis: Neu aufgebaut 2026-11-21: mvmfilter statt mode, Pegelgesetz je Mode exakt. Der Pegel steht über die Tastatur gleich, bis die oberen Moden zwischen 14 und 15 kHz ausblenden (bis 880 Hz innerhalb 0,1 dB, bei 1760 Hz −1,5 dB, bei 2349 Hz −4 dB, bei 4186 Hz −7 dB, beide Raten). Er wandert weniger als beim struck_bar: über 20 s gehaltenen Ton hat die 50-ms-Hüllkurve 4–10 dB Spanne (Standardabweichung 0,9–1,6 dB, 5–95 % 3–5 dB), kleiner in hohen Lagen. Über der obersten Mode liegt mehr Rauschen als vorher (mvmfilter fällt nur mit 6 dB/Okt: ab dem 1,5-fachen der obersten Mode 9–14 dB mehr; 16–20 kHz bei Taste 110 Hz −36,7 statt −60,8 dB re Gesamtpegel). Eine frische Stimme baut den Ton über tau = Q/(πf) auf (Grundmode 1,5 s bei 55 Hz, 0,19 s bei 440 Hz); endet die erste Note früher, friert der halb aufgebaute Klang ein und die nächste Note setzt dort an, nicht auf dem stehenden Pegel. Ob das ein Becken ist oder ein stehender Metallklang, ist am Instrument zu prüfen.

techniques.why: TR-808 cymbal and hi-hat after Werner, Abel & Smith, ICMC-SMC 2014: six band-limited Schmitt-trigger squares at the circuit's 205.3/304.4/369.6/522.7/800/540 Hz, duty 0.4798, restarted with their filters on every strike so each hit is the same metal; two band-passes (3440, 7100 Hz) feed three high-passed bands with an envelope each: a long low band, a 7 kHz band with a 30 ms swell, a 40 ms top tick. decay runs from closed hat through open hat to cymbal; tone sets the top tick. It does NOT follow the key: the same metal on every key, never a melodic voice; add a pitched layer with + for a pitch. Linear VCAs (the clipping VCAs are not modelled). No choke between voices; a re-strike on its own voice cuts the ring. It rings only while the synth's voice lives: a long decay needs a long release. Without oversampling the top above 12 kHz is up to 9 dB darker. 1.70 is a level choice.
techniques.code:
kdecay  = 0.40   ; decay[0.0..1.0]: closed hat to long cymbal, one continuum
ktone   = 0.50   ; tone[0..1]: level of the short top band against the two long ones
; DECAY: SELF
; LOUDNESS: decay
; FOLLOWS kfreq: no
; body resonance, FIXED in Hz
; TR-808 cymbal/hat, Werner, Abel & Smith (ICMC-SMC 2014)
kup timeinsts
if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
  reinit MET
endif
MET:
; kup 0: no strike at orchestra build
iamp = (i(kup) > 0 ? 1.0 : 0)
; squares and filters restart per strike at fixed phases: each hit the same metal
a1 vco2 1, 205.3, 2, 0.4798, 0
a2 vco2 1, 304.4, 2, 0.4798, 0.17
a3 vco2 1, 369.6, 2, 0.4798, 0.53
a4 vco2 1, 522.7, 2, 0.4798, 0.71
a5 vco2 1, 800, 2, 0.4798, 0.29
a6 vco2 1, 540, 2, 0.4798, 0.83
; never below 0.15 s: shorter moves the attack peak
idk = 0.15 + i(kdecay)*i(kdecay)*1.85
ae1 expsega 0.001, 0.0003, iamp+0.001, 0.001, iamp+0.001, idk, 0.001, 1, 0.001
ae2 expsega 0.001, 0.03, iamp+0.001, idk*0.5, 0.001, 1, 0.001
ae3 expsega 0.001, 0.0003, iamp+0.001, 0.001, iamp+0.001, 0.04, 0.001, 1, 0.001
amix = a1+a2+a3+a4+a5+a6
ab1 butbp amix, 3440, 1000
ab2 butbp amix, 7100, 1500
; minus the 0.001: silent before and after
ah1 buthp ab1*(ae1-0.001), 3000
ah2 buthp ab2*(ae2-0.001), 5000
ah3 buthp ab2*(ae3-0.001), 9000
rireturn
; level choice: 1.70
asig = (ah1 + ah2 + ah3*1.4*ktone) * 1.70 * kvol1

decay.note: Ring time of the low band, 0.15 s to 2 s on a square law (the 7 kHz band rings half as long): at 0 the hit is gone in about 0.14 s, at 1 it rings about 1.8 s. Read at the strike, so a change applies from the next hit.

closed.gloss: closed hat: the strike and a short metal ring, silent after about 0.14 s

open.gloss: open hat: the metal hangs for under half a second

cymbal.gloss: 808 cymbal: the low metal band rings for nearly two seconds

tone.note: Level of the short top band (above 9 kHz, gone in 40 ms) against the two long bands, from removed (0) to 1.4 (1): the stick's tick in the first 5 ms, about 10 dB above 9 kHz. It leaves the ring as it is.

soft.gloss: the top band removed: the strike without its tick

hard.gloss: the top band's tick pushed to 1.4 of its level

heard.hinweis: Ungehört. Der Vergleich mit einer Aufnahme einer echten TR-808 (Hi-Hat und Becken) steht aus; der Eintrag trägt den Namen dieses Instruments. Prüfbefund eingearbeitet: die Filter starten mit jedem Schlag neu, damit die ersten 2 ms nicht von der Vorgeschichte der Stimme abhängen.

techniques.why: ring modulation / AM at a 2:1 ratio -- carrier f times modulator 2f, so sum and difference land on f and 3f: a hollow ODD-harmonic tone (square-adjacent), with a drifting diode imbalance and carrier leak for the metallic edge
techniques.code:
krmw0   poscil 0.004, 0.091          ; modulator drift, +/-3.5 cents
krlk0   poscil 0.03, 0.037           ; diode imbalance, drifting
acar0   poscil 0.8, (kfreq * koct1)
amod0   poscil 1.0, (kfreq * koct1) * (2.0 + krmw0)
asig    = acar0 * (amod0 * 0.88 + 0.10 + krlk0) * kvol1 ; ring mod + carrier leak

techniques.why: Chebyshev waveshaper -- a fixed transfer table (GEN13) holding odd Chebyshev terms up to the 11th, which map exactly onto odd harmonics: the controlled way to add drive, dirt and distortion colour
techniques.code:
kdrv0   poscil 0.12, 0.074           ; drive wander
kdrb0   poscil 0.05, 0.119           ; second, incommensurate
adrv0   poscil 0.30 + kdrv0 + kdrb0, (kfreq * koct1)
ash0    tablei adrv0, giCheb, 1, 0.5 ; Chebyshev transfer curve
asig    = ash0 * 0.55 * kvol1   ; level-match the family

techniques.why: a sine folded by the Buchla 259 timbre circuit (Esqueda, Pontynen, Valimaki & Parker, DAFx 2017): five parallel cells fold the wave back each time it crosses one of their thresholds, so a plain sine grows odd harmonics whose strongest partial climbs and falls back. The west-coast way: fold a simple wave instead of filtering a rich one (analog_osc and bass_saw filter a saw). fold is NOT a brightness knob: the cells enter at 0.6, 1.8, 3.0, 4.1 and 5.5 V; it is round at 1 V, brightest near 5 V and again near 8 V, dull again at 10. The fold drifts a few percent by itself: the colour moves slowly, the loudness stays put. Odd harmonics like cheby, but many more of them, and moving. At the plugin's rate aliases stay 52 dB down at 1760 Hz, 29 at 4186; at 44100 high keys at a bright fold alias. In the top octave a bright fold grows quieter: its strongest partials lie above hearing.
techniques.code:
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes
; Buchla 259 timbre circuit, Esqueda/Pontynen/Valimaki/Parker DAFx-17 eqs 13-21, with first-order ADAA (Parker/Zavalishin/Le Bivic DAFx-16 eqs 9-10)
; WFOLDM(X): eq 18 over the five cells of eqs 13-17, written as s*x + sum w*a/2*(|x-t| - |x+t|). WFOLDF(X): its antiderivative, F(0) = 0 (DAFx-16 sec. 2.3)
kfold   = 3.5 ; fold[1..10]: peak volts into the cells; NOT a brightness knob: cells enter at 0.6/1.8/3.0/4.1/5.5 V, brightest near 5 and 8 V
#define WFOLDM(X) #-1.673453*($X) - 4.9998*(abs(($X)-0.6) - abs(($X)+0.6)) - 5.233187*(abs(($X)-2.994) - abs(($X)+2.994)) - 3.030991*(abs(($X)-5.46) - abs(($X)+5.46)) + 5.067336*(abs(($X)-1.8) - abs(($X)+1.8)) + 4.859915*(abs(($X)-4.08) - abs(($X)+4.08))#
#define WFOLDF(X) #-41.75083826 - 0.8367265*($X)*($X) - 2.4999*((($X)-0.6)*abs(($X)-0.6) - (($X)+0.6)*abs(($X)+0.6)) - 2.6165935*((($X)-2.994)*abs(($X)-2.994) - (($X)+2.994)*abs(($X)+2.994)) - 1.5154955*((($X)-5.46)*abs(($X)-5.46) - (($X)+5.46)*abs(($X)+5.46)) + 2.533668*((($X)-1.8)*abs(($X)-1.8) - (($X)+1.8)*abs(($X)+1.8)) + 2.4299575*((($X)-4.08)*abs(($X)-4.08) - (($X)+4.08)*abs(($X)+4.08))#
; level law, built once for all voices: 1/rms of one period of the cells through the keyed one-pole, for 0..12.75 V. Input scaling, not a meter: fold alone moves the level 5.6 dB
giWfold ftgenonce 0, 0, 256, -2, 0
if tab_i(255, giWfold) == 0 then
itn     = tan(3.14159265 * 1326.29 / 110 / 256)
ii      = 1
while ii < 256 do
iz      = 0
ivp     = 0
iss     = 0
ip      = 0
while ip < 256 do
ix      = ii * 0.05 * sin(6.283185307 * ip / 256)
iv      = $WFOLDM(ix)
iz      = (itn * (iv + ivp) - (itn - 1) * iz) / (1 + itn)
ivp     = iv
iss     = iss + (ip < 128 ? 0 : iz * iz)
ip      += 1
od
tabw_i  1 / sqrt(iss), ii, giWfold
ii      += 1
od
tabw_i  tab_i(1, giWfold), 0, giWfold
endif
; fold drifts +-8 % at 0.07 Hz from the note-on, this entry's own: the fold is not monotonic, so the colour travels, not the level
kfd     = kfold * (1 + 0.08 * sin(6.283185307 * 0.07 * knote))
kcps    = kfreq * koct1
knrm    tablei kfd * 20, giWfold
afx     poscil kfd, kcps
ax0     delay1 afx
aF1     = $WFOLDF(afx)
aF0     delay1 aF1
adx     = afx - ax0
amid    = (afx + ax0) * 0.5
aym     = $WFOLDM(amid)

fold.note: peak volts into the cells. Not monotonic: the strongest partial runs #1, #3, #5, #7, #9, #11 up to 5 V, is #1 again over 5.4-7.6, #5 near 8, #3 from 8.3. The level holds, but in the top octave a bright fold is quieter.

round.gloss: lightly folded: the 3rd harmonic 5 dB under the fundamental, seven partials

brightest.gloss: the strongest partial is the 11th: the brightest fold

second fold.gloss: bright again after a darker stretch at 5.5-7 V

dull.gloss: past the bright folds: round, the 3rd strongest

heard.hinweis: Neuer Körper, nur gemessen, nicht gehört. fold ist nicht monoton: rund bei 1 V, am hellsten bei etwa 5 und 8 V, bei 10 V wieder dumpf. Die Faltung driftet ab dem Notenbeginn um +-8 % mit 0,07 Hz: die Farbe wandert, der Pegel bleibt (-7,1 dB rms bei jedem fold-Wert, beide Raten). Bei 176400 (Plugin-Rate) liegt das Aliasing bei 1760 Hz mindestens 52 dB unter dem stärksten hörbaren Teilton, bei 4186 Hz mindestens 29 dB; bei 44100 aliasen hohe Lagen mit heller Faltung deutlich (bis -9 dB bei 1760 Hz). Der Ausgangs-Tiefpass folgt der Taste, statt wie in der Schaltung fest bei 1326 Hz zu liegen. In der obersten Oktave wird eine helle Faltung leiser, weil ihre stärksten Teiltöne über 20 kHz liegen (4186 Hz, fold 5: -25,5 dB unter 20 kHz statt -7,1 dB).

techniques.why: pipe / drawbar organ -- tonewheel and church organ: three ranks at typical registration, an 8' principal, a 4' octave and a 5 1/3' quint, each its own gbuzz stack, each drifting at its own rate
techniques.code:
kw80    poscil 0.00035, 0.061        ; rank 8' tuning wander
kw40    poscil 0.00045, 0.083        ; rank 4', incommensurate
kwq0    poscil 0.00030, 0.107        ; quint rank, incommensurate
a80     gbuzz 0.46, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kw80), 6, 1, 0.72, giCos ; 8' principal
a40     gbuzz 0.24, (kfreq * koct1) * 2.0023 * (1 + kw40), 4, 1, 0.66, giCos ; 4' octave, +4 cents
aq0     gbuzz 0.16, (kfreq * koct1) * 1.4987 * (1 + kwq0), 3, 1, 0.60, giCos ; 5 1/3' quint, -1.5 cents
asig    = (a80 + a40 + aq0) * kvol1

techniques.why: clarinet / chalumeau / bass clarinet -- a cylindrical single-reed bore, on the physical model this build ships for exactly that: Csound's `wgclar`, Perry Cook's clarinet in Smith's digital-waveguide formulation (Cook, ICMC 1992; Smith, 'Physical Modeling using Digital Waveguides', CMJ 16(4), 1992). The odd-only series is not an approximation here, it is what a cylinder closed at the reed produces. Replaces an `foscili` pair at modulator ratio 2 that stood in for it: that had 0.00% of its energy above 2 kHz and no even partials at all (-140 dB), a clean odd stack with no air in it whatever, and it carried no knob the player could reach.
techniques.code:
; LOUDNESS: blow
; `blow` is the blowing PRESSURE on this reed and pressure carries level with it --
; a clarinet blown harder is louder, which is the physics and not an invented
; envelope. Every number here is measured at 176400, the rate the plugin compiles
; Csound at, and read after decimation to 44100; a bare-44100 reading of this model
; is a different instrument (same body, centroid 340 Hz there against 1235 Hz here).
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes -- 0 to -11 cents from 55 Hz to 880 Hz, rms flat within 0.21 dB
; across that span, so the chalumeau and the bass register are this same body played
; low. STANDS: it is driven and holds as long as the note does.
; `kngain` IS NOT BREATH NOISE, whatever its name and the manual suggest. BJ heard it
; first and the split confirms it: over this axis the INHARMONIC share moves 0.15% ->
; 0.31% while the HARMONIC energy above 2 kHz goes 2.96% -> 24.81%. What it does is
; feed the reed nonlinearity, which redistributes the odd series upward -- at the low
; end the partials fall away smoothly (3rd..15th: -9.6 -14.1 -16.9 -19.0 -20.8 -22.5
; -24.1 dB), at the high end the upper ones carry the tone (-6.3 -19.7 -9.5 -2.5
; -29.2 -4.9 -12.6). Real noise appears only past `kngain` 0.6, and there the rms has
; collapsed to 0.061 because the model has left self-oscillation. So there is no
; breath in this bore to reach for; a breath layer would have to be MIXED IN, which
; this instrument is entitled to do (BJ 2026-08-05: "das ist ein synth, also kann man
; rauschen zumischen lassen, auch im rezept") and which v1.0 does not yet do.
; THE TWO AXES ARE COUPLED IN THE MODEL and the ranges are picked so each still
; travels on its own. Below `kngain` 0.20 nothing at all comes up, and the pressure
; at which the reed opens falls as `kngain` rises: kamp 0.83 at kngain 0.25, 0.70 at
; 0.35, 0.45 at 0.50.
; THE MOVEMENT IS THE BREATH, not a wobble laid on the pitch: a slow unsteadiness in
; the blowing pressure, which is what a player's breath does. It is small (0.02 of
; the pressure) and it stays inside the turbulent regime at every position of both
; knobs, because crossing that boundary inside a note is what an earlier, wider
; version did and it cost 58 dB of loudness travel in one note.
; NO ATTACK IS WRITTEN HERE and none can be. `wgclar`'s own `iatt` is dead in this
; host: one instance per voice is started at engine build and never restarted, so a
; note only unmutes a bore that is already standing -- measured with a preroll, 0.99
; of full level 5 ms after the gate opens, and IDENTICAL for a pressure ramp of
; 0.02 s and one of 0.24 s. A ramp changes only where the bore settles afterwards
; (hysteresis), which is a side effect and not an onset. The player's envelope owns
; the attack.
kovertone = 0.55   ; overtone [0.00..1.00]: how far up the reed is worked -- from a hollow chalumeau on its lowest partials to a bright reedy tone standing on its upper ones
kblow   = 0.55   ; blow [0.00..1.00]: how hard the reed is blown -- the pressure on the bore, soft and pure to driven and turbulent
kng     = 0.30 + 0.20 * kovertone                ; 0.50 is the ceiling: past it the model leaves
                                             ; self-oscillation entirely (rms 0.062 at 0.7).
                                             ; 0.30 is the dry end -- below 0.20 no pressure
                                             ; whatever brings breath out of the bore.
kwander oscili 0.02, 0.23, giSine            ; a player's breath is never quite steady
kpr     = 0.55 + 0.35 * kblow + kwander               ; started below the turbulent boundary a note stays
                                             ; dull for its whole length (hysteresis, measured:
                                             ; floor 0.35 -> 2.9% above 2 kHz where floor 0.45 ->
                                             ; 18.0% at the same target), so the range begins above it.
asig    wgclar kpr, kfreq * koct1, -0.3, 0.1, 0.1, kng, 5.735, 0, giSine, 30
                                             ; the -0.3 is `kstiff`, INERT in this build (output
                                             ; bit-identical -0.9 to 0.0 at both rates), so it sits at
                                             ; the documented value and never moves. kvamp is 0: no
                                             ; built-in vibrato. ONE wgclar and no more -- a second
                                             ; instance changes this one, 3rd partial -5.9 -> -14.1 dB.
asig    = asig * 1.30 * kvol1

heard.hinweis: Der Regler hieß bei der Abnahme `air`. BJs Befund im selben Atemzug -- "Air ist nicht air, sondern oberton" -- ist nachgemessen und trifft zu: über die Achse bewegt sich der inharmonische Anteil nur 0.15% -> 0.31%, während die HARMONISCHE Energie über 2 kHz von 2.96% auf 24.81% steigt. Er heißt deshalb seit derselben Sitzung `overtone`; kein Sample hat sich dabei geändert. OFFEN für v1.1: eine zugemischte Rauschschicht als echter Atem, von BJ im selben Satz erlaubt ("das ist ein synth, also kann man rauschn zumischen lassen, auch im rezept").

overtone.note: how far up the reed is worked -- `kngain` over 0.30..0.50. NOT breath noise, whatever the argument's name suggests: measured at 176400 and read after decimation to 44100, the inharmonic share moves only 0.15% -> 0.31% across this axis while the harmonic energy above 2 kHz goes 2.96% -> 24.81%. It feeds the reed nonlinearity and the odd series redistributes upward -- 3rd to 15th partial -9.6 -14.1 -16.9 -19.0 -20.8 -22.5 -24.1 dB at the low end against -6.3 -19.7 -9.5 -2.5 -29.2 -4.9 -12.6 at the high one, so it is a change of which partials carry the tone and not a tilt. 0.50 is a hard ceiling: real noise only appears past 0.6 and by then the model has left self-oscillation (rms 0.061 at 0.7). COUPLED TO `blow`: the pressure at which the reed opens falls as this rises -- kamp 0.83 at kngain 0.25, 0.70 at 0.35, 0.45 at 0.50.

hollow.gloss: the chalumeau, standing on its lowest partials

open.gloss: the upper odd partials coming up under the tone

reedy.gloss: bright, the tone carried by its upper partials

blow.note: how hard the reed is blown -- `kamp` over 0.50..0.90, which on this model is the blowing PRESSURE and not an output level. Measured at 176400 and read after decimation to 44100, at the authored `air`: the rms rises 0.21 -> 0.47 (7.2 dB) while the energy above 2 kHz goes 2.9% -> 35.3% and the centroid 446 -> 2046 Hz, so colour travels with the level rather than instead of it -- declared `; LOUDNESS: blow`, because a clarinet blown harder IS louder. Do not read the older 44100 figures for this argument: at a bare 44100 it shows a threshold at 0.76 that does not exist at the rate the plugin runs. The range stops at 0.90 because the model keeps rising past it with nothing new in the tone, and starts at 0.50 because a note begun below the turbulent boundary stays dull for its whole length (hysteresis, measured: floor 0.35 -> 2.9% above 2 kHz where floor 0.45 -> 18.0%, same target pressure).

soft.gloss: pure and contained, the reed barely worked

spoken.gloss: the normal weight of the tone

driven.gloss: pushed until the reed turns turbulent

; `blow` is the blowing PRESSURE on this reed and pressure carries level with it --
; a clarinet blown harder is louder, which is the physics and not an invented
; envelope. Every number here is measured at 176400, the rate the plugin compiles
; Csound at, and read after decimation to 44100; a bare-44100 reading of this model
; is a different instrument (same body, centroid 340 Hz there against 1235 Hz here).
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes -- 0 to -11 cents from 55 Hz to 880 Hz, rms flat within 0.21 dB
; across that span, so the chalumeau and the bass register are this same body played
; low. STANDS: it is driven and holds as long as the note does.
; `kngain` IS NOT BREATH NOISE, whatever its name and the manual suggest. BJ heard it
; first and the split confirms it: over this axis the INHARMONIC share moves 0.15% ->
; 0.31% while the HARMONIC energy above 2 kHz goes 2.96% -> 24.81%. What it does is
; feed the reed nonlinearity, which redistributes the odd series upward -- at the low
; end the partials fall away smoothly (3rd..15th: -9.6 -14.1 -16.9 -19.0 -20.8 -22.5
; -24.1 dB), at the high end the upper ones carry the tone (-6.3 -19.7 -9.5 -2.5
; -29.2 -4.9 -12.6). Real noise appears only past `kngain` 0.6, and there the rms has
; collapsed to 0.061 because the model has left self-oscillation. So there is no
; breath in this bore to reach for; a breath layer would have to be MIXED IN, which
; this instrument is entitled to do (BJ 2026-08-05: "das ist ein synth, also kann man
; rauschen zumischen lassen, auch im rezept") and which v1.0 does not yet do.
; THE TWO AXES ARE COUPLED IN THE MODEL and the ranges are picked so each still
; travels on its own. Below `kngain` 0.20 nothing at all comes up, and the pressure
; at which the reed opens falls as `kngain` rises: kamp 0.83 at kngain 0.25, 0.70 at
; 0.35, 0.45 at 0.50.
; THE MOVEMENT IS THE BREATH, not a wobble laid on the pitch: a slow unsteadiness in
; the blowing pressure, which is what a player's breath does. It is small (0.02 of
; the pressure) and it stays inside the turbulent regime at every position of both
; knobs, because crossing that boundary inside a note is what an earlier, wider
; version did and it cost 58 dB of loudness travel in one note.
; NO ATTACK IS WRITTEN HERE and none can be. `wgclar`'s own `iatt` is dead in this
; host: one instance per voice is started at engine build and never restarted, so a
; note only unmutes a bore that is already standing -- measured with a preroll, 0.99
; of full level 5 ms after the gate opens, and IDENTICAL for a pressure ramp of
; 0.02 s and one of 0.24 s. A ramp changes only where the bore settles afterwards
; (hysteresis), which is a side effect and not an onset. The player's envelope owns
; the attack.
kovertone = 0.55   ; overtone [0.00..1.00]: how far up the reed is worked -- from a hollow chalumeau on its lowest partials to a bright reedy tone standing on its upper ones
kblow   = 0.00   ; blow [0.00..1.00]: how hard the reed is blown -- the pressure on the bore, soft and pure to driven and turbulent
kng     = 0.30 + 0.20 * kovertone                ; 0.50 is the ceiling: past it the model leaves
                                             ; self-oscillation entirely (rms 0.062 at 0.7).
                                             ; 0.30 is the dry end -- below 0.20 no pressure
                                             ; whatever brings breath out of the bore.
kwander oscili 0.02, 0.23, giSine            ; a player's breath is never quite steady
kpr     = 0.55 + 0.35 * kblow + kwander               ; started below the turbulent boundary a note stays
                                             ; dull for its whole length (hysteresis, measured:
                                             ; floor 0.35 -> 2.9% above 2 kHz where floor 0.45 ->
                                             ; 18.0% at the same target), so the range begins above it.
asig    wgclar kpr, kfreq * koct1, -0.3, 0.1, 0.1, kng, 5.735, 0, giSine, 30
                                             ; the -0.3 is `kstiff`, INERT in this build (output
                                             ; bit-identical -0.9 to 0.0 at both rates), so it sits at
                                             ; the documented value and never moves. kvamp is 0: no
                                             ; built-in vibrato. ONE wgclar and no more -- a second
                                             ; instance changes this one, 3rd partial -5.9 -> -14.1 dB.
asig    = asig * 1.30 * kvol1

techniques.why: flute / recorder / piccolo / whistle / pan flute -- a blown air column: a hollow four-harmonic stack whose rolloff breathes on a three-second pressure cycle, with an octave layer beating against its own second harmonic; the blown character, not a physical bore model
techniques.code:
kbr0    poscil 0.5, 0.31             ; breath-pressure cycle, ~3 s
kfm0    = 0.24 + 0.16 * kbr0      ; pressure opens the harmonics
abd0    gbuzz 0.34, (kfreq * koct1), 4, 1, kfm0, giCos ; blown harmonic stack
kwo0    poscil 0.0009, 0.077         ; air-column wander, own rate
aoc0    poscil 0.05, (kfreq * koct1) * 2 * (1 + kwo0)  ; octave, beats with the body's 2nd
asig    = (abd0 + aoc0) * kvol1

techniques.why: brass -- trumpet / french horn / trombone / tuba / brass section: a twelve-harmonic stack whose rolloff opens once from dark to bright over the attack and then holds, voiced through a fixed 1200 Hz bell formant
techniques.code:
kop0    = 1 - exp(-knote * 2.2)       ; attack opens the series ONCE
kbm0    = 0.30 + kop0 * 0.42       ; dark at onset -> bright, then holds
klw0    poscil 0.0006, 0.083         ; lip instability, own rate
abz0    gbuzz 0.5, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + klw0), 12, 1, kbm0, giCos ; lip + bore
abl0    reson abz0, 1200, 900, 1   ; bell formant, FIXED in Hz
asig    = (abz0 * 0.95 + abl0 * 0.40) * kvol1

techniques.why: bowed string SECTION -- orchestral strings, a string ensemble, massed players (a single bowed instrument is `string`): three players sounding together, each with its own slow intonation drift and its own bow-pressure cycle, detuned against each other; a bright saw-family spectrum with a gentle harmonic-count breathing
mandatory_flags: ensemble/detune is a voice-level effect, not a cycle property
techniques.code:
krm0    = min(sr * 0.47, 20000) / (kfreq * koct1)        ; harmonics that fit
kctr0   limit krm0 * 0.62, 1.6, 7 ; corner centre, capped
ksd0x0  poscil 0.0009, 0.061         ; player 1 intonation
ksb0x0  poscil 0.35, 0.089           ; player 1 bow pressure
asr0x0  vco2 0.30, (kfreq * koct1) * 1.0000 * (1 + ksd0x0), 0
kbc0x0  limit (kfreq * koct1) * kctr0 * (1 + 0.7 * ksb0x0), 50, min(sr * 0.47, 20000) ; bow sharpens the corner
ase0x0  tone asr0x0, kbc0x0
ksd0x1  poscil 0.0009, 0.073         ; player 2 intonation
ksb0x1  poscil 0.35, 0.107           ; player 2 bow pressure
asr0x1  vco2 0.30, (kfreq * koct1) * 1.0042 * (1 + ksd0x1), 0
kbc0x1  limit (kfreq * koct1) * kctr0 * (1 + 0.7 * ksb0x1), 50, min(sr * 0.47, 20000) ; bow sharpens the corner
ase0x1  tone asr0x1, kbc0x1
ksd0x2  poscil 0.0009, 0.047         ; player 3 intonation
ksb0x2  poscil 0.35, 0.127           ; player 3 bow pressure
asr0x2  vco2 0.30, (kfreq * koct1) * 0.9958 * (1 + ksd0x2), 0
kbc0x2  limit (kfreq * koct1) * kctr0 * (1 + 0.7 * ksb0x2), 50, min(sr * 0.47, 20000) ; bow sharpens the corner
ase0x2  tone asr0x2, kbc0x2

techniques.why: plucked string / guitar / harp / koto / pizzicato (a violin or cello PLUCKED): ONE real string, set going and then left to ring -- NOT the ensemble string machine (that is `strings`, detuned saws) and NOT the plucked-string spectrum without the pluck (that is `harpsichord`, gbuzz choirs). The string is a comb resonator tuned to the played pitch. It has to be fed the whole time so a held note stands and the synth's own envelope does the striking -- but the feed arrives as scattered, time-smeared touches and the ring is kept long, so what is heard is the string and not what is driving it. A continuous wall of noise into the same resonator is audibly an electric string driver: aggressive and restless. Its top dies away after the attack the way a real string loses its brilliance -- twice over, fast for the first instant and slowly for the whole ring. IF THE PROMPT WANTS A PLUCK THAT IS ALLOWED TO DIE -- struck once and left to ring down under the key -- this entry cannot do it, because it is fed the whole time on purpose; `plucked_wire` is the one, a real Karplus-Strong wire with nothing driving it after the pluck. Choose between them from what the prompt asks for. bow = plucked with a pick to drawn with a bow, pick = where the string is set going, from right at the bridge to at the middle, damp = left ringing to stopped under the hand A STRING DRAWN WITH A BOW -- violin, viola, cello, bass, arco -- is `bowed_string`: a real bow on a waveguide string. This entry's `bow` axis only thickens the dust that drives the resonator, and BJ never took it.
techniques.code:
kdamp   = 0.00   ; damp [0.00..1.00]: the flat of the hand on the string, from left ringing to stopped
kpick   = 0.185  ; pick [0.10..0.50]: where along the string it is set going, as a fraction of its length
kstr    limit kfreq * koct1, 20, 12000
kfast   = exp(-knote * 20.00)                  ; the first instant's brilliance goes at once
kslow   = exp(-knote * 0.328)                  ; and the string keeps losing its top all the while
kbrth   poscil 0.120, 1.900                ; the hand behind it is never quite steady
kcut    limit 775.0 * (1 + 2.58 * kfast) * (1 + 4.06 * kslow) * (1 + kbrth) * (1 - 0.85 * kdamp), 60, 18000
aexd    dust 1.0, 736.2                        ; the drive arrives as separate touches, not as
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.1100, 0.00710                ;   a wall of noise -- a wall is an electric
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0820, 0.00470                ;   string driver, not a played string. Each
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0640, 0.00310                ;   touch is then smeared out in time so none
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0480, 0.00190                ;   of them arrives as a click. Allpasses
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0340, 0.00113                ;   spread WITHOUT darkening; a lowpass here
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0260, 0.00079                ;   buries the instrument's own colour
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0200, 0.00053
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0160, 0.00037
aexb    tone aexd, kcut
apik    vdelay aexb, (kpick / kstr) * 1000, 60
aexc    = aexb - apik
astr    streson aexc, kstr, 0.9884
aref    poscil 0.35, 400                          ; a fixed-loudness yardstick: how scattered the
abal    balance astr, aref                        ; drive is must not change how loud the tone is
asig    = abal * 0.85

bow.note: how the string is set going, and that is the whole difference between a guitar and a cello. A pick or a fingernail lets go in an instant, so everything in the string is woken at once and the sound arrives bright and then falls away. A bow never lets go: the hair grabs and slips and grabs again, feeding the string the whole time, so the top is rubbed off but nothing dies -- the tone stands and breathes instead. In the code this is how DENSELY the drive arrives: separate touches at the plucked end, a steady draw at the bowed one. Measured across the axis the colour travels from 4812 Hz down to 3463 Hz while how sharply the string rings does not change (34.3 -> 33.6 dB) and the loudness moves 0.04 dB.

plucked.gloss: picked and let go: bright at the front, then darkening

bowed.gloss: drawn with a bow: standing, breathing, the top rubbed off

pick.note: where along the string it is set going, as a fraction of its length. Not a tone control -- geometry: the body subtracts a copy of the drive delayed by `pick` of a period, so the harmonic whose node falls on that spot cannot be given any energy and is simply missing. That harmonic is 1/pick, so the axis is a NOTCH WALKING DOWN through the harmonics as it rises, and it bites hardest where 1/pick lands on one. Measured at 220 Hz, how far that harmonic sits below its neighbours: 0.10 takes 39 dB out of the 10th, 0.125 36 dB out of the 8th, 0.167 34 dB out of the 6th, 0.20 41 dB out of the 5th, 0.25 46 dB out of the 4th, 0.333 42 dB out of the 3rd, and 0.50 cancels EVERY even harmonic at once (44 dB, odd-to-even 44.1 dB) -- the hollow, woody one. BETWEEN those positions the notch falls between two harmonics and does much less: at the shipped default 0.185 the null sits at 5.4, BETWEEN two harmonics, so no harmonic is cancelled at all -- the fifth reads 1.8 to 10.0 dB below its neighbours depending on register (the comb's closed form 2|sin(pi n beta)| gives 6.6 dB; the spread is the broadband drive scattering the partial readings, not the axis), against the 34 to 46 dB above where the null lands ON one. That is why that one setting sounds like no setting at all. The default is 0.185 because that is what the entry has always played; if the sound wants its pluck position HEARD, start it at 0.25, 0.333 or 0.50. Loudness across the whole axis and four registers: 0.035 dB.

wiry.gloss: close to the bridge: the tenth harmonic cancelled, thin and hard

hollow.gloss: a quarter along: the fourth harmonic gone, 46 dB down

middle.gloss: over the middle: EVERY even harmonic gone at once, hollow and woody -- a clarinet made of string

damp.note: how freely the string is allowed to ring, as with the flat of the hand laid on it. Damping a string is a FREQUENCY-DEPENDENT loss and nothing else: the hand takes the highs first and the low partials keep going, which is why a muted string reads as dull rather than as quiet. In a digital string that loss is the loop filter (Jaffe & Smith, CMJ 7(2) 1983). `streson` exposes no loop filter, so THIS AXIS IS NOT ONE: it is the cutoff of the `tone` standing in FRONT of the resonator, scaled by `1 - 0.85 * kdamp`, and the difference is measurable and must be known before choosing a setting. A loop filter applies its loss once per round trip, so the loss compounds; a one-pole on the drive applies it once, and once its cutoff is below the played fundamental the RATIO between partial n and partial 1 stops changing. The axis therefore SATURATES, and how much of it is left depends on the register. Centroid travel over the whole axis, measured at the 4x the LRO runs: 1.55 octaves at 55 Hz, 1.58 at 110, 1.38 at 220, 1.05 at 440, 0.48 at 880 and 0.26 at 1760 (at 44100 it is 1.29 / 1.20 / 0.91 / 0.65 / 0.41 / 0.21). USE IT BELOW ABOUT 440 Hz. Above C5 it is worth less than this entry's own `bow`, which BJ heard as barely audible at 0.77 octaves. It is also back-loaded: at 220 Hz the four quarters give 0.18 / 0.25 / 0.36 / 0.59 octaves, so the last quarter is over 40 % of the whole travel and the `damped` anchor at 0.5 sits at less than a third of it. SECOND EFFECT, declare it rather than discover it: the scaling multiplies the whole `kcut` product, note envelopes included, so damping also softens this body's attack colour instead of sharpening it the way a real loop filter would -- the ratio of the first 50 ms centroid to the sustained one falls from 3.73x to 2.19x at 880 Hz and 2.87x to 1.87x at 440. `streson`'s own feedback is NOT touched and must not be: it is one flat gain for every partial, so lowering it does not damp anything -- it removes the resonance and leaves the broadband drive, which the closing `balance` then amplifies. That is what this axis used to do, and it is worth writing down because a comb-contrast meter certified it: balance had to apply 3.7x at 0 and 15.8x at 1, and the centroid ROSE 3099 -> 4924 Hz. Brighter and noisier, i.e. the opposite. Loudness over the whole damp x pick grid at six registers and both rates: 0.09 dB; true peaks 0.65 to 1.05 against the host's 2.523. THE SHIPPED STRING IS THE OPEN ONE, so the default is 0 and the axis only ever damps.

open.gloss: left to ring: the full top of the string, a clear singing note

damped.gloss: a hand resting on it: the top rolled off, the note dulls but is still a note -- and this is under a third of the travel, not half of it

muted.gloss: palm-muted: dark and dull in the low and middle registers, the highs gone and the low partials still ringing. Above C5 the axis has little left to take

techniques.why: a string DRAWN WITH A BOW -- violin, viola, cello, double bass, anything arco: a real bow on a real string, not a resonator fed with noise. The head's `t5bow` is a waveguide string in velocity waves with the bow's friction curve at the contact point (Smith, ICMC 1986; McIntyre, Schumacher & Woodhouse, JASA 1983): the hair sticks to the string and slips off it once per period, and that stick-slip IS the tone -- it stands as long as the bow is drawn, it is periodic, and nothing in it is noise. The string loses its top at the bridge through a one-pole whose cutoff is in Hz, so it is the same instrument at 44100 and at the 4x the plugin runs (which `wgbow`, the only other bow in this Csound, is not: its loss filter is relative to the sample rate and at 4x it is 1.6-1.9 octaves too bright). What radiates goes through a BOX: the violin's four signature body modes and the bridge hill as `mode` filters, scaled by `box` down to a cello. A bow ARM moves weight and speed over the note -- the hair bites at the start and lets go, and keeps drifting afterwards -- all of it in the arm, none of it on the pitch. NOT `string`, whose `bow` axis only thickens the `dust` that drives a comb resonator (that entry is the PLUCKED string: guitar, harp, pizzicato), and NOT `strings`, the ensemble machine of detuned saws. Cost: about 1.9 % of one core per voice at 4x against 0.8 % for `string`; sixteen always-on voices are roughly a third of a core. place = where along the string the bow is drawn, gut = the string itself from dark gut to bright steel, box = the size of the body from cello to violin
techniques.code:
; A BOWED STRING -- a bow on a string, the arm that draws it, and the box it is mounted on.

place.note: where along the string the bow is drawn, as a fraction of its length from the bridge. Geometry, not a tone control: the bow splits the string into two delay lines and the harmonic whose node sits under the hair is starved, so the colour is a COMB walking through the partials, and what moves most is the character of the stick-slip, not the brightness. Measured at 220 Hz, 4x: centroid 2409 Hz at 0.10, 2308 at 0.13, 2465 at 0.16, 2582 at 0.20 (273 Hz of travel), comb contrast 59 -> 55 dB, loudness 0.01 dB. THE RANGE IS WHERE THE BOW HOLDS THE FUNDAMENTAL: at the fixed weight the string falls into double-period motion from about 0.22 outward (a sub-octave 10-17 dB under the note at 110-440 Hz, measured 0.24 and 0.25), and nearer the bridge than 0.10 the bow catches the octave or the twelfth above about 880 Hz, as a real bow does below Schelleng's minimum force. Inside 0.10..0.20 the sub-harmonic stays below -50 dB at every tested pitch 55-1760 Hz and both rates. The bridge-side line can be no shorter than two sub-blocks plus one sample, so above kplace * sr / (2 * iK + 1) -- about kplace * 14700 Hz at 44100 and kplace * 19600 Hz at 4x, 1.9 and 2.5 kHz at the default -- the bow walks toward the middle by itself, and above about 6 kHz the pitch is wrong.

ponticello.gloss: close to the bridge: glassy and thin, the hair biting hard

normale.gloss: the ordinary place, an eighth of the string: full and even

tasto.gloss: over the end of the fingerboard: softer, rounder, the top held back

gut.note: the string itself: how much of its top it loses at the bridge on every round trip. This IS a loop filter -- the one-pole at the bridge (Jaffe & Smith, CMJ 7(2) 1983) with its cutoff in Hz, 1400 Hz at 0 rising to 8400 Hz at 1 (4100 at the default), so it compounds once per period and the string darkens the way a real one does, and it is the same string at 44100 and at the plugin's 4x. Measured at 220 Hz, 4x: centroid 1748 Hz at 0, 1841 at 0.3, 2308 at 0.6, 3076 at 1 (1329 Hz of travel); at 880 Hz 4023 -> 5570 Hz; loudness 0.01 dB; comb contrast unchanged (58-59 dB). TWO THINGS TO KNOW. First, a string cannot be darker than its own third partial, or the bow has nothing left to grip: the cutoff is floored at 3 x the played pitch, so above about 440 Hz the dark end saturates (at 880 Hz, 0 and 0.3 read the same). Second, darkness pulls the pitch: the darker the string, the more the Helmholtz corner is smeared at the bridge and the earlier the hair catches it, so the note sits SHARP -- at 440 Hz +6 cents at 0, +3 at 0.3, +2 at 0.6, +1 at 1; at 880 Hz +14 at 0, +6 at 0.6, +3 at 1. Declared, not tuned out: it is the model's own behaviour and a fitted correction would be a number laid over it.

gut.gloss: a gut string: dark, warm, the top gone -- for the low and middle registers

wound.gloss: a wound string: the ordinary singing string, clear but not wiry

steel.gloss: bare steel: bright and wiry, every partial present

box.note: the size of the body the string is mounted on. The box is a bank of five `mode` filters at the violin's signature frequencies -- A0 272 Hz (the air through the f-holes), CBR 407, B1- 462, B1+ 551 and the bridge hill around 2300 Hz (J. Woodhouse, Euphonics 5.3) -- and `box` scales all five together: at 1.0 a violin, at 0.37 the modes land where a cello's do (A0 100 Hz, B1 171/204 Hz, hill 850 Hz), at 1.2 a small fiddle. The Q values (18/20/25/25/4) are not in the source and are this entry's, by ear. The bank is held against the string with `balance`, so the box is a filter and never a fader: loudness 0.01 dB over the range. Measured at 220 Hz, 4x: centroid 2978 Hz at 0.37 (the cello body sits BELOW a 220 Hz note and leaves it bright), 2252 at 0.7, 2308 at 1.0, 2164 at 1.2 (813 Hz of travel), comb contrast 52-59 dB. Around 880-1100 Hz the hill lifts the second and third partial 4-7 dB above the fundamental, as a violin's body does at A5; at 0.37 that region moves down to about 330-410 Hz.

cello.gloss: a cello's box: the air at 100 Hz, the wood at 170-200 Hz, the hill at 850

viola.gloss: a viola's box, between the two

violin.gloss: a violin's box: A0 272, B1 462/551, the hill at 2.3 kHz

techniques.why: a wire under tension, plucked once and then left alone: the note is made by the pluck and nothing feeds it afterwards, so it rings and dies the way a real wire does -- long and singing at the bottom of the keyboard, a short bright tick at the top. This is NOT `string`, which is a comb resonator fed the whole time so that a held note stands; it is the other thing, an actual travelling wave in a wire, and it fades by itself. Karplus-Strong with the Jaffe-Smith extensions (David A. Jaffe and Julius O. Smith, 'Extensions of the Karplus-Strong Plucked-String Algorithm', Computer Music Journal 7(2), 1983), as Csound's `wgpluck2` implements it: two delay rails with a one-pole reflection filter standing in for the bridge. THREE THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE REACHING FOR IT. (1) IT TAKES THE KEY AT THE START OF THE NOTE AND THEN HOLDS IT. `wgpluck2` reads its frequency at i-rate, so the `reinit` on `ktrig` in the code is what makes it play the note at all -- and glide, pitch bend, vibrato and everything else on the pitch bus do not reach it once the note has begun. A legato slide leaves the wire at the pitch it was plucked at. A note that has to bend needs a pitch-following body beside it via `+`. (2) IT DECAYS, and how fast depends steeply on the pitch. Measured at the oscillator's default 4x oversampling, time to fall 20 dB: at refl 0.70 a note at 110 and 220 Hz has still not dropped 20 dB after 25 seconds, 440 Hz takes 4.4 s and 880 Hz 0.54 s; at refl 0.85 that is 8.5 s at 220, 1.05 s at 440 and 0.14 s at 880. So a long held note in the top octave will have gone silent by itself while the key is still down. That is the wire, not a fault -- but it is why this entry does not answer a prompt that asks for a sustained tone. The ring length also follows the LRO's oversampling setting, and steeply: at 1x that same 440 Hz note is down in 0.18 s where 4x gives 2.3 s. The model grows its delay line by whole periods until it holds at least 512 samples and rescales the reflection to match, so a shorter line -- a lower rate or a higher note -- ends up with a lossier bridge. It cannot be undone from outside: unwinding that rescaling would need a reflection below zero, which the model does not accept. Every figure here is at the default. (3) IT PLAYS SLIGHTLY FLAT, more so the higher the note and the higher refl. The bridge filter's pole is refl itself, so raising it adds delay to the loop, and the loop's length is the pitch; the delay line is also truncated to whole samples, which bites harder the shorter it is. Across the axis at the default 4x: within 4 cents at 110 and 220 Hz, within 18 at 440, up to 44 cents flat at 880 and up to 95 at 1760. Since 2026-11-20 the size is derived from the model's own source (`Opcodes/repluck.c`) and no longer only measured: with N0 = floor(sr/f) the model runs s = ceil(512/N0) steps per sample around a loop of D = 2*floor(s*N0/2) - 2 steps, its reflection rescaled to r' = 1 - (1 - refl)/s, and the bridge adds a phase delay of atan2(r' sin w, 1 - r' cos w)/w steps at w = 2*pi*f/(s*sr); the period is (D + that delay)/s samples. That form meets the rendered pitch within half a cent from 110 to 1760 Hz at all three anchors, so the flatness is a property of the model, stated here and not corrected, and it is why the axis stops at 0.85. MOVING refl WHILE A NOTE RINGS BENDS THAT NOTE: the bridge's delay follows the knob while the wire's length was fixed at the pluck -- 14 cents at 440 Hz, 28 at 880 and 51 at 1760 across the whole axis. ABOVE THE AXIS IS COLOUR, NOT A NOTE. refl 0.90 to 0.98 is a different thing altogether: at 0.98 the sound is gone in 0.17 s at 220 Hz and sits 91 cents flat there, 172 cents at 440. What is left is a crackle, a small dry transient. Worth having -- layered under a pitched body with `+`, never asked to carry the pitch. THE PICKUP POINT IS THE SECOND AXIS. `pick` is where along the wire the sound is heard, and it is real geometry: a harmonic whose still point falls on that spot is simply missing. At 220 Hz, read over the first half-second because the note is already dying after that, the second harmonic runs from -7.0 dB below the fundamental at 0.25 to -11.0 at 0.35, and the third drops into a 68 dB hole at 0.33 -- wiry, then reedy, then round. It moves the LEVEL as well, and the body declares that instead of hiding it (`; LOUDNESS: pick`): across the axis the peak falls 1.25 dB while the note's settled energy RISES 1.75, in opposite directions, and the peak moves by the same amount at every register (-1.24 to -1.25 dB from 55 to 1760 Hz). What travels is the distance between them -- the peak sits 9.7 dB above the settled level at 0.25 and 6.7 dB at 0.35 -- because the wave is spiky near the end of the wire and smooth further along. That is a pluck being a transient, not a volume control, and it is the case §4 stopped judging by threshold on 2026-07-27. Both figures are `lco_measure`'s own peak and rms at the oscillator's default 4x. THE AXIS STOPS AT 0.35 FOR MOVEMENT, NOT FOR LOUDNESS. Raising the pickup damps the colour's travel over the note (46 Hz at 0.25, 20 at 0.35, 16 at 0.37), and at 0.37 combined with the shortest ring (refl 0.85) the body stands still outright when the LRO is run at 1x oversampling. 0.35 is the last point that still moves at every refl and every oversampling setting. Beyond it: at 0.50 the colour stands still at 55, 110 and 220 Hz, and past 0.50 nothing is new -- that is the middle of the wire and everything beyond mirrors what came before, 0.80 measuring within 3 dB of 0.20 over the first six partials. The middle itself, 0.50, kills the even harmonics outright (second harmonic 43 dB down at the attack) and stands still: a striking sound, and a deliberate one -- set it by hand, outside the axis. TWO NOTES ON THE CODE. There is deliberately NO `dcblock`: `wgpluck2` produces no DC worth blocking here (0.05 % of rms at worst), while `dcblock2`'s corner scales with the sample rate, so at the oscillator's 4x it becomes an ~800 Hz highpass that takes 23 dB out of a note at 110 Hz -- it destroys exactly the low end this body is good at. And `PLUCKWIRE:` is a LABEL, which cannot be indexed the way this library's variable names are: a second copy of this body in the same instrument must be given a different label. IF THE PROMPT WANTS A PLUCKED SOUND THAT STANDS while the key is held, this is the wrong entry and `string` is the right one -- same family, fed continuously, so a held note does not die. Choose between them from what the prompt asks for. refl = how long it rings.

refl.note: how long the wire rings on after the pluck. Low is the long one: at 0.70 a note below about 300 Hz simply does not stop inside the note, and 440 Hz takes 4.4 s to fall 20 dB; at 0.85 that same 440 Hz is down in 1.05 s and 880 Hz in 0.14 s. So the axis runs from a wire left ringing to a short dry pluck, and it shortens much faster the higher you play. It also detunes: the note goes flat as the axis rises, measured +3.2 down to -4.0 cents at 220 Hz across the window and -4.0 to -18.2 at 440. Turned while a note rings it bends that note by the same amount, because the wire's length was fixed at the pluck. That is what stops the axis at 0.85 rather than at 0.98, where the model still runs but the pitch is no longer the played one -- that region is a crackle, not a note, and the entry text says how to use it. The two loudness meters disagree on this axis and the difference IS the parameter: the attack does not move at all (peak spread 0.0 dB at 110, 220 and 440 Hz), while the note's total energy falls -- 0.5 dB at 110 Hz, 2.9 at 220, 6.1 at 440 -- because a shorter ring simply holds less of it. It is not a fader; it is the ring length being what it says.

ringing.gloss: left to ring: below 300 Hz it never stops inside the note

plucked.gloss: an ordinary pluck, ringing but clearly dying

dry.gloss: short and dry, and already a few cents flat

pick.note: where along the wire the sound is picked up, as a fraction of its length. A harmonic with a node at that point is cancelled, so the axis runs wiry (near the end, all harmonics present and the second only 7 dB down at the attack) through hollow (0.33, where the third harmonic falls into a 68 dB hole) to round. It is a TIMBRE axis that also moves the level, declared as such in the body: from 0.25 to 0.35 the peak falls 1.25 dB while the four-second energy rises 1.75, so neither meter alone is 'the loudness' -- what moves is the distance between them, 9.7 dB down to 6.7. The axis ends at 0.35 because the colour's travel over the note thins out as the pickup rises (46 Hz at 0.25, 20 at 0.35) and at 0.37 with the shortest ring the body stops moving altogether at 1x oversampling; past 0.50 the wire mirrors itself.

wiry.gloss: near the end of the wire: spiky, all harmonics, hard attack

hollow.gloss: the third harmonic cancelled -- reedy, a little nasal

round.gloss: smoother and softer-edged, the last point that still moves at every refl

techniques.why: synth bass: a dark sawtooth with a sine one octave below it, the plain starting point of a bass patch. One band-limited saw through Csound's 2-pole Butterworth lowpass (butterlp, no resonance), corner near the 24th harmonic; the corner travels half an octave up and down once every 5 s, restarting with each note, so a held note's colour breathes. No ladder and no resonance: there is no squelch or self-oscillation in this body, so for an acid line pair it with the synth's own filter, envelope and glide. Limit: from about 880 Hz up the corner sits at the 15 kHz cap and the colour stands still. For a pure sub use sub_sine, for a wide detuned saw supersaw, for one bare waveform with shape controls analog_osc.
techniques.code:
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes
; subtractive: vco2 saw through butterlp (2-pole Butterworth, no resonance), sine octave below
ivph0   = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; per-voice phase
; drift keyed to knote: every note starts at the same point (a free LFO would not)
kvdr0   = 0.0007 * sin(6.283185307 * (0.043 + 0.0037 * ivoice) * knote + 6.283185307 * ivph0)
abs0    vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kvdr0), 0
kmv0    = 2 ^ (0.5 * sin(6.283185307 * 0.2 * knote))
kcut0   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 24 * kmv0, 100, 15000
; corner smoothed at audio rate in log frequency: butterlp is direct form II, and a step in
; its corner (every retrigger) clicks
alc0    tone a(log(kcut0 / 100)), 50
acut0   = 100 * exp(alc0)
adk0    butterlp abs0, acut0
asb0    oscili 0.30, (kfreq * koct1) * 0.5
asig    = (adk0 * 0.72 + asb0) * kvol1

techniques.why: supersaw / hypersaw -- the trance and rave lead, and the JP-8000's string pads. Seven sawtooth oscillators, one of them the played note and six standing off it. This is a DIGITAL oscillator and that is the whole reason it is its own entry: the saws are deliberately not band limited, so they alias, and Szabo names that fold-back as one of the four things every other emulation misses -- it is what makes the sound airy. Built from Adam Szabo, `How to Emulate the Super Saw`, BSc thesis, KTH Stockholm 2010 (TRITA-CSC-E 2010:131), which measured a Roland JP-8000 and JP-8080: the detune offsets (table 1), the 11th degree detune curve (fig 7), the two mix curves (fig 11), the pitch-tracking high pass on the first harmonic (fig 14/15) and the free-running random phases (fig 18-21). `detune` and `mix` are the machine's own two knobs.

kmix    = 0.75    ; mix [0..1]: the six against the centre; they are equal at 0.75

kpoly   = 10028.7312891634                     ;   is NOT proportional. An 11th degree fit
kpoly   = kpoly * kknob - 50818.8652045924     ;   through 17 measured points, by Horner --
kpoly   = kpoly * kknob + 111363.4808729368    ;   nearly flat to 0.5, steep after 0.9, so
kpoly   = kpoly * kknob - 138150.6761080548    ;   most of the knob is fine tuning and only
kpoly   = kpoly * kknob + 106649.6679158292    ;   the top of it spreads wide
