kspread limit kpoly * kknob + 0.0030115596, 0, 1

kf0     = kfreq * koct1                        ; Szabo 2010 table 1: the offsets are not
kfa     = kf0 * (1 - 0.11002313 * kspread)     ;   symmetric and not evenly spaced; the
kfb     = kf0 * (1 - 0.06288439 * kspread)     ;   centre saw is never detuned at all
kfc     = kf0 * (1 - 0.01952356 * kspread)
kfd     = kf0 * (1 + 0.01991221 * kspread)
kfe     = kf0 * (1 + 0.06216538 * kspread)
kff     = kf0 * (1 + 0.10745242 * kspread)

ipa     = rnd(1)                               ; free running: a voice draws its phases once,
ipb     = rnd(1)                               ;   when it starts, and no note resets them, so
ipc     = rnd(1)                               ;   no two notes meet the same waveform. Szabo 2010 fig 18-21:
ipd     = rnd(1)                               ;   resetting them to a fixed phase makes the
ipe     = rnd(1)                               ;   attacks flange identically every time,
ipf     = rnd(1)                               ;   and modulating them adds artefacts
ipg     = rnd(1)

aa      phasor kfa, ipa                        ; plain ramps, NOT band limited. The fold-back
ab      phasor kfb, ipb                        ;   above Nyquist is the "airiness" the study
ac      phasor kfc, ipc                        ;   names as one of the four things other
ad      phasor kf0, ipd                        ;   emulations miss -- this is a digital
ae      phasor kfd, ipe                        ;   oscillator and it is meant to alias
af      phasor kfe, ipf
ag      phasor kff, ipg

kctr    = -0.55366 * kmix + 0.99785            ; Szabo 2010 fig 11: turning the mix up pulls
kside   = -0.73764 * kmix * kmix + 1.2841 * kmix + 0.044372

                                               ;   the maximum the manual claims
aside   = (aa + ab + ac + ae + af + ag) * 2 - 6
actr    = ad * 2 - 1
amix    = (aside * kside + actr * kctr) * 0.47
                                               ; one amplitude for all seven, as the machine

                                               ; declared: six saws add incoherently where one

                                               ;   The axis is not a fader -- it moves the
                                               ;   centroid 345 Hz and the beating from 2.0 to

                                               ;   0.75 you hear seven against each other

detune.note: how far the six side saws stand off the centre one. The knob is not proportional: Szabo fitted an 11th degree polynomial through 17 measured settings, and it stays nearly flat to 0.5, steepens, then rises drastically after 0.9. So most of the travel is fine tuning -- measured on the outermost saw at 220 Hz: +0.6 cents at 0, +8.7 at 0.25, +18.1 at 0.5, +44.5 at 0.75, +176.7 at 1.0. The offsets are not symmetric and the centre saw is never detuned at all. The beating between the seven is the movement of this body: 2.3 dB at 0, 9.5 dB at 0.5.

tight.gloss: all seven on the note; one thick saw, barely moving

classic.gloss: +18 cents on the outer saw -- the pad and string spread

wide.gloss: +177 cents, close to a chord; the screaming lead end

mix.note: the six side saws against the centre one. Turning it up pulls the centre saw DOWN in a straight line while the six come up in a parabola; they meet at 0.75, not at the maximum the JP-8000 manual claims. Both curves are Szabo's fits to the measured amplitudes. Level follows: 3.8 dB from 0 to 0.75, because six saws add incoherently where one does not.

centred.gloss: the six are almost silent -- a single aliasing saw

even.gloss: all seven at the same level, where they were measured to meet

hollow.gloss: the centre pulled under the six; the note itself recedes

heard.hinweis: kein Beleg für eine Abnahme durch BJ gefunden. NICHT als abgenommen behandeln und nicht aus Herkunft, Commit-Text oder „ear-approved“ in docs/ erschließen — genau das war der Fehler (2026-07-30).
heard.massstab: Abgenommen ist ein Instrument erst über eine HTML-Abhörseite, auf der die PARAMETERKOMBINATION sichtbar und von BJ wählbar ist — nicht über einen Ordner mit vorgerenderten Dateien. techniques.why: hard sync / oscillator sync -- the classic tearing sync lead: a slave saw restarted by the master every cycle, its ratio sweeping 1.5x..3.7x
mandatory_flags: true hard sync is not yet a supported kind; approximated with FM
techniques.code:
ivph0   = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; per-voice phase
kvdr0   poscil 0.0007, 0.043 + 0.0037 * ivoice, giSine, ivph0
kswp0   oscili 1.1, 0.16            ; slave-ratio sweep
krat0   = 2.6 + kswp0            ; 1.5 .. 3.7 x master
azro0   = 0
amst0, asyn0  syncphasor (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kvdr0), azro0
aslv0, adum0  syncphasor (kfreq * koct1) * krat0, asyn0
asig    = (aslv0 * 2 - 1) * 0.45 * kvol1 ; hard-synced saw

techniques.why: A single resonant peak riding on a saw-like or triangle-like body, the Casio CZ's resonance without a filter. Method: a cosine read at r times the period's own phase, restarting every period and multiplied by a window that falls to zero at the period's end, after US 4,658,691 (Ishibashi, Casio, figs. 17-23). dcw = where the peak sits, harmonic 1.6 to 8.6; window = saw window to triangle window. The peak drifts by 0.6 harmonic over 14 s from each note-on. One rms at every setting: dcw is colour, not level. NOT `sync`: no restart step, no tearing edge. At the saw window it is close to a saw through a resonant lowpass, but the peak is a harmonic number, follows the key and never rings; name `analog_osc` and the synth's filter for a sweep in Hz. Limit: the peak is held at or below 18 kHz, so high keys lose the top of dcw (flat from 0.66 at 2637 Hz, from 0.3 at 4186 Hz).
techniques.code:
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes
kdcw    = 0.30 ; dcw[0..1]: where the resonant peak sits, harmonic 1.6 to 8.6 (the CZ DCW)
kwin    = 0.0  ; window[0..1]: window peak position, saw window to triangle window
; The Casio CZ resonant wave after US 4,658,691 (Ishibashi, Casio), FIGS. 17-23: a cosine
; read at r times the period's own address, so it starts over every period, multiplied
; by a window that is zero where the period ends. The patent's FIG. 19 is the same read
; without the window and jumps at every restart; the window's zero is what removes the
; jump, so nothing here needs band-limiting machinery to be continuous.
kdrf0   = 0.6 * sin(6.283185307 * 0.071 * knote)
kr0     = max(1.6, min(1.6 + 7 * kdcw, 18000 / (kfreq * koct1) - 0.6)) + kdrf0
                                      ; the peak is held at or below 18 kHz at any rate, so
                                      ;   a high key loses the top of dcw; never below the
                                      ;   mapping's own floor 1.6 (r stays >= 1). The drift
                                      ;   is added AFTER both: a clamp around it would stop
                                      ;   it there
ks0     = 0.002 + 0.498 * kwin        ; 0 would divide by zero below; 0.002 is still a saw
kL0     = 1 - ks0
; Level from the wave's own mathematics, not a meter. With p uniform over one period and
; x = w(p)(1-cos(a p))/2, w the triangle rising to 1 at s and falling to 0 at 1:
;   mean = (1/2 - H(a))/2,  E[x^2] = (1/2 - 2 G(a) + G(2a)/2)/4,
;   H(b) = integral of w cos(b p),  G(b) = integral of w^2 cos(b p),
; each integral split at s and closed by parts (q = 1-p on the falling side). The terms
; cancel to ~1e-4 at s = 0.002; in this double-precision Csound the result stays within
; 3e-12 of a numeric integral over r 1..9.2 and s 0.002..0.5.
kb1     = 6.283185307 * kr0
kb2     = 2 * kb1
kg1     = ((ks0*ks0/kb1)*sin(kb1*ks0) + (2*ks0/(kb1*kb1))*cos(kb1*ks0) - (2/(kb1*kb1*kb1))*sin(kb1*ks0)) / (ks0*ks0)
kc1     = (kL0*kL0/kb1)*sin(kb1*kL0) + (2*kL0/(kb1*kb1))*cos(kb1*kL0) - (2/(kb1*kb1*kb1))*sin(kb1*kL0)
ksn1    = -(kL0*kL0/kb1)*cos(kb1*kL0) + (2*kL0/(kb1*kb1))*sin(kb1*kL0) + (2/(kb1*kb1*kb1))*cos(kb1*kL0) - 2/(kb1*kb1*kb1)
kG1     = kg1 + (cos(kb1)*kc1 + sin(kb1)*ksn1) / (kL0*kL0)
kg2     = ((ks0*ks0/kb2)*sin(kb2*ks0) + (2*ks0/(kb2*kb2))*cos(kb2*ks0) - (2/(kb2*kb2*kb2))*sin(kb2*ks0)) / (ks0*ks0)
kc2     = (kL0*kL0/kb2)*sin(kb2*kL0) + (2*kL0/(kb2*kb2))*cos(kb2*kL0) - (2/(kb2*kb2*kb2))*sin(kb2*kL0)
ksn2    = -(kL0*kL0/kb2)*cos(kb2*kL0) + (2*kL0/(kb2*kb2))*sin(kb2*kL0) + (2/(kb2*kb2*kb2))*cos(kb2*kL0) - 2/(kb2*kb2*kb2)
kG2     = kg2 + (cos(kb2)*kc2 + sin(kb2)*ksn2) / (kL0*kL0)
kh1     = ((ks0/kb1)*sin(kb1*ks0) + (cos(kb1*ks0) - 1)/(kb1*kb1)) / ks0
khc     = (kL0/kb1)*sin(kb1*kL0) + (cos(kb1*kL0) - 1)/(kb1*kb1)
khs     = -(kL0/kb1)*cos(kb1*kL0) + sin(kb1*kL0)/(kb1*kb1)
kH1     = kh1 + (cos(kb1)*khc + sin(kb1)*khs) / kL0
kmu0    = 0.5 * (0.5 - kH1)
kvar0   = 0.25 * (0.5 - 2*kG1 + 0.5*kG2) - kmu0*kmu0
kgn0    = 0.177 / sqrt(kvar0)         ; rms 0.177 at every dcw/window: the peak then stays
                                      ;   near 0.5, the hottest corner at about 0.53
kdc0    = kmu0 * kgn0                 ; the mean the body takes out, in output units
aph0    phasor min(kfreq * koct1, 0.49 * sr)  ; phasor takes 1 off its phase at most once a
                                              ;   sample: at sr or above it never wraps and the
                                              ;   table read runs away, which kfreq times a live
                                              ;   octave switch can reach; below sr/2 also keeps
                                              ;   the top note from folding down
; r, s and the gain are taken only where a period restarts, where the windowed wave is 0
; whatever they are. Taken mid-period, a step in r is a step in the wave: a fresh strike on
; a sounding voice resets the drift (r jumps up to 0.6) and the knobs arrive once per host
; block, and both read as a broadband burst. The mean taken out is NOT 0 there (-mean*gain
; is -0.16..-0.23), so it is not switched at the restart but travels from its old to its
; new value across the new period: continuous at both ends, the period's mean off by half
; the change for that one period.
kon0    init 1
adl0    delay1 aph0
adf0    = adl0 - aph0                 ; positive only on the sample where the phase wrapped
atk0    = 0.5 * (adf0 + abs(adf0)) + kon0     ; kon0: the voice's first k-period takes its
                                              ;   values at once, not a period late
akr0    upsamp kr0                    ; upsamp, not a(): a() ramps from the previous k
aks0    upsamp ks0                    ;   value, and the four must come from ONE k-cycle,
akg0    upsamp kgn0                   ;   or the mean and gain belong to another r
akd0    upsamp kdc0
ar0     samphold akr0, atk0
as0     samphold aks0, atk0
agn0    samphold akg0, atk0
adn0    samphold akd0, atk0           ; the mean this period travels to
adp0    delay1 adn0                   ; on the wrap sample: the mean before it changed
ado0    samphold adp0 + kon0 * (adn0 - adp0), atk0    ; the mean it travels from; a voice's
                                              ;   first period has none before it: its own
kon0    = 0
acs0    tablei aph0 * ar0, giCos, 1, 0, 1     ; wrap mode: the address restarts with the period
awn0    = min(aph0 / as0, (1 - aph0) / (1 - as0))
asig    = (awn0 * (1 - acs0) * 0.5 * agn0 - (ado0 + (adn0 - ado0) * aph0)) * kvol1
                                      ; the RAISED cosine is 0 where the window rises, so
                                      ;   the windowed wave has no step even under the saw
                                      ;   window's near-vertical rise; the mean is taken out
                                      ;   exactly, not by a filter

dcw.note: where the resonant peak sits, harmonic 1.6 (0) to 8.6 (1): the CZ's DCW. The rms is the same at every setting, so it moves colour, not level. Held at or below 18 kHz: from a 1.96 kHz key up the top of the travel is flat.

dark.gloss: resonance between harmonic 1 and 2.2: near a sine, H2 at -2 to -20 dB over the drift

nasal.gloss: peak on the 4th harmonic: a narrow band over a soft body

resonant.gloss: peak on the 8th harmonic, high above the fundamental

window.note: the window under the resonance: a falling saw (0, the CZ's saw resonance) to a symmetric triangle (1, its triangle resonance). Toward 1 the even harmonics off the peak drop out; the fundamental comes 0.5-2 dB closer.

saw.gloss: saw window: every harmonic present under the peak

triangle.gloss: triangle window: even harmonics off the peak drop out, by amounts moving with the drift

heard.hinweis: Neu gebaut 2026-11-20, nur gemessen: Gate PASS bei 44100 und 176400 (Lautheitsspreizung 0,0 dB, rms -15,04 dB an allen Ecken), Tonhoehe 0,0 Cent bei 55-1760 Hz, Neuanschlag und Knopfstufen ohne Knack (gemessen bei dcw 0,3/Fenster 0 und dcw 0,05/Fenster 1). Nach der Verifikation geändert: die Resonanzspitze bleibt bei 18 kHz gedeckelt, hohe Tasten verlieren das obere Ende von dcw.

techniques.why: A living wave that never repeats: one cycle of breakpoints whose heights take a small random step at every repetition, so the overtones drift on and on while the pitch stays the key's; grainy at the rough end. Method: Xenakis' dynamic stochastic synthesis (Formalized Music, rev. 1992, ch. XIII-XIV; Luque, LMJ 19, 2009) on Csound's gendy, Cauchy walks between mirror barriers. rough = the step (drift speed, grain), points = breakpoints per cycle (few round, many bright), wander = the period walks too. Which partial leads is the walk's: in over half of all seconds 2f or 3f is stronger than f, in a tenth by over 10 dB (an octave or twelfth up); fewer points steady it. Each voice keeps ONE continuing walk; a note picks it up where the last left it. NOT noise, NOT a granular cloud (it stays a harmonic tone); NOT a fixed harmonic stack (name additive) or a detuned analog wave (name analog_osc).
techniques.code:
; Xenakis (Formalized Music, 1992) and Luque (2009), on Csound's gendy
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes
krough  = 0.05 ; rough[0.01..0.15]: amplitude step of every breakpoint per cycle, drifting to grainy
kpts    = 10   ; points[6..24]: breakpoints per cycle, few round, many bright
kwand   = 0    ; wander[0..0.05]: segment-frequency spread, the period itself walks
kf0     = kfreq * koct1
ksc0    = min(krough * sqrt(220 / kf0), 0.15)
; gendy.c breaks above f*points = sr: held to 22050 Hz, the same at every rate
kpn     = min(kpts, 22050 / (kf0 * (1 + kwand)))
; per-voice seed, or the voices walk the same increments
iseed   = 1 + int(random:i(0, 2147483640))
        seed iseed
; never restart the walk at a note: a fresh walk jumps the level
agd0    gendy 0.5, 1, 1, 0.5, 0.5, kf0 * (1 - kwand), kf0 * (1 + kwand), ksc0, 0.3, 24, kpn
; the walk's DC
agd0    atone agd0, 5
; keep balance2's default half-power point (slower: the rms wanders; faster: bass ripple)
aref0   poscil 0.3, kf0
asig    balance2 agd0, aref0
asig    = asig * kvol1

rough.note: Each breakpoint's step per cycle, scaled by sqrt(220/f) so the drift per second is even across the keys. Change per cycle at 220 Hz: 1.2 % at 0.01, 3.6 % at 0.05, 9.5 % at 0.15. At 55 Hz no change above 0.075.

liquid.gloss: 1.6 % change per cycle, colour sways 1.1x in 3 s: a slow, smooth glide

restless.gloss: 3.6 % per cycle, colour swings 1.3x in 3 s: a tone plainly alive

grainy.gloss: 7 % per cycle, colour swings 1.5x in 3 s: a rough, grainy surface

points.note: Breakpoints per cycle, whole numbers (10.7 plays as 10); a step changes the wave at once, without a click. Centroid at 220 Hz 1.8 f at 6, 2.5 f at 10, 5.2 f at 24. Fewer are used where f x points would pass 22050 Hz.

round.gloss: centroid 1.8 f, f leads over half the time: the roundest, most pitched

buzzy.gloss: centroid 5.2 f, energy spread up to h4 and beyond: bright and buzzy

wander.note: Spread of the segment frequencies around the key, so the period walks as well. At 0 the period is exactly the key's. At 0.05 the pitch strays 8 cents on average, up to 15 (37 at the wildest corner).

pitched.gloss: the period is exactly the key's: only the overtones move

drifting.gloss: pitch strays about 1.5 cents, up to 4: a faint life in the pitch

unstable.gloss: pitch strays about 8 cents, up to 15: an unsteady, wobbly tone

heard.hinweis: Neu gebaut 2026-11-20: Xenakis' dynamische stochastische Synthese auf gendy, Knöpfe rough/points/wander. Jede Stimme führt EINEN fortlaufenden Walk, kein Neustart pro Note (der Neustart gab Einsätze 3.6 dB über und 5.4 dB unter dem gehaltenen Pegel; jetzt +1.0/-0.7). Gemessen: Gate PASS bei 44100 und 176400, Periode = Taste (höchstens 0.7 Cent), Pegel über balance2 gehalten, 16 Stimmen unkorreliert (max |r| 0.85). Welcher Teilton führt, wandert mit dem Walk: 2f oder 3f liegt in 51-61 % der Sekunden über f.

techniques.why: harpsichord / cembalo / spinet / virginal -- a plucked keyboard: two bright gbuzz choirs, an 8' and a 4' a hair sharp, drifting against each other; the plucked-string spectrum without the pluck (a string that is plucked and dies away is `plucked_wire`; the fed one that stands is `string`)
mandatory_flags: pluck transient/decay is not modeled; only the sustained spectral character is approximated
techniques.code:
khw80   poscil 0.00040, 0.071        ; 8' choir tuning drift
khw40   poscil 0.00055, 0.094        ; 4' choir, incommensurate
ah80    gbuzz 0.56, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + khw80), 9, 1, 0.80, giCos ; 8' choir, bright
ah40    gbuzz 0.24, (kfreq * koct1) * 2.0031 * (1 + khw40), 6, 1, 0.72, giCos ; 4' choir
asig    = (ah80 + ah40) * kvol1

techniques.why: a sung vowel: five formants, each a stream of decaying sine grains fired once per period (FOF, the CHANT method, Rodet 1984), with the sung-vowel formant table of the Csound manual (Appendix D). The key sets the grain rate, the formants stay fixed in Hz, so a vowel keeps its identity across the keyboard until the harmonics grow too sparse to draw it (above about 1.5 kHz). Above F1 the first formant is raised to the fundamental, as sopranos do (Sundberg). A vowel, not a singer: no text, no vibrato, no breath, no choir. The vowel drifts slowly by itself. vowel = which vowel, u o a e i in order; voice = whose formants, bass to soprano: it moves the upper formants (the singer's band near 3 kHz) more than the brightness.
techniques.code:
kvowel  = 2.0    ; vowel [0..4]: the sung vowel, u o a e i in that order, gliding through the ones between
kvoice  = 1.0    ; voice [0..3]: whose vowel it is: bass, tenor, alto, soprano, gliding between neighbours
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes
; the key sets the grain rate (the pitch); the five formants stay where the tables put them
; body resonance, FIXED in Hz
; formants from the head tables giVoxHz / giVoxDb / giVoxBw (Csound manual, Appendix D);
; index = (voice * 5 + formant) * 5 + vowel
; LOUDNESS: vowel
; LOUDNESS: voice
kf0     limit kfreq * koct1, 20, 12000
; kgateraw, not kgate: kgate is smoothed and only approaches 0, so the grains would run
; (and cost CPU) after the note. With xfund 0 fof starts no new grain.
kfund   = (kgateraw > 0 ? kf0 : 0)
; idle: 50 ms after the gate falls every grain has ended (kdur <= 20 ms), so the bank is
; skipped until the next note (an idle voice then costs 0.04 % of a core at 176400)
kidle   init 1
; a note that starts when every grain has ended (kdur <= kcap <= 20 ms) restarts fof's grain
; clock: a reinit with iskip 0 sets fundphs to a wrap (ugens7.c fofset0, iphs 0), so the
; first grain is at the note-on and not up to a period later, at the phase the last note
; froze. One k-cycle later a second pass with iskip 1 touches no grain and puts the opcode
; back where its lifetime test is bypassed (see the fof lines), so a held note never runs out.
kon     = (kgateraw > 0 && kidle > 0.021 ? 1 : 0)
kidle   = (kgateraw > 0 ? 0 : kidle + ksmps / sr)
kleg    init 0
if kon == 1 || kleg == 1 then
  reinit VOXFOF
endif
kleg    = kon
asig    = 0
        if kidle > 0.05 kgoto VOXIDLE
; movement keyed to the note: the vowel drifts by up to a third of a vowel (two rates of
; opposite sign, this entry's own constants, so it crosses the set vowel both ways within
; the first 3 s), reflected at u and i so that it does not stop at either end
kdrift  = 0.2 * sin(6.283185307 * 0.13 * knote) - 0.12 * sin(6.283185307 * 0.31 * knote)
kvr     = kvowel + kdrift
kvw     = (kvr < 0 ? -kvr : (kvr > 4 ? 8 - kvr : kvr))
kvc     limit kvoice, 0, 3
kv0     = int(kvc)
kv1     = min(kv0 + 1, 3)
kvf     = kvc - kv0
kF1a    tablei (kv0 * 5 + 0) * 5 + kvw, giVoxHz
kF1b    tablei (kv1 * 5 + 0) * 5 + kvw, giVoxHz
kF1     = kF1a + (kF1b - kF1a) * kvf
kA1a    tablei (kv0 * 5 + 0) * 5 + kvw, giVoxDb
kA1b    tablei (kv1 * 5 + 0) * 5 + kvw, giVoxDb
kA1     = kA1a + (kA1b - kA1a) * kvf
kB1a    tablei (kv0 * 5 + 0) * 5 + kvw, giVoxBw
kB1b    tablei (kv1 * 5 + 0) * 5 + kvw, giVoxBw
kB1     = kB1a + (kB1b - kB1a) * kvf
kF2a    tablei (kv0 * 5 + 1) * 5 + kvw, giVoxHz
kF2b    tablei (kv1 * 5 + 1) * 5 + kvw, giVoxHz
kF2     = kF2a + (kF2b - kF2a) * kvf
kA2a    tablei (kv0 * 5 + 1) * 5 + kvw, giVoxDb
kA2b    tablei (kv1 * 5 + 1) * 5 + kvw, giVoxDb
kA2     = kA2a + (kA2b - kA2a) * kvf
kB2a    tablei (kv0 * 5 + 1) * 5 + kvw, giVoxBw
kB2b    tablei (kv1 * 5 + 1) * 5 + kvw, giVoxBw
kB2     = kB2a + (kB2b - kB2a) * kvf
kF3a    tablei (kv0 * 5 + 2) * 5 + kvw, giVoxHz
kF3b    tablei (kv1 * 5 + 2) * 5 + kvw, giVoxHz
kF3     = kF3a + (kF3b - kF3a) * kvf
kA3a    tablei (kv0 * 5 + 2) * 5 + kvw, giVoxDb
kA3b    tablei (kv1 * 5 + 2) * 5 + kvw, giVoxDb
kA3     = kA3a + (kA3b - kA3a) * kvf
kB3a    tablei (kv0 * 5 + 2) * 5 + kvw, giVoxBw
kB3b    tablei (kv1 * 5 + 2) * 5 + kvw, giVoxBw
kB3     = kB3a + (kB3b - kB3a) * kvf
kF4a    tablei (kv0 * 5 + 3) * 5 + kvw, giVoxHz
kF4b    tablei (kv1 * 5 + 3) * 5 + kvw, giVoxHz
kF4     = kF4a + (kF4b - kF4a) * kvf
kA4a    tablei (kv0 * 5 + 3) * 5 + kvw, giVoxDb
kA4b    tablei (kv1 * 5 + 3) * 5 + kvw, giVoxDb
kA4     = kA4a + (kA4b - kA4a) * kvf
kB4a    tablei (kv0 * 5 + 3) * 5 + kvw, giVoxBw
kB4b    tablei (kv1 * 5 + 3) * 5 + kvw, giVoxBw
kB4     = kB4a + (kB4b - kB4a) * kvf
kF5a    tablei (kv0 * 5 + 4) * 5 + kvw, giVoxHz
kF5b    tablei (kv1 * 5 + 4) * 5 + kvw, giVoxHz
kF5     = kF5a + (kF5b - kF5a) * kvf
kA5a    tablei (kv0 * 5 + 4) * 5 + kvw, giVoxDb
kA5b    tablei (kv1 * 5 + 4) * 5 + kvw, giVoxDb
kA5     = kA5a + (kA5b - kA5a) * kvf
kB5a    tablei (kv0 * 5 + 4) * 5 + kvw, giVoxBw
kB5b    tablei (kv1 * 5 + 4) * 5 + kvw, giVoxBw
kB5     = kB5a + (kB5b - kB5a) * kvf
; F1 tuning (Sundberg): above F1 a singer raises F1 to the fundamental; untuned, the first
; formant falls below H1 and the note loses its body (measured: -44 dB at 2 kHz, tenor a)
kF1t    = max(kF1, kf0)
; grain length: a grain lasts until its own decay is 20 dB down where the end fade starts
; (0.65 kdur): kdur = ln(10) / (pi * 0.65 * B) = 1.13 / B, per formant. fof's CPU grows with
; the grains alive, so the length is also capped at 20 ms and at 10 periods (uncapped,
; 16 voices at 1760 Hz = 95 % of a core); a B narrower than the cap allows is widened to
; 1.13 / cap, so it is heard as the B it gets, not cut. The decay fade is 0.35 kdur.
kcap    = min(0.02, 10 / kf0)
kbf     = 1.13 / kcap
; the rise (giRis, 1/2 - cos/2) lasts 3 ms, or 0.65 kdur where the grain is shorter (high
; keys), so that it ends where the decay fade begins and never outlasts the grain
; level: a periodic train of damped sinusoids (rate f0, formant F, bandwidth B, amplitude a)
; has power a^2/(8 pi) * (f0/b) * S, b = B/2, S = sinh(2 pi y)/(cosh(2 pi y) - cos(2 pi x)),
; x = F/f0, y = b/f0 (Fourier series of the train + the closed-form Lorentzian comb sum).
; S is 1 on average and peaks where a harmonic sits on a formant. fof starts each grain at
; a * exp(pi B Tr) (ugens7.c newpulse: preamp = expamp^-rismps), so that it reaches a at
; the end of the rise Tr; its energy is then R times the plain decay's: with q = 2 pi B Tr,
; the rise (integral of rise^2 * exp(q (1 - s)), closed form) gives 3/8 (e^q - 1)
; - 1/2 q^2 (e^q + 1)/(q^2 + pi^2) + 1/8 q^2 (e^q - 1)/(q^2 + 4 pi^2), the decay after it
; 1 - e^(q - 2 pi B kdur) = 1 - e^q e^-7.1 (+1.2 dB at B 40 Hz, +7 dB at 200 Hz, +9 dB where
; Tr = 0.65 kdur). Input gain only, from the opcode's own envelope.
kBe1    = max(kB1, kbf)
kdur1   = 1.13 / kBe1
kris1   = min(0.003, 0.65 * kdur1)
ky1     = 0.5 * kBe1 / kf0
kS1     = sinh(6.2832 * ky1) / (cosh(6.2832 * ky1) - cos(6.2832 * kF1t / kf0))
kq1     = 6.2832 * kBe1 * kris1
kE1     = exp(kq1)
kqq1    = kq1 * kq1
kR1     = 0.375 * (kE1 - 1) - 0.5 * kqq1 * (kE1 + 1) / (kqq1 + 9.8696) + 0.125 * kqq1 * (kE1 - 1) / (kqq1 + 39.478) + 1 - 0.000825 * kE1
kBe2    = max(kB2, kbf)
kdur2   = 1.13 / kBe2
kris2   = min(0.003, 0.65 * kdur2)
ky2     = 0.5 * kBe2 / kf0
kS2     = sinh(6.2832 * ky2) / (cosh(6.2832 * ky2) - cos(6.2832 * kF2 / kf0))
kq2     = 6.2832 * kBe2 * kris2
kE2     = exp(kq2)
kqq2    = kq2 * kq2
kR2     = 0.375 * (kE2 - 1) - 0.5 * kqq2 * (kE2 + 1) / (kqq2 + 9.8696) + 0.125 * kqq2 * (kE2 - 1) / (kqq2 + 39.478) + 1 - 0.000825 * kE2
kBe3    = max(kB3, kbf)
kdur3   = 1.13 / kBe3
kris3   = min(0.003, 0.65 * kdur3)
ky3     = 0.5 * kBe3 / kf0
kS3     = sinh(6.2832 * ky3) / (cosh(6.2832 * ky3) - cos(6.2832 * kF3 / kf0))
kq3     = 6.2832 * kBe3 * kris3
kE3     = exp(kq3)
kqq3    = kq3 * kq3
kR3     = 0.375 * (kE3 - 1) - 0.5 * kqq3 * (kE3 + 1) / (kqq3 + 9.8696) + 0.125 * kqq3 * (kE3 - 1) / (kqq3 + 39.478) + 1 - 0.000825 * kE3
kBe4    = max(kB4, kbf)
kdur4   = 1.13 / kBe4
kris4   = min(0.003, 0.65 * kdur4)
ky4     = 0.5 * kBe4 / kf0
kS4     = sinh(6.2832 * ky4) / (cosh(6.2832 * ky4) - cos(6.2832 * kF4 / kf0))
kq4     = 6.2832 * kBe4 * kris4
kE4     = exp(kq4)
kqq4    = kq4 * kq4
kR4     = 0.375 * (kE4 - 1) - 0.5 * kqq4 * (kE4 + 1) / (kqq4 + 9.8696) + 0.125 * kqq4 * (kE4 - 1) / (kqq4 + 39.478) + 1 - 0.000825 * kE4
kBe5    = max(kB5, kbf)
kdur5   = 1.13 / kBe5
kris5   = min(0.003, 0.65 * kdur5)
ky5     = 0.5 * kBe5 / kf0
kS5     = sinh(6.2832 * ky5) / (cosh(6.2832 * ky5) - cos(6.2832 * kF5 / kf0))
kq5     = 6.2832 * kBe5 * kris5
kE5     = exp(kq5)
kqq5    = kq5 * kq5
kR5     = 0.375 * (kE5 - 1) - 0.5 * kqq5 * (kE5 + 1) / (kqq5 + 9.8696) + 0.125 * kqq5 * (kE5 - 1) / (kqq5 + 39.478) + 1 - 0.000825 * kE5
kP      = ampdb(2 * kA1) * kS1 / ky1 * kR1 + ampdb(2 * kA2) * kS2 / ky2 * kR2 + ampdb(2 * kA3) * kS3 / ky3 * kR3 + ampdb(2 * kA4) * kS4 / ky4 * kR4 + ampdb(2 * kA5) * kS5 / ky5 * kR5
; 0.61: rms 0.12 at the defaults, 220 Hz (a level choice; the engine trims a standing body)
knorm   = 0.61 / sqrt(kP)
; iolaps 64 = 10 grains of the new note + 10 of the old after a jump, with margin; too few
; is a PerfError that kills the voice. itotdur 1 with iskip 1: iskip bypasses fof's
; lifetime test, so the grains never stop (the host's p3 of 2e9 s would overflow int32).
; iskp is 0 only on the pass a rested note-on asks for; i(kon) reads 0 on the build pass,
; where fof initialises fully anyway because nothing is allocated yet.
VOXFOF:
iskp    = (i(kon) == 1 ? 0 : 1)
af1     fof ampdb(kA1) * knorm, kfund, kF1t, 0, kBe1, kris1, kdur1, 0.35 * kdur1, 64, giSine, giRis, 1, 0, 0, iskp
af2     fof ampdb(kA2) * knorm, kfund, kF2, 0, kBe2, kris2, kdur2, 0.35 * kdur2, 64, giSine, giRis, 1, 0, 0, iskp
af3     fof ampdb(kA3) * knorm, kfund, kF3, 0, kBe3, kris3, kdur3, 0.35 * kdur3, 64, giSine, giRis, 1, 0, 0, iskp
af4     fof ampdb(kA4) * knorm, kfund, kF4, 0, kBe4, kris4, kdur4, 0.35 * kdur4, 64, giSine, giRis, 1, 0, 0, iskp
af5     fof ampdb(kA5) * knorm, kfund, kF5, 0, kBe5, kris5, kdur5, 0.35 * kdur5, 64, giSine, giRis, 1, 0, 0, iskp
asig    = af1 + af2 + af3 + af4 + af5
; a damped sine that starts at phase 0 has a mean that is not zero, so the grain train
; carries DC; a 5 Hz high-pass takes it out. It sits inside the idle skip, so its state
; freezes with the bank; istor = iskp clears that frozen state on the pass a rested
; note-on asks for and keeps it on every other pass
asig    atone asig, 5, iskp
rireturn
VOXIDLE:
asig    = asig * kvol1

vowel.note: the vowel, u o a e i in order, gliding through those between: F1 and F2 move. Power-weighted centroid at 220 Hz, drift held: u 618, o 566, a 965, e 649, i 426 Hz; level within 1.7 dB (declared).

u.gloss: closed and dark: F1 and F2 both low

a.gloss: open: F1 at its highest, the power centroid near 1 kHz

i.gloss: closed: F1 at its lowest, F2 near 2 kHz, a wide gap between them

voice.note: whose formants: bass, tenor, alto, soprano. Moves the upper formants: the 2-4 kHz band goes from -8 dB (bass) to -20 dB (alto, soprano) of the whole; the centroid barely moves.

bass.gloss: the lowest formants, a strong band at 2.2-2.8 kHz

soprano.gloss: high formants, the band near 3 kHz 12 dB weaker

heard.hinweis: Neuer Körper, nur gemessen, nicht gehört. Ein Vokal, kein Sänger: kein Text, kein Vibrato, kein Atem, kein Chor. Die Vokaldrift bewegt die Lautstärke innerhalb eines Tons um bis zu 2,5 dB (Sopran, a, 440 Hz). CPU bei 176400: 0,85 % eines Kerns pro Stimme bei 220 Hz, etwa 2,2 % ab 1760 Hz. Legato von tief nach hoch: der letzte tiefe Grain klingt in den neuen Ton hinein. Nachschlag unter 21 ms Pause: der erste Grain kommt bis zu eine Periode verspätet.

techniques.why: sub bass: a sine fundamental with its divider octave beneath it, the octave 9 dB under the fundamental. The octave's level breathes +-2 dB over a 4-second cycle that restarts with every note, so the low end swells and recedes slowly while the fundamental stays still. The fundamental is the key you play; the octave runs at exactly half its frequency and is never reset, so the two stay phase-locked through glides and from note to note, and the waveform never drifts; its peak moves only with the octave's breath. Material for a clean low register under other layers or alone: no attack, no strike, nothing above the fundamental. The waveform repeats every two periods of the key, which a pitch probe flags as period doubling; that is the octave, by design. The 808 bass drum is analog_kick, not this.
mandatory_flags: 'sub' is a register/mix role, not a distinct spectrum; approximated as a pure sine
techniques.code:
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes -- the fundamental is kfreq * koct1, the divider octave exactly half of it
; phase lock: both poscil run free, never reinit'd, and x0.5 is exact, so 2:1 on every
; sample. Do not reinit, phase or detune either: a sub that drifts is no divider.
; Breath keyed to knote, not a free LFO
afn0    poscil 0.50, kfreq * koct1, giSine
ksb0    = 0.50 * ampdb(-9 + 2 * sin(6.283185307 * 0.25 * knote))
; a(): a k-rate level lands the note-on restart as a step, not a ramp
asb0    poscil a(ksb0), kfreq * koct1 * 0.5, giSine
asig    = (afn0 + asb0) * kvol1

heard.hinweis: Körper am 2026-11-20 neu gebaut: Grundton plus phasenstarre Teiler-Oktave, deren Pegel mit 0,25 Hz um ±2 dB atmet, an knote gebunden. Der frühere Vermerk „kein Beleg für eine Abnahme durch BJ gefunden“ betraf den Vorgänger (gbuzz-Oktave mit freilaufender Drift).

techniques.why: analogue oscillator / vco / dco: ONE waveform generator with every control the shape needs. `wave` picks between two vco2 generators -- the ramp one and the pulse one -- and `width` is the SAME position on both: the fraction of the period spent in the first phase, symmetric at 0.5. So a waveform is a pair of numbers, not a name: a triangle is wave 0 with width 0.5, a saw wave 0 with width near either end, a square wave 1 with width 0.5, a narrow pulse wave 1 with width 0.12. The width is a modulation DESTINATION -- whatever writes it, an LFO, an envelope, a hand, is pulse width modulation, and the measure of that movement is the interval of widths it covers. `finetune` shifts the pitch in cents so several layers can be detuned against each other; `drive` is not a shaper at all: it is how hard this oscillator is driven INTO the synth's filter, 0 dB up to as loud as the body may be, so the saturating element is the ladder's own input stage -- a Minimoog fed through its External Input Volume, which is what the sound is named after; `age` is component drift, and it is the axis between the two kinds of machine in that list: at 0 nothing drifts and this is a DCO, a digitally clocked pitch, while the drift itself is what a VCO does. Level MOVES across `drive`, by design and by measurement -- that axis is a level; across `width` it moves too, and must -- see both parameters.

wave.note: which of the two generators is heard: 0 the ramp one (vco2 imode 4), 1 the pulse one (imode 2), and between them the two are crossfaded. Both read `width` as the same fourth argument, so this control does not name a waveform on its own -- it picks the family and `width` picks the position in it. Measured at 220 Hz with the width at its symmetric 0.5: centroid 675 Hz on the ramp generator (a triangle) against 5620 on the pulse one (a square); at width 0.02 the ramp generator reads 2180 (a saw).

ramp.gloss: the triangle/saw generator -- `width` sets where the ramp breaks

pulse.gloss: the square/pulse generator -- `width` sets the duty

width.note: the fraction of one period spent in the first phase -- rising on the ramp generator, high on the pulse generator -- and it is the same argument to vco2 in both cases. 0.5 is the symmetric one on either: a triangle, a square. There every even harmonic cancels -- odd/even measured 131.3 dB on the ramp generator and 96.5 on the pulse one -- because the amplitudes carry |sin(pi*n*w)| on both (over n on the pulse, over n^2 on the ramp -- the pulse is the derivative of the asymmetric triangle, which is one power of n). Away from 0.5 the even harmonics come in and the nth is cancelled wherever n*w is a whole number. w and 1-w are the same magnitude spectrum, so 0.12 and 0.88 sound alike: measured on the pulse generator with `age` at 0, odd/even 1.6 dB against 1.6 and centroids 4317.1 against 4317.4 Hz. On the PULSE generator a width off 0.5 is also quieter, because the DC it carries, A*(2w-1), is taken out and a narrow pulse is mostly that -- measured 3.77 dB down at 0.12 against 0.5 and 11.28 at 0.02, where rms 2A*sqrt(w(1-w)) predicts 3.74 and 11.06 -- and that is the sound of the thing, not a fault to correct. On the RAMP generator there is no such term: its rms is 1/sqrt(3) at every width -- measured -9.21 dB at 0.02, 0.12, 0.5, 0.88 and 0.98 alike -- so there the same number is colour alone.

end.gloss: the far end: a sawtooth on the ramp generator, a sliver of a pulse on the other

narrow.gloss: well off symmetric -- thin and nasal, and on the pulse generator quieter

symmetric.gloss: odd harmonics only, on either generator: a triangle, a square

wide.gloss: the mirror of narrow -- same spectrum, same level

finetune.note: cents off the played note, so two or three layers of this oscillator can be detuned against each other -- the octave knobs the player has (koct1/2/3) move in octaves and cannot do it. Beating between two layers a few cents apart is what makes a sound thick; that thickness is composed from layers here and is not a knob on one oscillator. Measured: -25 asked gives -25 heard.

flat.gloss: a slow beat against a layer at zero

sharp.gloss: the same beat the other way

drive.note: how hard the oscillator is driven INTO the synth's filter, and nothing else: 0 to 1 is 0 dB up to the loudest this body may be, even in dB across the knob -- +11.4 dB on the ramp generator, +5.5 dB on the narrowest pulse, because that wave is already twice as tall and there is less room above it. There is no shaper in the oscillator. The saturating element is the ladder's own input stage -- the same construction as a Minimoog fed through its External Input Volume, where the mixer runs hot and the filter's transistor stages bend. So this control needs `filter_algorithm` on `ladder` to have its character; on the svf it is level alone, which is what an external input into a clean mixer also is. Measured through this synth's ladder at cutoff 1200, resonance 0.35, 24 dB/oct, filter drive 0: at 110 Hz the output rises 10.70 dB from clean to full, its crest falls 3.17 to 2.45 and its centroid falls 707 to 580 Hz -- the driven sound is darker and denser, not brighter. The reference this was built against (BJ's own Minimoog V External Input Volume recording, 2026-08-01) reads 16.00 dB, crest 2.31 to 1.65, centroid 3253 to 600 Hz, and BJ on its top: 'beim MiniV ist ExtInpVol auch erheblich zu krass'. The top of this knob is instead where the HOST stops being transparent (2.523 in body units), and the body computes how far that is from vco2's own definition of the wave it just made, so the top lands there at every width instead of running into the scaffold's hard clip on the pulse generator.

clean.gloss: unity -- the oscillator as it stands

warm.gloss: a third of the way up, the ladder's stages just starting to bend

hot.gloss: as loud as this body goes -- the filter is being overdriven

age.note: how far the components have drifted: a slow pitch wander, a jitter on the duty, and a slow level wobble, each scaled by this one value and each at its own unrelated rate so they never lock. At 0 the oscillator is mathematically exact and sounds it: that setting is a DCO and not a VCO -- rock-stable digital pitch is the thing a DCO was built to have. Every voice enters the drift at a different phase, so a chord does not wander in lockstep.

dco.gloss: no drift at all. This is what a DCO IS: the pitch comes off a divider rather than out of a VCO's temperature-dependent core, so it does not move. BJ named this anchor (2026-07-30) — a digitally clocked core is exactly this case.

techniques.code:
; LOUDNESS: width
; LOUDNESS: wave
; the pulse generator's level follows its width: what is left once the DC A*(2w-1)
; is taken out is 2A*sqrt(w(1-w)) -- 3.77 dB down at 0.12 and 11.28 at 0.02. So
; `width` moves the level on that generator, and `wave`, which decides how much of
; it is heard, carries that with it. The ramp generator has no such term: rms
; 1/sqrt(3) at every width. A pulse gets quieter the narrower it gets, and that IS
; pulse width modulation (BJ 2026-07-28, LCO_CONCEPT.md section 4).
; LOUDNESS: drive
; `drive` is the LEVEL this oscillator sends into the synth's filter, and there is
; no shaper in here at all. That is what the knob is on a Minimoog: the External
; Input Volume feeds the mixer at high gain and the LADDER's own transistor stages
; do the saturating. Measured on BJ's Minimoog V recording of exactly that
; (2026-08-01): the level rises 16.00 dB from clean to driven, the crest falls
; 2.31 to 1.65 and the spectral centroid falls 3253 Hz to about 600 -- the driven
; sound is DARKER and denser, not brighter. A waveshaper held to the clean level
; cannot produce any of those three; a pregain into a saturating filter produces
; all three. So this axis moves the level, and must.

kwave   = 0.00    ; wave [0..1]: which generator -- 0 the ramp, 1 the pulse
kwidth  = 0.02    ; width [0.02..0.98]: the fraction of the period spent in the first phase
kfinetune = 0.00  ; finetune [-50..50]: cents off the played note
kdrive  = 0.00    ; drive [0..1]: how hard this oscillator is driven into the filter
kage    = 0.35    ; age [0..1]: component drift -- pitch, width and level wobble

ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)          ; each voice enters the drift elsewhere
kdrf    poscil 0.007 * kage, 0.043 + 0.0037 * ivoice, giSine, ivph
kjit    poscil 0.012 * kage, 0.057             ; age: width jitter
klvl    oscili 0.030 * kage, 0.7               ; age: level wobble
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1) * (2 ^ (kfinetune / 1200)) * (1 + kdrf)

kfold   = kwidth + kjit                        ; ONE width, and both generators read it
kdw     limit abs(kfold - 2 * round(kfold * 0.5)), 0.01, 0.99
                                               ; the clamp sits OUTSIDE the axis on
                                               ;   purpose. At 0.02 it would sit on
                                               ;   the width's own end and eat the
                                               ;   negative half of `kjit` there --
                                               ;   the drift would stop at exactly
                                               ;   the setting the entry ships. 0.01
                                               ;   and 0.99 is what Csound asks for.
                                               ; it FOLDS at 0 and 1 rather than wrapping:
                                               ;   w and 1-w are the same spectrum, so the
                                               ;   sound travels the same path either way,
                                               ;   but a wrap makes vco2 jump across its
                                               ;   own table discontinuity and emit a lone
                                               ;   one-sample spike. Measured over 8 s at
                                               ;   full depth: 15 wrapping, 0 folding.
aramp   vco2 0.6, kf0, 4, kdw                  ; ramp: 0.5 a triangle, either end a saw
apuls   vco2 0.6, kf0, 2, kdw                  ; pulse: 0.5 a square, either end narrow
apuls   = apuls - 0.6 * (2 * kdw - 1)          ; a width off 0.5 carries DC A*(2w-1), and
                                               ;   taking it out leaves the pulse quieter
                                               ;   the narrower it is -- 3.77 dB at 0.12.
                                               ;   The ramp has no such term: rms 1/sqrt(3)
                                               ;   at every width, colour alone.
aosc    = aramp * (1 - kwave) + apuls * kwave

; the DRIVE is a level, and the filter is what it drives.
kpk     = 0.6 * ((1 - kwave) + kwave * 2.36 * max(kdw, 1 - kdw))
                                               ; how tall this wave ALREADY is, from vco2's
                                               ;   own definition rather than from a meter:
                                               ;   the ramp peaks at its amplitude argument
                                               ;   at every width, and the pulse, once the
                                               ;   DC A*(2w-1) two lines up is taken out,
                                               ;   peaks at 2A*max(w,1-w). `kdw` already
                                               ;   carries the age jitter, so this follows
                                               ;   it. The 2.36 is that 2 with vco2's own
                                               ;   band-limiting overshoot on the pulse --
                                               ;   its edges ring past the ideal wave by a
                                               ;   measured 1.18 at width 0.5, against 1.01
                                               ;   on the ramp, which has no edge. Computing
                                               ;   the INPUT a generator needs is arithmetic
                                               ;   on the generator; it is not a fitted
                                               ;   curve laid over its output.
kgmax   = 2.23 / kpk                           ; so the TOP of the knob is the same place
                                               ;   whatever the wave: just under the host's
                                               ;   transparent ceiling (2.523 in body units;
                                               ;   the margin carries `klvl` and vco2's band
                                               ;   limiting overshoot). Where the wave is
                                               ;   already tall there is less room and the
                                               ;   knob gives less -- +11.4 dB on the ramp,
                                               ;   +5.5 on the narrowest pulse -- which is
                                               ;   also what a mixer does. Without this the
                                               ;   pulse generator's upper half met the
                                               ;   scaffold's own hard clip instead of the
                                               ;   ladder: measured p99.9 of 2.92 at width
                                               ;   0.12 and drive 0.67 against a 2.746 wall.
asig    = aosc * (kgmax ^ kdrive) * (1 + klvl) ; even in dB across the knob, which is what a
                                               ;   volume control is. Nothing shapes the wave in
                                               ;   here -- the saturating element is the
                                               ;   synth's LADDER, whose four stages see
                                               ;   whatever level this sends them
                                               ;   (2*Vt*tanh(x/2*Vt), Vt 1.22, so they
                                               ;   bend from about |x| 2.4 up) and which
                                               ;   applies no output compensation on
                                               ;   purpose. Set filter_algorithm to
                                               ;   `ladder` for that; on the svf this knob
                                               ;   is level alone, which is also what an
                                               ;   external input into a clean mixer is.
                                               ; The top is where the host stops being
                                               ;   transparent: this generator peaks 0.617
                                               ;   on the ramp, and 0.617 * 4 = 2.47 sits
                                               ;   just under the scaffold's 2.523. On the
                                               ;   PULSE generator at a narrow width the
                                               ;   wave already peaks 1.28, so there the
                                               ;   last part of the travel meets that
                                               ;   safety clip instead of the ladder --
                                               ;   the same fact as `width`'s own level,
                                               ;   seen from the other end.

techniques.why: air blown across the mouth of a bottle: a wide, soft, almost noteless tone with only two or three partials over the breath, and it stands as long as it is blown. Built from Csound's waveguide clarinet bore, driven at its blowing pressure (`kamp`) with its upper colour cut back until the tube reads as air over an opening rather than as a reed. NOT the reed instrument (`clarinet`) and not a struck vessel. blow = the pressure: the bore stays closed and hooting over the lower travel and SPEAKS in the top third, where the odd partials come up about 10 dB against the fundamental.
techniques.code:
; LOUDNESS: blow
; `blow` is the blowing PRESSURE on this bore, and pressure carries level with it --
; a bottle blown harder is louder, which is the physics and not an invented envelope.
; Measured at 220 Hz, meter calibrated 88/88, sr 44100: over the map the 3rd partial
; rises 10.1 dB against the fundamental and the crest goes 1.9 -> 4.4 while the rms
; moves 2.05 dB, so colour is what travels. NOT exempted and recorded here rather
; than hidden: the axis and the six registers together still spread 5.74 dB, above
; the 3.00 dB cross-register bound -- 4.11 dB of that is wgclar's own register tilt.
kblow   = 0.55   ; blow [0.00..1.00]: how hard the bottle is blown -- the pressure on the bore, from a closed hoot to as wide open as it goes before it blows out
kpr     = 0.60 + 0.20 * kblow                ; `kamp` IS the blowing pressure on this bore, not
                                             ; an output level. The bore SPEAKS between 0.72 and
                                             ; 0.76: below that the spectrum is frozen, above it
                                             ; the odd partials jump. 0.83 blows the model out of
                                             ; self-oscillation (loudness travel 59 dB), so 0.80
                                             ; is the ceiling and the map stops there.
kdrift  oscili 0.22, 0.07, giSine            ; the air over the mouth is never quite steady
asig    wgclar kpr, kfreq * koct1, -0.3, 0.1, 0.1, 0.5, 5.735, 0, giSine, 30
                                             ; `kngain` stays at 0.5. Measured 2026-07-31: over
                                             ; its documented 0..0.5 it is a LEVEL axis and adds
                                             ; no breath at all -- it is not the bore's axis.
                                             ; the -0.3 is `kstiff` and is INERT -- measured
                                             ; bit-identical from -0.9 to 0.0 in this build, so
                                             ; never put a control on it.
                                             ; kvamp is 0: the model's own vibrato stays off.
                                             ; ONE wgclar and no more: a second instance in the
                                             ; same body changes this one -- measured, the 3rd
                                             ; partial of a bore at kamp 0.80 falls from -2.3 to
                                             ; -12.3 dB with an unused second bore beside it.
asig    butterlp asig, kfreq * koct1 * (3.16 * (1 + kdrift))
                                             ; the bore's upper colour cut back until the tube
                                             ; reads as air over an opening and not as a reed;
                                             ; the slow wander on this corner is the body's own
                                             ; movement, and it is coherent where a wander on the
                                             ; pressure was not (it crossed the speaking
                                             ; threshold and read as variance, not motion).
asig    = asig * 1.45 * kvol1

blow.note: the blowing pressure on the bore (`kamp` 0.60..0.80). Measured at 220 Hz, meter calibrated 88/88, sr 44100: the 3rd partial relative to the fundamental goes -12.4 -> -2.3 dB and the 5th -23.5 -> -9.8 dB, the crest 1.9 -> 4.4, while the rms moves 2.05 dB -- a colour axis that carries some level with it, declared `; LOUDNESS: blow`. The change is a THRESHOLD, not a ramp: nothing moves from 0.60 to 0.72 and the bore opens between 0.72 and 0.76. Above 0.80 the model leaves self-oscillation (0.83: loudness travel 59 dB), which is why the map stops there. Not measured at the rate the plugin runs (176400): the harness renders at 44100 and fails its own calibration above that.

hooted.gloss: closed and dull, barely more than the fundamental

at the edge.gloss: the last of the closed tone, just under where it speaks

speaking.gloss: the bore open, the odd partials up about 8 dB

wide open.gloss: as open as the tube goes before it blows out

techniques.why: A metal body held ringing by moving air, never struck: three resonators (modal synthesis) in the coupled form of Mathews & Smith (SMAC 2003; Csound's `mvmfilter`), worked by one stream of lowpassed noise. It stands for as long as the key is held and never decays. Same modal family as `struck_bar`, `cymbal` and `singing_bowl`, which all begin with a strike and ring from it; this one has no attack, only air, and its colour comes from the air breathing. Rebuilt 2026-11-20: the air's brightness is a ratio of the key and breathes on a 10 s cycle keyed to the note; the noise is seeded per voice; one loudness through stretch, drive and breath by a derived law; the resonators keep their ring across a key change, so a lower note no longer bursts (+36 dB before) and a voice that has been running speaks at once. stretch = tube to stretched bell; drive = how far the air opens.
techniques.code:
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes
; A metal body held ringing by moving air, never struck. Modal synthesis: three
; `mvmfilter` resonators (a parallel bank of two-pole resonators) worked by one stream of
; lowpassed noise. The ratios are this entry's own -- a declared family from a
; whole-number tube (1:2:3) to a stretched bell (1:3.6:8.2), not a measured instrument.
; The note stands for as long as the key is held and never decays.
kstr    = 0.475   ; stretch[0.0..1.0]: how far the two upper modes sit off the 2nd and 3rd harmonic
kdrv    = 0.40    ; drive[0.0..1.0]: how many octaves above the key the air opens at the top of each breath
kf1     = kfreq * koct1
kr2     = 2.00 + 1.60 * kstr
kr3     = 3.00 + 5.20 * kstr
; --- THE AIR. The 31-bit generator (third argument 1), seeded per voice: one constant
;     seed gives all 16 voices the same sequence and a chord sums it coherently. The 16-bit
;     generator repeats every 65536 samples, a comb a Q-340 mode locks onto -- 55 Hz played
;     +47 cents at 176400. Uniform, so its variance is 0.05^2/3 at every seed.
aair    rand 0.05, frac(abs(sin(ivoice * 12.9898)) * 43758.5453), 1
; --- ITS BRIGHTNESS, a RATIO of the key (LCO_CONCEPT §4), so a knob position reads the
;     same at every register: the cutoff sits ON the played pitch at the dark end of each
;     breath and opens 1.5 + 2.5*drive octaves above it at the bright end. The breath is
;     keyed to the note: dark at note-on, brightest at 5 s, dark again at 10 s.
kbr     = 0.5 - 0.5 * cos(6.283185307 * 0.10 * knote)
;     A FALLING cutoff is slewed (half-time 20 ms): the SVF's state holds the air it
;     passed, and a cutoff dropped by up to nine octaves in one k-cycle (a high key, then
;     a low one) released it into the new lowest mode -- +7.8 dB for seconds, peak x3 at
;     44100. It is floored at the key, so a RISING cutoff still jumps with the key and the
;     level law's precondition holds (the key's mode never sits above the cutoff).
kcut    = kf1 * 2 ^ ((1.5 + 2.5 * kdrv) * kbr)
kcut    portk kcut, 0.02
kcut    limit kcut, min(max(kf1, 20), 18000), 18000
;     The lowpass is `zdf_2pole` (Opcodes/wpfilters.c, Zavalishin's topology-preserving
;     state-variable filter), not `butterlp`: butterlp is direct form II, whose state holds
;     the input scaled by ~(1/tan(pi*fc/sr))^2/4, so the cutoff leaping up with the key at
;     note-on released it as a burst -- +32 dB of air for 2 ms from idle to 880 Hz, a strike
;     on a body that is never struck. The SVF's state is in signal scale. At Q = 1/sqrt(2)
;     it is the same bilinear Butterworth, so the level law below holds unchanged.
aair    zdf_2pole aair, kcut, 0.70710678
; --- THE RESONATORS are `mvmfilter` (Opcodes/biquad.c), the coupled form of M. Mathews and
;     J. O. Smith, "Methods for Synthesizing Very High Q Parametrically Well Behaved Two Pole
;     Filters" (SMAC 2003). Its state is a phasor, turned by r*e^(i*theta) each sample, so a
;     new key turns the ring on at the new pitch with the amplitude it had: no burst on a
;     lower key, no build-up on any key. `mode` keeps a state scaled by 1/f and burst by
;     (f_old/f_new)^2 when a ringing voice took a lower key: +36 dB from 880 to 110 Hz.
;     tau = Q/(pi*f) rings as long as `mode` at that Q (measured equal within 0.1 %).
;     Frequency and tau stay k-rate: with an a-rate frequency the opcode sets r = 0.
; --- THE LEVEL LAW, applied to the modes' INPUT. The impulse response is r^n*cos(n*theta),
;     r = exp(-1/(tau*sr)), theta = 2*pi*f/sr, so white noise of variance s2 leaves a mode
;     at s2*E, E = 0.5/(1 - r^2) + 0.5*(1 - r^2*cos(2*theta))/(1 - 2*r^2*cos(2*theta) + r^4),
;     exact up to sr/2. Dividing each input by sqrt(E) leaves every mode at s2 times the
;     air's lowpass at that mode, at every key and every rate: impulse-response energy
;     1.0000 from 55 Hz to 21 kHz at 44100 and 176400. Modes fade out between 19 and 20 kHz:
;     the opcode clamps at sr/2, a clamped mode is a false partial, and a fixed 20 kHz keeps
;     the same partials at every rate.
kfa     limit kf1, 20, 20000
kfb     limit kf1 * kr2, 20, 20000
kfc     limit kf1 * kr3, 20, 20000
kwb     limit (20000 - kf1 * kr2) / 1000, 0, 1
kwc     limit (20000 - kf1 * kr3) / 1000, 0, 1
; --- ONE LOUDNESS through breath, drive and stretch. The lowpass is the bilinear-transform
;     Butterworth (g = tan(pi*fc/sr), R = 1/(2Q)): |H(f)|^2 = 1/(1 + (tan(pi*f/sr)/tan(pi*fc/sr))^4). The
;     bank's power is therefore s2 * sum(w^2 * |H(f_mode)|^2), and the air is scaled to hold
;     that sum at its fully open value 0.6^2 + 0.3^2 + 0.16^2 = 0.4756. Breath and drive move
;     the balance between the modes, never the level. Computed, not fitted.
ktc     = tan(3.14159265 * kcut / sr)
kha     = 1 / (1 + (tan(3.14159265 * kfa / sr) / ktc) ^ 4)
khb     = 1 / (1 + (tan(3.14159265 * kfb / sr) / ktc) ^ 4)
khc     = 1 / (1 + (tan(3.14159265 * kfc / sr) / ktc) ^ 4)
kpow    = 0.36 * kha + 0.09 * khb * kwb * kwb + 0.0256 * khc * kwc * kwc
aair    = aair * sqrt(0.4756 / kpow)
kpa     = exp(-6.283185307 * kfa / (340 * sr))      ; r^2 of each mode, Q 340 / 260 / 190
kpb     = exp(-6.283185307 * kfb / (260 * sr))
kpc     = exp(-6.283185307 * kfc / (190 * sr))
kca     = cos(12.566370614 * kfa / sr)              ; cos(2*theta)
kcb     = cos(12.566370614 * kfb / sr)
kcc     = cos(12.566370614 * kfc / sr)
kea     = 0.5 / (1 - kpa) + 0.5 * (1 - kpa * kca) / (1 - 2 * kpa * kca + kpa * kpa)
keb     = 0.5 / (1 - kpb) + 0.5 * (1 - kpb * kcb) / (1 - 2 * kpb * kcb + kpb * kpb)
kec     = 0.5 / (1 - kpc) + 0.5 * (1 - kpc * kcc) / (1 - 2 * kpc * kcc + kpc * kpc)
a1      mvmfilter aair / sqrt(kea), kfa, 340 / (3.14159265 * kfa)
a2      mvmfilter aair / sqrt(keb), kfb, 260 / (3.14159265 * kfb)
a3      mvmfilter aair / sqrt(kec), kfc, 190 / (3.14159265 * kfc)
asig    = (a1 * 0.6 + a2 * 0.3 * kwb + a3 * 0.16 * kwc) * 10 * kvol1

stretch.note: the two upper modes: 1:2:3 at 0, 1:2.76:5.47 at the default, 1:3.6:8.2 at 1. at 220 Hz: level within 0.15 dB along the axis (both rates); mode 3 at the top of the breath -13 dB at 0, -20 at 1.

tube.gloss: 1:2:3, on the 2nd and 3rd harmonic; mode 3 at -13 dB at the top of the breath

leaning.gloss: 1:2.30:3.99: second mode 245 cents sharp of the octave, third near the double octave

bell.gloss: 1:2.76:5.47: both upper modes off the harmonic series; the found body

plate.gloss: 1:3.6:8.2: the widest spread; the third mode drops to -20 dB at the top of the breath

drive.note: how far the air opens above the key at the top of the 10 s breath: 1.5 octaves at 0, 4 at 1. at 220 Hz: level within 0.15 dB along the axis (both rates); mode 3 there: -24 dB at 0, -13 at 1.

muffled.gloss: opens 1.5 octaves above the key: mode 3 at -24 dB, the fundamental carries it

room.gloss: opens 2.5 octaves: the default; mode 3 at -15 dB at the top of the breath

bright.gloss: opens 3.3 octaves: modes 2 and 3 rise to -7 and -13 dB at the top of the breath

hissing.gloss: opens 4 octaves: all three modes lit; no path lets the air through, only the rings

heard.hinweis: Körper am 2026-11-20 neu gebaut (Resonatoren nach Mathews & Smith, Luft als Verhältnis zur Taste, Atem an die Note gebunden, Pegel abgeleitet, Rauschen pro Stimme); der frühere Eintrag betraf den Vorgänger: Status „nur einzelne Dateien gehört“, BJ 2026-07-30: „approved aus von dir vorgebauten files mit intransparenter parameterlage aus einem Ordner“. Gate: bei 44100 bestanden; bei 176400 liegen die Register 4,0 dB auseinander (Grenze 3,0; 55 Hz am lautesten). Der Pegel wandert innerhalb einer Note, und nach dem Laden baut sich der Körper aus der Stille auf.

techniques.why: divide-down organ / string machine -- a transistor organ, combo organ, theatre organ or Solina-family string synthesizer: ONE master clock divided by twelve integers, exact binary octaves below, and every stop a footage sum off that same RUNNING chain. No key starts a tone -- the chain runs and a key only opens taps onto it. The OCTAVE ranks come off that chain, so unisons and octaves between two keys are EXACT; every other interval is equal-tempered and beats as it does anywhere else. Four mixable stops (`flute` the hollow tibia, `diapason` the bright principal chorus, `reed` the nasal kinura/brass/sax family, `strings` the raw saw bus of a string machine), `age` for how far the chain's integer division strays from equal temperament, and `ensemble` for the three-phase bucket-brigade chorus -- the only thing in the instrument that moves, since the chain itself is rigid.

flute.note: the tibia rank: 8', 4', 2' and 1' voiced close to sines, the lowest rank's own third partial 5 dB above the others', which is what keeps it from going hollow. The woody core of an organ and the closest one gets to a pure tone -- it is what carries a theatre organ's warmth. Raising it does not brighten the sound, it fills it out from below.

closed.gloss: the rank is out; nothing of the tibia is heard

soft.gloss: a thin round underlay beneath the brighter stops

hollow.gloss: the woody tibia clearly present, the sound rounded out

full.gloss: the hollow tibia carries the whole registration

diapason.note: the principal chorus: every octave footage plus the 2 2/3' quint and the 1 3/5' tierce. The bright, singing, church-organ body. The quint and tierce are what give it a metallic edge that no stack of octaves alone can reach.

closed.gloss: the chorus is out; nothing of the principal is heard

blended.gloss: an edge of brightness over the flutes

singing.gloss: the principal chorus carries, bright and vocal

full.gloss: the full chorus, quint and tierce ringing on top

reed.note: the kinura / brass / sax family. The fundamental is gone and a formant rides partials 3 to 7 -- that missing fundamental is exactly what makes a reed nasal, snarling and vocal instead of round. It is the most aggressive of the four stops and by far the peakiest, though the diapason is marginally louder. It holds its shape up to a played 2.5 kHz or so; above that the bandpass's own warping lifts the fundamental back and it turns into a bright square.

nasal.gloss: a pinched, reedy voice cutting through the flues

snarling.gloss: the full kinura -- hard, buzzing and aggressive

strings.note: the raw saw bus of a string machine -- Solina, Logan, Elka -- at 8' and 4'. Alone with `ensemble` up it IS a string machine; under the organ stops it adds a thin bright rasp the flue pipes do not have.

thin.gloss: a faint bright rasp over the organ stops

full.gloss: the bare saw bus of a string machine

age.note: how far the divider chain's tuning strays from equal temperament. The chain divides one master clock by twelve INTEGERS, and that rounding leaves every pitch class its own small fixed offset. This is a DIFFERENT temperament, not a detuning: raising it does not make chords sour, it moves each interval somewhere else. Over the travel the minor third and minor sixth get rougher while the fifth, the sixth and the minor seventh lock TIGHTER than equal temperament manages; octaves and unisons never move at all. 0 is an exactly equal-tempered chain; 1 is the measured Yamaha D-85; above it the chain is coarser than any that was ever built. It is a FIXED offset per key, not a wobble -- a single note cannot show it, two keys together can.

equal.gloss: exactly equal-tempered; the chain's own error taken out

vintage.gloss: the temperament of a real divide-down organ -- at this setting its fourth comes out exactly pure

tempered.gloss: the chain's departure clearly audible in a held chord

coarse.gloss: a coarser chain than was ever built; the temperament plainly its own

ensemble.note: the three-phase bucket-brigade chorus of a string machine: the whole sound through three swept delay lines 120 degrees apart. This is the ONLY thing in the instrument that moves -- the generator chain is rigid by construction. At 0 the tone stands perfectly still: that is the standing-tone escape, not a defect. The knob is a chorus and not a fader; the level holds across its whole travel.

still.gloss: dead still -- the rigid, frozen tone of a bare divider chain

shimmer.gloss: a slow gentle swim over the tone

swimming.gloss: the wide three-phase chorus of a string machine

drowning.gloss: the chorus at full sweep, the pitch visibly swaying

techniques.code:
; LOUDNESS: flute
; LOUDNESS: diapason
; LOUDNESS: reed
; LOUDNESS: strings
; A divide-down organ -- transistor organ, combo organ, string machine. ONE master clock,
; twelve integer divisors, exact binary octaves, and every stop a footage sum off that same
; RUNNING chain: the drawbar principle. Nothing here is keyed to the note -- the chain runs
; and a key only opens taps onto it. The OCTAVE ranks come off that chain, so unisons and
; octaves between two keys are EXACT; every other interval is equal-tempered and beats exactly
; as it does anywhere else. The quint and tierce are taken as exact harmonics of the key rather
; than as their own divider outputs, so they lock where a real chain's would beat slightly.
; Method: top-octave generator, divisors round(478 / 2^(k/12)) -- the MK50240 set. Measured
; against a Yamaha D-85 (49 notes, C3-C7): its tuning error depends on the PITCH CLASS alone
; (0.01 cents spread across octaves) and those divisors reproduce its 12-value pattern to
; 0.03 cents rms. The stop recipes are that organ's own recovered drawbar levels.
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes.   DECAY: none -- it stands for as long as the key is held.
; It MOVES only through `ensemble`; the chain itself is rigid, and that rigidity is the point.
kflute    = 1.00  ; flute [0..1]: the tibia rank -- 8', 4', 2' and 1' voiced nearly to sines, no quint
kdiapason = 0.45  ; diapason [0..1]: the principal chorus -- octave footages plus the 2 2/3' quint and 1 3/5' tierce
kreed     = 0.00  ; reed [0..1]: the kinura / brass / sax family -- fundamental gone, a formant riding partials 3-7
kstrings  = 0.00  ; strings [0..1]: the raw saw bus of a string machine, 8' and 4'
kage      = 1.00  ; age [0..3]: how far the chain's tuning departs from equal temperament; 1 = the measured D-85
kensemble = 0.45  ; ensemble [0..1]: the three-phase bucket-brigade chorus; 0 is the standing-tone escape

kbase   limit kfreq * koct1, 8.0, 12600.0       ; the host already holds kfreq to 20..12000;
                                                ;   this guards the koct1 product and keeps
                                                ;   log() away from zero
kny     = min(sr * 0.45, 20000)                             ; no voicing corner may pass Nyquist
kpch    = 12 * (log(kbase / 261.6256) / 0.69314718055994531) + 120
                                                ; semitones above C, held positive. NOT logbtwo,
                                                ;   whose table is 0.38 cents out at the bottom of
                                                ;   the keyboard -- harmless now that round() sits
                                                ;   below it, but this line is also the pitch-class
                                                ;   claim's only evidence, and it should be exact.
kkey    = round(kpch)                           ; the KEY picks the divisor, never the bend --
                                                ;   a divider chain has twelve of them, not one
                                                ;   per cent, and rounding the bend would make
                                                ;   the chain a staircase under a glide.
kpc     = kkey - 12 * int(kkey / 12)            ; the pitch class this key asks the chain for
kdiv    = round(478 / pow(2, kpc / 12))         ; the divisor the top-octave chip actually has
kf      = kbase * pow((478 / kdiv) / pow(2, kpc / 12), kage)

at1      vco2 0.5, kf,       10        ; 8'      the rank that sounds the key. The flip-flops
at2      vco2 0.5, kf * 2.0, 10        ; 4'        put out SQUARES, so each rank already
at3      vco2 0.5, kf * 3.0, 10        ; 2 2/3'    carries its own odd partials.
at4      vco2 0.5, kf * 4.0, 10        ; 2'
at5      vco2 0.5, kf * 5.0, 10        ; 1 3/5'
at8      vco2 0.5, kf * 8.0, 10        ; 1'

af1     tone at1, limit(kf * 4.5, 20, kny)         ; the tibia is voiced rank by rank, close to
af2     tone at2, limit(kf * 2.2, 20, kny)         ;   sines -- the lowest rank brightest, its own
af4     tone at4, limit(kf * 4.4, 20, kny)         ;   third partial 5 dB above the others', which
af8     tone at8, limit(kf * 8.8, 20, kny)         ;   is what keeps the stop from going hollow.
aflu    = af1 * 1.00 + af2 * 1.12 + af4 * 0.52 + af8 * 0.50

adia    = at1 * 0.94 + at2 * 0.94 + at3 * 0.31 + at4 * 1.00 + at5 * 0.25 + at8 * 0.38
adia    tone adia, limit(kf * 12.0, 20, kny)      ; the principal is voiced as a chorus, after the sum

apul    vco2 0.5, kf, 2, 0.10         ; the reed's narrow pulse, on the 8' rank
kbpc    limit kf * 4.5, 20, kny * 0.8    ; the reed's formant, kept inside the band
kbpw    limit kf * 5.0, 20, kny * 0.8
ar1     butbp apul, kbpc, kbpw
ared    butbp ar1,  kbpc, kbpw        ; the formant rides the note: partials 3-7, up to
                                      ;   a played ~2.5 kHz. Above that butbp's own warping
                                      ;   lifts the fundamental back and the stop turns from
                                      ;   a reed into a bright square. Declared, not clamped.

as1     vco2 0.5, kf,       0         ; the string machine's saw bus, 8'
as2     vco2 0.5, kf * 2.0, 0         ; and 4'
astr    = as1 * 0.80 + as2 * 0.30

abus    = aflu * kflute * 0.23 + adia * kdiapason * 0.22 + ared * kreed * 1.00 + astr * kstrings * 0.52

ksw1    poscil 1.0, 0.62, giSine               ; the bucket brigade's clock, three phases.
ksw2    poscil 1.0, 0.62, giSine, 0.3333       ;   Its sweep does NOT scale with the knob: a
ksw3    poscil 1.0, 0.62, giSine, 0.6667       ;   brigade always sweeps, and scaling it made
                                               ;   the bottom of the knob a static comb.
ac1     vdelay3 abus, 6.0 + 3.4 * ksw1, 20.0
ac2     vdelay3 abus, 6.0 + 3.4 * ksw2, 20.0
ac3     vdelay3 abus, 6.0 + 3.4 * ksw3, 20.0
amix    = abus + (ac1 + ac2 + ac3) * 0.333 * kensemble
asig    balance amix, abus, 1                  ; the knob is a chorus, not a fader: held against
                                               ;   the dry at a 1 Hz corner, as `analog_osc` holds
                                               ;   its drive. Mixing wet in bare cost 4.4 dB.

techniques.why: A Shepard tone: six sines an octave apart under one fixed bell-shaped window over log frequency, so the key sets the chroma and not the octave -- organ-like and hollow, a pitch you can name but not place; at follow 0 every octave of a key is the same sound, and a scale climbed long enough comes back to where it began. With rise off 0 it is Risset's endless glissando, the barber pole that rises or falls forever. Method: Shepard (JASA 36(12), 1964) and Risset's continuous version (JASA 46(1A), 1969) on Csound's hsboscil. height = where the window sits, follow = window fixed (Shepard scale) or riding the key, rise = speed of the endless glissando. No partial is the fundamental by design: the pitch probe reports period doubling, and a low key does not sound low at follow 0. NOT an organ: an octave-stack organ with a real fundamental is `organ` or `divider_organ`.
techniques.code:
kheight = 0    ; height[-1.5..2]: octaves the Shepard window sits above or below 440 Hz
kfollow = 0    ; follow[0..1]: 0 the window stands still for every key, the Shepard scale; 1 it rides the key's register
krise   = 0    ; rise[-1..1]: endless Risset glissando, octaves per 4 s; 0 stands on the key
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes (chroma only; the octave is the window, set by height and follow)
; Shepard (1964) and Risset (1969) on hsboscil; giWin is the sin^2 bell. Base C0 is a
; constant (ibasfreq is i-rate); hsboscil drops ktone's whole octaves, so the key is chroma
kshpos  = log(kfreq * koct1 / 16.351597831) / log(2)
; whole octaves dropped: the sum stays bounded
kshgl   init 0
kshgl   = kshgl + krise * 0.25 * ksmps / sr
if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
  kshgl = 0
endif
kshgl   = kshgl - floor(kshgl)
kshtone = kshpos + kshgl
; keep the 0.6 depth: less is not heard with the window low
kshdrf  = 0.6 * sin(6.283185307 * 0.05 * knote)
; 4.75 = 440 Hz; the centre is bounded so its edges stay audible, the drift added after
kshwin  = min(max(4.75 + kfollow * (kshpos - 4.75) + kheight, 3.25), 7.25) + kshdrf   ; window centre, FIXED in Hz at follow 0
; sin^2 bell at six points: one level everywhere; 0.8 puts the peak near 0.5
ashep   hsboscil 0.8, kshtone, kshwin, 16.351597831, giSine, giWin, 6
asig    = ashep * kvol1

height.note: where the bell window sits, in octaves around 440 Hz (follow 0) or the key (follow 1): dark to bright at one loudness. Its resting centre stays within 155.6 Hz..2.49 kHz; the slow drift moves it 0.6 octave around that.

deep.gloss: window resting at 156 Hz, drifting 103-235 Hz: dark and hollow, the low octaves lead

bright.gloss: window near 1.2 kHz: glassy and thin, the high octaves lead

follow.note: 0: the window stands for every key, so all octaves of a key sound alike (the Shepard scale; the octave switch does nothing); 1: it rides the key's register while its centre lies within 155.6 Hz..2.49 kHz.

circular.gloss: one octave for every key: pitch class without height, a scale that circles

registered.gloss: the window rides the key from 156 Hz to 2.5 kHz: lower keys darker, higher brighter

rise.note: Risset's endless glissando, +-1 = an octave per 4 s, restarting at each note-on. Off 0 the pitch leaves the key on purpose. Integrated, so turning it mid-note bends the slope, never jumps the pitch.

falling.gloss: sinks without end, an octave every 8 s, never arriving lower

rising.gloss: climbs without end, an octave every 8 s, never arriving higher

heard.hinweis: Neu gebaut 2026-11-20, nur gemessen: Gate PASS bei 44100 und 176400 (rms -10,97 dB an 27 Ecken x 6 Registern); bei follow 1 im Band 20 Hz-20 kHz -10,97 dB auf jeder Taste von 20 Hz bis 12 kHz (Fenstermitte auf 155,6 Hz..2,49 kHz begrenzt); Teiltöne exakte Oktavvielfache der Taste; Glissando +-0,25 Okt/s ohne Klick; Oktaven bei follow 0 spektral identisch.

motions.why: dark to bright, ONCE: the spectrum opens over the note and stays open. A one-way gesture — it never travels back. Stands on its own (a filter opening) and is also the opening half of the larger movements.
motions.code:
ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; each voice starts its movement
                                        ; elsewhere -- a chord must not move in lockstep
kpos    = min(knote / 2.5, 1)           ; one-way ramp, holds at the top
adrv    = tanh(asig * 4.4)              ; a fixed BRIGHT copy of the same tone
adrv    balance adrv, asig, 1           ; matched to the clean level ONCE ...
asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + adrv * kpos   ; ... so this can only move COLOUR

motions.why: bright to dark, ONCE: the spectrum closes over the note and stays closed. The mirror of open_up, and equally a gesture in its own right — not a phase of a cycle.

                                        ; elsewhere -- a chord must not move in lockstep

motions.why: one pass across the spectrum. The SPEED is not fixed — `slow`, `fast` and `snap` set it; on its own it is a single unhurried traversal.

asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + adrv * kpos   ; ... so this can only move COLOUR

asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + adrv * kpos   ; ... so this can only move COLOUR

motions.why: a slow there-and-back at about 0.16 Hz. The RATE is steady -- breathing is -- but no two passes are shaped alike: a second rate in an irrational ratio keeps each pass uneven. That unevenness is what separates it from `cycle`.

                                        ; elsewhere -- a chord must not move in lockstep

kb2     oscili 0.18, 0.259, giSine, ivph ; so no two passes are shaped alike
kpos    = 0.5 + kb1 + kb2

adrv    balance adrv, asig, 1           ; matched to the clean level ONCE ...
asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + adrv * kpos   ; ... so this can only move COLOUR

motions.why: the timbre keeps travelling and NEVER comes back to where it was. Not a cycle and not a rate: random steps at two speeds, so no state recurs for the length of any note. It must be moving within the first seconds — a note is short.
motions.code:

ke2     randi  0.20, 0.83, ivoice + 7   ; in lockstep. Random steps at two rates:
kpos    = 0.5 + ke1 + ke2               ; no period at all, so no state ever recurs
adrv    = tanh(asig * 4.4)              ; a fixed BRIGHT copy of the same tone
adrv    balance adrv, asig, 1           ; matched to the clean level ONCE ...
asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + adrv * kpos   ; ... so this can only move COLOUR

motions.why: a regular tremor in the PITCH, about a sixth of a semitone wide -- vibrato. Not a colour movement and not a loudness one: the tone itself wavers, evenly, the way a played note does.
motions.code:

                                        ; must not move in lockstep
kv      oscili 0.3, 5.5, giSine, ivph   ; a regular 5.5 Hz tremor, +-0.3 ms of delay
asig    vdelay asig, 2 + kv, 10         ; a modulated delay IS a pitch tremor

motions.why: a regular pulsation of the LOUDNESS, about 4.5 times a second. This is the one movement that touches level rather than colour, because that is what the word means -- but it PULSES and never fades: the note's own envelope still belongs to the player.

                                        ; must not move in lockstep
ktr     oscili 0.18, 4.5, giSine, ivph  ; +-1.4 dB, a steady pulse -- never a fade
asig    = asig * (1 + ktr)

motions.why: a glinting in the TOP of the spectrum: the high partials catch the light and let it go again, irregularly. Only the top moves -- the body of the tone stands still. This form re-weights partials that are ALREADY there, so it needs a tone with a bright tail; on a mellow FM tone there is nothing above the highpass to glint with. The corner is the 8th harmonic, not a fixed frequency, so "the top" means the same thing at every pitch -- and the glint therefore THINS toward the top of the keyboard, where the band above the 8th harmonic is nearly empty. That is the physics of the word, not a defect: high notes have less top left to glint with.
motions.code:
ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; each voice moves on its own -- a chord
                                        ; must not move in lockstep
kglt    = min(kfreq * koct1 * 8, sr * 0.45, 20000) ; "the top" is a RATIO: the 8th harmonic up,
                                        ; clamped to the band. 2200 Hz was this corner
                                        ; at C#4 and the 2nd harmonic at 880 Hz.
ahi     butterhp asig, kglt             ; the top of the spectrum, on its own
abri    = asig + ahi * 1.2              ; a fixed GLINTING copy of the tone ...
abri    balance abri, asig, 1           ; ... matched to the clean level ONCE
kg      randi  0.5, 9.0, ivoice         ; irregular glints, never a steady beat
kpos    = 0.5 + kg
asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + abri * kpos   ; so this can only move COLOUR

alt.when: the tone is FM -- then glint the INDEX, which MAKES and unmakes sidebands instead of re-weighting ones that may not exist
alt.code:
kg      randi  0.45, 9.0, ivoice        ; irregular glints, never a steady beat
asig    foscili 0.5, kfreq * koct1, 1, 2, 3.0 + kg * 3.0, giSine
                                        ; the index itself glints: the
                                        ; sidebands come and go. foscili
                                        ; holds its own level, so nothing
                                        ; has to hold it afterwards.

motions.why: the movement dies away: it stirs at the start and comes to rest, and does not start again. A gesture that decelerates into stillness.
motions.code:

                                        ; elsewhere -- a chord must not move in lockstep
kmot    oscili 0.5, 0.5, giSine, ivph
kpos    = 0.5 + kmot * exp(-knote * 0.35)  ; the movement decays to rest and stays

adrv    balance adrv, asig, 1           ; matched to the clean level ONCE ...
asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + adrv * kpos   ; ... so this can only move COLOUR
